en.name: Dish.
description:
'Brazier' dish with a large, flat circular base and straight, shallow sides finished with a narrow brim. The piece is made of red clay and covered with a tin glaze. It is decorated with gold and cobalt-blue lustre on a creamy white background. The base of the dish, decorated with interlaced, small and stylized vegetal patterns, is divided into quadrants with alternating blue and golden motifs. The brim is decorated with the traditional ‘fish-like border’ pattern. Golden spirals fill and break up the white background throughout the piece.  
Technically, ceramics from the AH 8th and 9th / AD 14th and 15th century are no more than a continuation of the Almohad tradition. However, the incorporation of cobalt oxide into the glaze in the Nasrid era gave rise to a wide range of blues, and the application of copper sulphate, silver and red ochre to achieve metallic highlights resulted in some exceptional pieces. Centuries-old gilded Andalusian ceramics had their heyday during the Nasrid reign in Granada.  
The manufacture of this type of ceramic required three firings. The final firing, in a reduction kiln, was the most delicate as it required perfect control of the kiln and its temperature. The mix of metal sulphides had to adhere to the piece without the glaze from the previous firing melting again.  
The importance of the pottery workshops of the kingdom of Granada, and specifically of Malaga as the main centre of production, caused the expression *obra de maliqa* (made in Maliqa) to be used, with some variations, to refer to gilded ceramics regardless of where they were produced. This term was also used in the Christian world for pottery workshops of Nasrid origin that, from the late AH 8th / AD 14th century, began to move to various places on the east coast of Spain, of which Manises was the most important centre for highlighted ceramics produced in the Malaga style for Christian customers.

This enormous dish represents a continuation of the technique and decorative style of Nasrid ceramicists in Mudéjar workshops to meet the needs of their Christian clientele, who wanted new shapes like this shallow dish with its flat base, straight sides and horizontal rim.
place: Nasrid kingdom of Granada or Christian kingdom of Valencia, Spain.
keywords: Ceramic; gilding; highlight; Nasrids; Mudéjar; Granada; Manises; Valencia

es.name: Plato.
description:
Plato tipo “braserillo” de amplia base circular plana, y paredes rectas y poco profundas rematadas en un borde estrecho. La pieza está realizada en arcilla de color rojizo y recubierta con vidriado estannífero. Presenta decoración de reflejos metálicos en dorado y azul de cobalto sobre fondo blanco cremoso. El fondo del plato, decorado con ataurique granadino, está distribuido en cuadrantes con alternancia de motivos azules y dorados. El labio presenta la característica “orla de peces”. El borde muestra una composición de arabesco, con estrechas cintas entrelazadas en azul. Caracolillos dorados de relleno matizan el fondo blanco de toda la pieza.  
  
Técnicamente, la cerámica de los siglos XIV y XV no es más que una continuación de la almohade; sin embargo, la incorporación del óxido de cobalto al vidriado, en época nazarí, permitió una amplia gama de azules, y con la aplicación de sulfuro de cobre, plata y almagre para obtener el reflejo metálico se consiguieron piezas excepcionales. La loza dorada andalusí, fabricada ya en siglos anteriores, alcanza su apogeo en el reino nazarí de Granada.  
  
La fabricación de este tipo de cerámica requería tres cochuras. La última, efectuada en horno reductor, era la más delicada, pues suponía un perfecto control del horno y su temperatura. La mezcla de sulfuros metálicos debía adherirse a la pieza sin que el vidriado de la anterior cocción se refundiera.  
  
La importancia de los alfares del reino de Granada, y concretamente de Málaga como gran centro productor, hizo que la expresión “obra de Maliqa”, con ligeras variaciones, equivaliese a loza dorada, independientemente de su lugar de producción. Esta denominación fue también usada en el mundo cristiano por alfares de origen nazarí que, desde finales del siglo XIV, se desplazaron hacia Levante y se instalaron en varias localidades; de ellas, Manises fue el centro más importante de la cerámica de reflejos, fabricada al estilo de Málaga para clientes cristianos.

Este enorme plato representa la continuación de la técnica y la decoración cerámicas nazaríes en los talleres mudéjares para satisfacer las necesidades de su clientela cristiana, deseosa de nuevas formas, como la de este recipiente poco profundo, de base plana, paredes rectas y borde horizontal.
place: Reino nazarí de Granada o reino cristiano de Valencia.
keywords: cerámica; loza dorada; reflejos metálicos; nazaríes; mudéjar; Granada; Manises; Valencia

fr.name: Plat.
description:
Plat du genre “braserillo” à large base circulaire plate, aux parois droites et peu profondes terminées par une aile étroite. La pièce est réalisée en argile de couleur rougeâtre et recouverte d'une glaçure stannifère. Elle présente une décoration aux reflets métalliques en doré et bleu de cobalt sur un fond blanc crème. Le fond du plat, décoré d'un *ataurique* grenadin, est divisé en quadrants avec alternance de motifs bleus et dorés. L'aile présente une décoration d'arabesques avec de fins rubans bleus entrelacés. Les petites coquilles dorées qui meublent les interstices nuancent le fond blanc crème de l'aile.  
Techniquement, la céramique des VIIIe et IXe siècles H (XIVe et XVe siècles J.-C.) n'est que la continuation de la céramique almohade ; cependant, à l'époque nasride, l'introduction de l'oxyde de cobalt dans la glaçure permit d'offrir une ample gamme de bleus et, grâce à l'application de sulfure de cuivre, d'argent et de rouille pour obtenir des reflets métalliques, on obtint des pièces exceptionnelles. La faïence dorée andalouse, déjà fabriquée aux siècles précédents, atteint son apogée sous la dynastie nasride de Grenade.  
La fabrication de ce type de céramique exigeait trois cuissons. La dernière, effectuée dans un four réducteur, était la plus délicate car elle supposait un contrôle parfait de la température du four. On devait faire adhérer le mélange des sulfures métalliques de la pièce sans laisser fondre la glaçure de la précédente cuisson.  
L'importance des ateliers de poterie du royaume de Grenade et, notamment, de Málaga comme grand centre de production, fit que l'expression “produit de Maliqa”, avec de légères variantes, équivalait à “faïence dorée” indépendamment du lieu de production. Cette appellation fut également employée dans le monde chrétien par les potiers d'origine nasride qui, depuis la fin du XIVe siècle, se déplaçaient vers le Levant et s'installaient dans des localités diverses ; Manisès, entre autres, fut le centre le plus important de la céramique à reflets métalliques, fabriquée dans le style de Málaga pour une clientèle chrétienne.

Cet énorme plat représente la continuation de la technique et de la décoration des céramiques nasrides dans les ateliers mudéjars pour satisfaire les besoins de la clientèle chrétienne, demandeuse de formes nouvelles, comme celle de ce récipient peu profond, à base plate, aux parois droites et à bord horizontal.
place: Royaume nasride de Grenade ou royaume chrétien de Valence.
keywords: céramique ; faïence dorée ; reflets métalliques; Nasrides ; mudéjar ; Grenade ; Manisès ; Valence

en.name: ‘Transylvanian’ rug
description:
The term “Transylvanian” rug does not relate to the area of production but to the geographical region where many such rugs were preserved, that is, Transylvania. Rugs belonging to this group could be found mainly in Transylvanian churches. They were made in the villages of Anatolia during the 17th and 18th centuries.  
Size wise, Transylvanian rugs are rather small. Their most distinctive feature is a border filled with elongated, polygonal cartouches; however, sometimes, these are substituted by a row of simplified rosettes. The majority of so-called Transylvanian rugs are decorated with the double prayer niche, created from two *mihrab* niches in mirror image. They are mainly red, but some white-ground examples are known. “Transylvanian” rugs were very popular in Poland and many of them form part of Polish collections.  
The Kraków rug was probably made in Uşak. On the red field of the double niche, an indigo-blue cartouche of Uşak type joins with the pointed tops of the niches with flowering stems. The presence of such a medallion also suggests the place of origin of the rug. The lozenge-shape cartouche is decorated with a four-lobed motif inscribed within a double diamond, two palmettes situated on the vertical axis, and motifs of carnations and tulips as well. Placed along the edges of the cartouche are rows of graceful, small white flowers. The spandrels are decorated with lanceolate leaves and roses. The main border is filled with a row of rosettes and the outside borders with trefoil motifs.
keywords: Transylvania; ‘Transylvanian rug’; prayer rug; *mihrab*; Uşak; Anatolia; Ushak
materials: Wool (warp, weft, pile); symmetrically knotted pile (Turkish knot)

en.name: Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow
description:
The most valuable part of the church is its interior furnishing. The illusionist wall painting (1740–1743) is a highly accomplished work by the Paulist painter, Ivan Krstitelj Ranger, from Tyrol. Along with scenes relating to the titular saint, Mary, Ranger painted the ceilings and walls of the church with numerous saintly and allegorical figures as well as scenes from the Old and New Testaments. Although the pulpit has been identified as the work of the Graz sculptor Joseph Schokotnigg, it is stylistically reminiscent of Johann Baptist Straub's of 1730 in Schwarzspanierkirche in Vienna (today in Laxenburg Church). The same sculptor is ascribed the altars of St. Joseph and St. Barbara (1742–1743; gilded 1761), located alongside the triumphal arch of the church; an analogy is noted in the very distinctive compositional approach, similar to that seen in the Altar of the Immaculate Conception in Krakaudorf (Styria). The architecture and decoration of the high altar of 1743 is more traditional. With the exception of the earlier statue of *Mary the Immaculate* in the central intercolumniation (by the local sculptor, Ivan Pittner and derivative of the earlier high altar of 1729), the remaining sculpture is related stylistically to the work of Philipp Jakob Straub.  
The side chapel altars are more modest architecturally and hold works of the local sculptor, Ivan Adam Rosemberger, among others. There are some works connected with J. Schokotnigg's oeuvre (*St. John Nepomuk* and *St. Francis Xavier* on the Altar of the Holy Rosary of around 1743–1744), and some by F. J. Straub (*St. Andrew*, *St. Stephen* and *St. James* on the Altar of St. Stephen).  
Although more modest in terms of sculptural achievement, the interior of the Church of Our Lady of the Snow was completed with the addition of the choir rail in 1742. Here, sculptures of the Annunciation have been identified as the work of Zagreb sculptor, Joseph Weinacht. Finally, the *Pietà* group placed in a niche on the church façade (end of the 17th century) is by the Varaždin sculptor, Ivan Jakob Altenbach. All of which gives insight into the broad range and quality of Baroque sculpture in Croatia – comprising works that range from those created by top Central European artists to the more modest works of local and domestic sculptors.

The interior of the Pilgrimage Church of Our Lady of the Snow is among the most complete, representative and beautiful Baroque interiors in northern Croatia. With the harmony of the motifs, the wall painting and the church furnishing, it is an outstanding example of a Baroque *Gesamtkunstwerk*, or complete work of art. It was furnished and decorated in the 1740s, mainly due to donations from the Croatian aristocracy, who commissioned the region's leading artists.
type: Religious, monastic church and interior furnishing
artist: The parish priest, Pavao Kunek, and parishioners (pulpit); under-governor Baltazar Bedeković and Helena Rozalija Somogy (high altar), Count Ivan Franjo Čikulin (Altar of St. Joseph), Zagreb under-sheriff Nikola Vojković (Altar of St. Barbara), Archbishop of Kalocsa, Count Gabrijel Herman Patačić of Zajezda (Altar of the Holy Rosary), Bishop Stjepan Puc (Altar of St. Stephen Protomartyr)

Painters: Ivan Krstitelj (Johann Baptist) Ranger (1700–1753); sculptors: Joseph Schokotnigg (active 1700–1755), Ivan Adam Rosemberger (d. 1758), Ivan Pittner (active c. 1721–1745), the circle of sculptor Filip (Philipp) Jakob Straub (1706–1774), Joseph Weinacht (active 1744–1750), Ivan Jakob Altenbach (active c. 1675–1678)
history: Countess Elizabeta Keglević commissioned the church in around 1676 on the foundations of an older Gothic building. Probably with the help of donations from under-governor Adam Najšić, it was given the Baroque treatment in 1739 when the chapels and sacristy were added to it and the covered walkway was built. The wall painting and inventory of the church date to the 1740s. The pulpit, erected in 1742 with contributions from the parishioners and constructed under the auspices of parish priest, Pavel Kunek, has polychroming and gilding undertaken in 1743, thanks to a donation from Second Lieutenant Ignac Bedeković. While the local community financed the pulpit, representatives of the Croatian aristocracy were among the donors for the rest of the furnishing, as detailed above under “patrons”.
keywords: Belec, Ivan Krstitelj Ranger, Joseph Schokotnigg, Ivan Adam Rosemberger, Ivan Pittner, Filip (Philipp) Jakob Straub, Johann Baptist Straub, wall painting, sculpture, altar, pulpit
tags: Belec, Ivan Krstitelj Ranger, Joseph Schokotnigg, Ivan Adam Rosemberger, Ivan Pittner, Filip (Philipp) Jakob Straub, Johann Baptist Straub, wall painting, sculpture, altar, pulpit

en.name: Khan al-Khalili and Market of al-Sagha
description:
On founding the city of Cairo, Gawhar al-Siqilli had the Great Eastern Palace built, and behind it, a mausoleum known as *turbet al-za'afran* (saffron tomb), in which the mortal remains of the Fatimid Caliphs rested.  
In the second half of the 8th/14th century, Amir Jaharkas al-Khalili had his *khan* built on the same site, the bones were transferred in baskets to a rubbish dump on a hill outside the city. Al-Maqrizi recounts how Amir Jaharkas al-Khalili justified this act with a *f*atwa (a decision on a point of law) declaring that the Shi'ites, heretics in the eyes of the Muslim faith, had no right to remain in their tombs. Al-Maqrizi lived through the transition from the *Bahri* Mamluks to the Circassian Mamluks. He interprets the assassination of the *amir* (in the Battle of al-Nasiri near Damascus in 791/1389) and the fact that his naked body was subsequently left to rot, as a punishment from God for the desecration of the tomb of the Imams and their descendants.  
There are no remains of the original building but for the name Khan al-Khalili that the *suq* that was preserved in memory of its founder, Jaharkas al-Khalili, *amir* of the stables, in the service of Sultan Barquq.  
In 917/1511, Sultan al-Ghuri ordered the *khan* of Jaharkas al-Khalili to be pulled down and replaced by warehouses, shops, rented accommodation (*rab'*) and *wikala*s. There were three main entrances to the area set out on a grid of streets, each a monumental gateway, a copy of the majestic entrances traditionally associated with mosques, *madrasa*s and *khanqa*s. Two gateways, near the al-Husayni sanctuary face each other and open with an enormous pointed arch crowned by another tri-lobed arch filled with fine *muqarnas*. The *voussoirs* of the pointed arch are also decorated with *muqarnas* and the spandrels with floral motifs with the Sultan's epigraph in the centre. Above the frame, a *naskhi* inscription band reads: “al-Malik al-Ashraf Abi al-Nasr Qansuh al-Ghuri ordered this sacred place to be built, glory be to his victory”.  
The third gateway, known as Bab al-Badistan, is found to the far west of the street entering the market area from the al-Husayni sanctuary. It follows the same construction pattern as the former two (a pointed arch within a tri-lobed arch), but differs in its decoration. The spandrels are filled with geometric designs in marble surrounding the circular epigraph of the Sultan: “Glory be to our lord Sultan al-Malik al-Ashraf Abi al-Nasr Qansuh al-Ghuri, may his triumphs be glorious”. The trilobed arch is built of *mushahhar* stone, while the *voussoirs* of the pointed arch display an original geometric design in a succession of triangles.  
  
  
**Market of al-Sagha**  
  
Al- Maqrizi describes the location of al-Sagha (goldsmiths') *suq* in the street between the two Fatimid Palaces as follows: “this place is located in the direction of the *madrasa* of al- Salihiyya in a line between two palaces”.  
In the Fatimid era, the kitchens of the Great Eastern Palace occupied this site from where, during the month of *Ramadan*, more than 1000 pots of food were left each day to be shared among the poor. The gateway to the palace, located on the south west corner, was used exclusively for the delivery of meat and other victuals and held onto the name Bab al-Zuhuma, due to the unpleasant smell of fat (*zuhm*) which the site gave off. It is the same gateway that was destroyed in order to build the hall (*qa'a*) of the *Hanbali shaykh* between the years 641/1243 and 647/1249 of the al-Salihiyya Madrasa. It was the first of its kind in Cairo to bring together the teaching of the four legal rites.  
At the beginning of the *Bahri* Mamluk era, Sultan Barakat Khan (r. 676/1277-678/1279) son of Baybars al-Bunduqdari, founded the al-Sagha *suq* to support the *al-faqih*s and *Qur'an* reciters of the Madrasa of al-Salihiyya.  
Goldsmiths worked inside the market selling all kinds of artefacts and jewellery made of precious metals. The market also housed the operations of moneychangers. Located at the very backbone of international trade in Mamluk Egypt, the jewellery market was based on a structure of narrow streets and passageways and had several entrances. The main entrance was opposite the Madrasa of al-Salihiyya and many of the shops belonged to Armenians, Copts and Jews, the latter group installing themselves in an area (*harat al-yahud*) to the west of the suq.

es.name: Jan al-Jalili y zoco al-Saga
description:
Cuando Gawhar al-Siqilli fundó la ciudad de El Cairo, construyó el gran palacio oriental y dispuso detrás de él un mausoleo, conocido por el nombre de *turbet al-Za‘afran* (tumba del azafrán), donde reposaban los restos mortales de los califas fatimíes.  
En la segunda mitad del siglo VIII/XIV, cuando el emir Yaharkas al-Jalili construyó su *jan* en este lugar, la osamenta fue transportada en cestas y tirada en una colina en las afueras de la ciudad, en una zona de escombros. Al-Maqrizi nos relata que, para legitimar este acto, el emir Yaharkas al-Jalili se apoyó en una *fatwa* (dictamen jurídico) que declaraba a los fatimíes (*chi‘i*es) herejes de la religión musulmana y que, por lo tanto, no tenían derecho a permanecer en sus tumbas. Este historiador, que vivió la época de transición entre los mamelucos *bahri*es y circasianos, interpreta la violenta muerte del emir —asesinado en la batalla de al-Nasiri, cerca de Damasco (791/1389)— y el abandono de su cuerpo desnudo a la putrefacción como un castigo de Dios por haber profanado la sepultura de los imanes y sus descendientes.  
A pesar de que el nombre de este mercado se ha mantenido como Jan al-Jalili, en referencia a Yaharkas al-Jalili, emir de los establos del sultán Barquq, no queda nada del edificio original.  
En el año 917/1511, el sultán al-Guri mandó destruir el Jan al-Jalili y en su lugar construyó almacenes, tiendas, casas de alquiler (*rab‘*) y *wikala*s estructurados en calles perpendiculares, con tres puertas monumentales que imitan el modelo de los majestuosos accesos de mezquitas, *madrasa*s y *janqa*s. Dos de ellas, cerca del santuario de al-Husayni, están enfrentadas y se abren con un gran arco apuntado, coronado por otro trilobulado relleno de finos mocárabes. La dovela del arco apuntado está decorada también con mocárabes, mientras las albanegas están llenas de motivos florales con el emblema epigráfico del sultán en su centro. Encima del alfiz, una banda con inscripción *nasji* reza: “Ordenó construir este bendito lugar el sultán al-Malik al-Achraf Abi al-Nasr Qansuh al-Guri; gloria a su victoria.”  
La tercera puerta, llamada Bab al-Badistan, se encuentra en el extremo oeste de la calle que se adentra en el zoco desde el santuario de al-Husayni. Presenta la misma disposición que las dos anteriores —el arco apuntado coronado por otro trilobulado—, pero una decoración diferente. Las albanegas de los dos arcos están rellenas con un ornamento en mármol de motivos geométricos, que encaja el emblema epigráfico circular del sultán: “Gloria a nuestro señor el sultán al-Malik al-Achraf Abi al-Nasr Qansuh al-Guri; sean gloriosos sus triunfos”. El arco trilobulado está realizado en piedra *muchahhar*, mientras la dovela del arco apuntado presenta una original decoración geométrica que forma una sucesión de triángulos.  
  
  
**Zoco al-Saga**  
  
Al-Maqrizi hace referencia a la localización del zoco al-Saga (de los orfebres) en la calle situada entre los dos palacios de la época fatimí: “este sitio está en dirección a la *madrasa* al-Salihiyya, en una línea entre los dos palacios”.  
En la época de los fatimíes, el lugar estaba ocupado por las cocinas del gran palacio oriental desde donde salían, todos los días del mes de ramadán, más de mil ollas de comida para repartir entre los pobres. La puerta del palacio, situada en la esquina suroeste, utilizada exclusivamente para introducir la carne y otros tipos de vituallas, se quedó con el nombre de Bab al-Zuhuma, por el mal olor a grasa (*zuhm*) que se desprendía del lugar. Se trata de la puerta que fue demolida para construir, entre los años 641/1243 y 647/1249 (época ayyubí), la sala (*qa‘a*) del jeque de los *hanbali*es en la *madrasa* al-Salihiyya, la primera en El Cairo en reunir la enseñanza de las cuatro doctrinas jurídicas.  
Al principio de la época de los mamelucos *bahri*es, el sultán Barakat Jan (r. 676/1277-678/1279), hijo de Baybars al-Bunduqdari, constituyó el zoco al-Saga *waqf* en beneficio de los alfaquíes y recitadores del Corán de la *madrasa* al-Salihiyya.  
El interior de este mercado, donde los orfebres fabricaban y vendían todo tipo de objetos y joyas de metales preciosos, albergaba también todas las operaciones de cambio de dinero. Situado en el lugar más céntrico de la espina dorsal del comercio internacional del Egipto mameluco, este zoco de las joyas está estructurado en pequeñas calles y estrechos pasadizos, y contaba con varias puertas; la puerta principal se encontraba frente a la puerta de la *madrasa* al-Salihiyya. Muchas de las tiendas pertenecían a armenios, coptos y judíos, estos últimos instalados en un barrio (*harat al-yahud*) cercano al oeste del zoco.

fr.name: Khan al-Khalili et souk al-Sagha
description:
Lorsque Gawhar al-Siqilli fonda la ville du Caire, il construisit le grand palais oriental derrière lequel il plaça un mausolée, connu sous le nom de *turbet al-za‘afran* (tombe du safran), où reposaient les dépouilles mortelles des califes fatimides. Au cours de la seconde moitié du VIIIe/XIVe siècle, quand l’émir Jaharkas al-Khalili construisit son *khan* à cet endroit, les ossements furent transportés dans des corbeilles et jetés sur une colline des environs de la ville, dans une zone de décombres. Al-Maqrizi nous rapporte que, pour justifier son acte, l’émir s’appuya sur une *fatwa* (édit juridique) qui déclarait les fatimides (*chiites*) hérétiques de la religion musulmane et qui leur refusait par conséquent le droit de demeurer dans leurs tombes. Cet historien, qui vécut à l’époque de transition entre les Mamelouks *bahrides* et circassiens, interprète la mort violente de l’émir – assassiné à la bataille de al-Nasiri, près de Damas (791/1389) – et l’abandon de son corps à la putréfaction comme un châtiment de Dieu pour avoir profané la sépulture des imams et de leurs descendants. Bien que ce marché ait continué de porter le nom de souk al-Khalili en référence à Jaharkas al-Khalili qui fut émir des écuries du sultan Barquq, il ne reste rien de l’édifice d’origine.  
En 917/1511, le sultan al-Ghuri fit détruire le *khan* de al-Khalili, et érigea à sa place des entrepôts, des boutiques, des maisons de location (*rab‘*) et des *wikala*s structurés en rues perpendiculaires avec trois portes monumentales à l’imitation des luxueux accès de mosquées, *madrasa*s et *khanqa*s. Deux d’entre elles, situées près du sanctuaire de al-Hussayn, se font face et s’ouvrent avec un grand arc brisé couronné par un autre arc trilobé rempli de fins *mouqarnas*. La voûte de l’arc brisé est également décorée de *mouqarnas*, tandis que les écoinçons sont tapissés de motifs floraux avec l’emblème épigraphique du sultan au centre. Au-dessus de l’*alfiz*, un bandeau à inscription *naskhide* proclame: “C’est le sultan al-Malik al-Achraf Abi al-Nasr Qansuh al-Ghuri qui a fait construire cet endroit béni, gloire à sa victoire”.  
La troisième porte, appelée Bab al-Badistan, se trouve à l’extrême ouest de la rue qui pénètre dans le souk depuis le sanctuaire de al-Hussayn. Elle présente la même disposition que les deux précédentes – l’arc brisé couronné d’un autre arc trilobé –, mais une décoration différente. Les écoinçons des deux arcs sont remplis d’une ornementation en marbre à motifs géométriques enchâssant l’emblème épigraphique circulaire du sultan: “Gloire à notre seigneur le sultan al-Malik al-Achraf Abi al-Nasr Qansuh al-Ghuri, que ses triomphes soient glorieux”. L’arc trilobé est réalisé en pierre *muchahhar*, tandis que la voûte de l’arc brisé présente une originale décoration géométrique qui forme une succession de triangles.  
  
  
**Souk al-Sagha**  
  
Évoquant le souk al-Sagha (souk des orfèvres), al-Maqrizi le situe dans la rue entre les deux palais de l’époque fatimide: “ce site se trouve en direction de la *madrasa* al-Salihiyya sur une ligne entre les deux palais”.  
À l’époque des Fatimides, l’endroit était occupé par les cuisines du grand palais oriental, d’où sortaient, chaque jour du mois de *ramadan*, plus de mille marmites de nourriture à répartir entre les pauvres. La porte du palais, située à l’angle sudouest, exclusivement utilisée pour introduire la viande et d’autres types de victuailles, conserva le nom de Bab al- Zuhuma en raison de la mauvaise odeur de graisse (*zuhm*) qui s’exhalait de l’endroit. Il s’agit de la porte qui a été démolie pour construire, entre les années 641/1243 et 647/1249 (époque ayyoubide), la salle (*qa‘a*) du *cheikh* des *hanbalites* dans la *madrasa* al-Salihiyya, la première au Caire à réunir l’enseignement des quatre doctrines juridiques.  
Au début de l’époque des Mamelouks *bahrides*, le sultan Barakat Khan (r. 676/1277-678/1279), fils de Baybars al-Bunduqdari, constitua le souk al-Sagha en *waqf* au bénéfice des docteurs de la loi et lecteurs de Coran de la *madrasa* al-Salihiyya.  
L’intérieur de ce marché, où les orfèvres fabriquaient et vendaient toutes sortes d’objets et de joyaux en métaux précieux, abritait aussi toutes les opérations de change d’argent. Situé au plein coeur de l’épine dorsale du commerce international de l’Égypte mamelouke, ce souk des bijoux est structuré en petites ruelles et étroites venelles, et comptait de nombreuses portes; la porte principale se trouvait face à la porte de la *madrasa* al-Salihiyya. De nombreuses boutiques appartenaient à des Arméniens, à des coptes et à des juifs, ces derniers installés dans un quartier (*harat al-yahud*) proche de l’ouest du souk.

en.name: ‘Molla Narsaddin’
description: The central area of the carpet is taken up with a part of the plot from a “Molla Nasreddin” story , hence the name of this carpet. Designed to be read from right to left, there is a house on a white background, and representations of birds, donkeys and peasant motifs, all woven around “Molla Nasreddin”. Stylised flowers decorate the edges. Above Nasreddin’s head, “Molla Nasreddin” is written, and on each of the four sides of the central area within the white border the Arabic alphabet is written in black thread.
dates: Date unknown, purchased by the Museum in 1909
keywords: Carpet; narrative carpet; Azerbaijan; ‘Molla Nasraddin’; folklore
materials: Wool warp and weft; symmetrical knot

en.name: Great Mosque (Ulu Cami)
description:
Ruling between the years 1359-1391, the famous Menteşe Emir Ahmet Gazi administered a section of the land that had been divided up amongst his siblings after his father’s death. Not only did Ahmet Bey remain in power longer than any other Menteşe Bey, his period of reign was also the Emirate’s most brilliant. A few of the buildings that Ahmet Gazi had constructed in Beçin, Milas, Balat, Fethiye, and Çine, are still standing today. Of these, the Milas Great Mosque has been completely restored in the last few years and is still open for worship.  
The walls of the mosque, which is located in a beautiful garden full of shrubs and trees, were built with bricks, and stones gathered from ancient buildings; the blocks with inscriptions and the decorative brickwork here and there are especially noteworthy. Besides the main entrance in the centre of the north facade, there is also an entrance on both the east and west fronts. The stairs located to the right of the portal on the north facade were constructed to provide access to the roof for the chanting of the call to prayer. According to the Arabic inscription above the entrance, the mosque’s construction was completed in October 1378. Another inscription, written in Ottoman on the top part of the entrance on the west facade, is a *waqf* charter dating from 1904. The variety seen in the building’s supports and roof shows that it underwent important renovations at various times in history: the rather massive buttresses on all of the facades must be later additions.  
Both the plan and roof design of Milas Great Mosque continues the Seljuq tradition. Like the Seljuq mosques with basilical plans, this mosque also has aisles that are perpendicular to the *qibla* wall; while the aisles are covered with various types of vaults, the bay in front of the *mihrab* is distinctly differentiated from the rest with a dome. The marble *minbar* decorated with several rosettes was renovated in 1879; however, the inscription of the former *minbar*, dated January 1380, was copied onto the new one.

es.name: Mezquita Mayor (Ulu Cami)
description:
El famoso emir menteşí Ahmet Gazi, que gobernó entre 1359 y 1391, había heredado una parte del territorio dividido entre los hermanos a la muerte de su padre. Ahmet Gazi no solo permaneció en el poder más tiempo que ningún otro *bey* menteşí, sino que su reinado fue también el de mayor esplendor del emirato. Algunos de los edificios que hizo construir en Beçin, Milas, Balat, Fethiye y Çine siguen hoy en pie. Entre ellos está la mezquita Mayor, restaurada por completo en los últimos años y abierta aún al culto.  
Los muros de la mezquita, situada en un hermoso jardín lleno de arbustos y árboles, son de ladrillo y de piedras tomadas de edificios antiguos; especialmente notables son los bloques con inscripciones y el enladrillado decorativo que se ve aquí y allá. Además de la entrada principal en el centro de la fachada norte, tiene otras dos laterales: una en la fachada este y otra en la oeste. A la derecha de la puerta de la fachada norte hay una escalera por la que se sube al tejado, desde el que se llama a la oración. La inscripción en árabe del portal indica que la construcción de la mezquita se terminó en octubre de 1378. La inscripción en caracteres turcos de la parte alta de la entrada oeste es el acta fundacional de un *waqf* y data de 1904. La heterogeneidad de los soportes y de los materiales del tejado prueba que ha sido reformada en distintas épocas; los gruesos contrafuertes de todas las fachadas debieron de añadirse tardíamente.  
La planta y el tejado de la mezquita Mayor de Milas continúan la tradición selyuquí. Como en las mezquitas selyuquíes de planta basilical, las naves, perpendiculares al muro de la *qibla*, están cubiertas por bóvedas de varios tipos, mientras que la crujía situada frente al *mihrab* se diferencia del resto por la cúpula. El *mimbar* de mármol, decorado con varias rosetas, se restauró en 1879; no obstante, la inscripción del antiguo, con fecha de enero de 1380, se copió en el nuevo.

en.name: Vase with *chinoiseries*
description: Glass has always been used to imitate more valuable materials. This baluster vase with *chinoiseries* imitates much more costly porcelain in form, material and decor. The production of opaque white glass started in the early 15th century and enjoyed a heyday in the late 17th and early 18th centuries. At the same time, porcelain was becoming more widespread. Painted cups, small jugs, plates, sugar pots and decorative vases were a more affordable alternative to expensive porcelain crockery.

en.name: *Inside a Jewish household*
short_description: This copy of a beautiful watercolour by Charles Lallemand shows the inside of a bourgeois Jewish household. This snapshot of daily life reveals a great deal of similarity between Jewish and Muslim traditional dress and interiors.
holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
keywords: Judaism; Jews in Tunisia
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: *Intérieur d’une maison juive*
short_description: Reproduction d’une très belle aquarelle de Charles Lallemand représentant l’intérieur d’une maison bourgeoise juive. A noter, dans la scène de la vie quotidienne, une certaine similitude avec l’intérieur et les costumes des autochtones musulmans.
holder: Institut supérieur d’Histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie
keywords: Judaisme; Juifs de tunisie
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

ar.name: خيمة.
description:
تنتمي هذه الخيمة إلى النوع المستطيل الشكل ذي العمودين والمسقط البيضوي، وهي تتألف من جدارين مستطيلين كل منهما مؤلف من تسعة أقسام، وسقف. يشكل قسما السقف على الضلعين الطويلين والقطع المثلثة الشكل على الضلعين القصيرين شكلاً يشبه القبة، وقد تم ربط سقف الخيمة وجدرانها معاً بنظام المسامير والعقد، وتم إخفاء هذه الوصلات من الداخل بواسطة ستائر قصيرة، كما تم استخدام الستائر أيضاً في الجانب السفلي من جدار الخيمة. السقف يحمله عمودان ، أما أقسام الجدران فليس لها دعامات بل تم شدها بواسطة حبال تثبيت.  
البنية الخارجية للخيمة مصنوعة من قماش أخضر رمادي أملس، أما البنية الداخلية فهي من القماش الأحمر المزخرف بكثافة بمجموعات من النماذج المتكررة. ويتطابق تركيب الزخارف ونماذجها مع زخارف الخيام العثمانية التي تحوي أعمدة وأقواس وزهريات ورصائع، وقد تم استعمال جزء من الجدار كوحدة زخرفية تتكرر على الأقسام الأخرى. تم ملء الأقواس برصائع تدعى "الشمس"، ويظهر في كل من الرصائع المدببة مجموعة متنوعة من الأزهار التي تنبثق من نماذج لزهريات. وتمثل الزخارف الزهرية الكثيفة التي تملأ الرصائع والإطارات شكل حديقة، كما تظهر الأقواس والأعمدة في سقف الخيمة، وترمز الأشرطة التي تحمل نماذج النجوم بين عمودين في السقف إلى السماء.  
تم تطبيق الزخارف الملصقة بتقنية الحواشي حيث تمت حياكة قطع من القماش الحريري بأشكال وألوان متعددة وقطع صغيرة من الجلد على الأرضية لتشكل نماذج من الزخارف، وقد تم وضع خمس طبقات كحد أعلى من القماش فوق بعضها البعض.  
لم تدخل السويد في حرب مباشرة مع العثمانيين، وخلال حربهم مع الساكسونيين حصلوا على غنائم كثيرة كان من بينها الخيام التركية.

خيمة ذات أرضية بيضوية وعمادين. الجدران والسقف مزينة بحشد من الورود والأشجار المنبثقة من المزهريات ــ صورة حديقة حقيقية. يضاف إلى ذلك أن السقف الذي يشكل قنطرة يظهر طوقاً من النجوم وسط السقف، رمزاً للسماء.
keywords: تقنية اللصق؛ خيمة؛ زخرفة زهرية؛ نسيج.

en.name: Tent.
description:
This tent belongs to the type of double-columned, rectangular tents with an oval floor plan. It consists of two rectangular walls, each of nine sections, and a roof. The two roof sections of the long sides and the triangular pieces of the short sides form a covering that resembles a vault. The tent roof and the walls are fastened to each other by a toggle and loop system. On the interior and exterior of the tent, this joint section is hidden by a valance. The lower edge of the tent wall also has a valance. The ceiling is supported by two columns. The wall sections do not have struts, but are made taut by guy ropes.  
The outer shell of the tent is of plain verdigris cloth. Only the inner shell of red cloth is decorated with a rich array of patterns. The composition and the motifs of this tent conform to general Ottoman tent ornamentation showing columns, arches, vases and medallions. A section of the wall was taken as a basic unit and its scheme of decoration was repeated on each of the other sections. The arches are filled with medallions called 'sun' (*şemse*). Each of the pointed medallions shows a great variety of flowers growing out from vase motifs. The dense floral infilling of the medallions and the borders presents the illusion of a garden. The arch and column motif likewise occurs on the ceiling of the tent. The ceiling with a band of star motifs between the two columns of the tent symbolises the sky.  
The ornamentation is worked in the hemmed appliqué technique. Pieces of silk fabric in various shapes and colours in combination with small pieces of leather were sewn to a ground to form patterns. It was carried out by placing a maximum of five layers of fabric on top of each other.  
The Swedes were never directly engaged in war against the Ottomans. Fighting against the Saxons, they captured a great deal of booty, also coming into ownership of Turkish tents.

Tent with an oval floor plan and two columns. The walls and roof are decorated with flowers and trees growing out of vases – the perfect illusion of a garden. In addition, the roof forming a vault shows a band of stars in the middle of the ceiling, symbolising the sky.
keywords: Tent; textiles; appliqué technique; floral decoration

es.name: Tienda de campaña.
description:
Tienda de campaña rectangular, de doble columna y plata oval. Este tipo de tiendas presentan dos paredes rectangulares, de nueve secciones cada una y un tejado. Las dos secciones de la cubierta a doble vertiente y las secciones triangulares de los lados cortos recuerdan a una bóveda. La cubierta y las paredes están unidas con un sistema de nudo y cabillas. Sendas cenefas oculta las juntas en el exterior y el interior de la tienda. La parte inferior también presenta una cenefa. Dos columnas sujetan la cubierta y las paredes se tensan con cuerdas, sin puntales.  
La tela exterior de color verde grisáceo y la interior roja, decorada con gran variedad de diseños. La composición y motivos decorativos que decoran esta tienda siguen la norma general de las tiendas otomanas, con columnas, arcos, jarrones y medallones. Se tomó una de las secciones ornamentales de la pared con unidad básica, para luego repetirla como organizador de la composición decorativa. Los arcos se rellenan con medallones denominados “soles” (şemse), decorados con motivos de jarrones en los que crecen gran variedad de flores. La fuerte presencia floral en los medallones y en los bordes crea la ilusión de un jardín. El techo se decora con el mismo motivo de arcos y columnas.  
La ornamentación de esta tienda se hizo con la técnica de bordado de aplicación, según la cual, se cosían piezas de seda de diferentes colores y tamaños junto con pequeños fragmentos de cuero siguiendo un esquema. En este caso, hay hasta cinco capas de tejido.  
Los suecos nunca lucharon directamente contra los turcos, pero en su lucha contra los sajones, lograron un gran botín, en el que se incluían tiendas de campaña turcas.

Tienda de campaña de planta oval y dos columnas, Las paredes y el suelo están decorados con jarrones de los que crecen flores, creando la ilusión de un jardín.  
La cubierta presenta forma abovedada y está decorada con bandas de estrellas en el centro del techo, simbolizando el cielo.
dates: Siglo XI de la Hégira/ XVII d.C.
keywords: tienda de campaña; tejidos; técnica de bordado de aplicación; decoración floral
materials: Algodón, seda y cuero, Bordado de aplicación.
tags: Algodón, seda y cuero, Bordado de aplicación.

fr.name: Tente
description:
Tente appartenant au type des tentes de plan ovale à deux colonnes. Elle  consiste en deux parois rectangulaires, chacune divisée en neuf sections, et une toiture. Les deux sections de toiture des grands côtés et les sections triangulaires des petits côtés forment une couverture qui ressemble à une voûte. La toiture et les murs sont attachés ensemble par un système de cabillots et de boucles, les joints étant dissimulés aussi bien à l'extérieur qu'à l'intérieur par un bavolet, de même que la partie basse des murs. Le plafond est soutenu par deux colonnes, les murs de toile tendus au moyen de cordes.  
L'extérieur est en toile unie vert-de-gris. Seul l'intérieur en toile rouge est richement décoré. Les motifs de colonnes, d'arcs, de vases et de médaillons sont ceux que l'on trouve habituellement dans les luxueuses tentes ottomanes. Une même composition est reproduite plusieurs fois. Les arcs sont occupés par des médaillons “soleils” (*semse*), contenus dans une mandorle et ornés de diverses fleurs disposées dans un vase. Ce dense décor floral de médaillons et de bordures veut créer l'illusion d'un jardin. Le motif de l'arc et des colonnes est repris au plafond, décoré d'un bandeau de motifs en étoile entre les deux colonnes, pour symboliser le ciel.  
L'ornementation fait appel à la technique de l'appliqué. Combinés à de petites pièces de cuir, des morceaux de tissus de soie de différentes formes et couleurs sont cousus sur le fond pour constituer les motifs. On peut trouver plusieurs épaisseurs de tissus superposées.  
Les Suédois n'affrontèrent jamais les Ottomans. C'est en combattant les Saxons qu'ils s'emparèrent d'un riche butin qui contenait des tentes turques.

Tente de plan ovale et à deux piliers. Les parois sont décorées de fleurs et d’arbres sortant de vases pour donner une illusion de jardin. Le plafond voûté présente au centre un bandeau d’étoiles symbolisant le ciel.
dates: XIe siècle de l’Hégire (XVIIe siècle J.-C.)
keywords: Tente; textiles, technique de l’appliqué; décoration florale.

de.name: Kath. Pfarrkirche St. Gallus
description: Im Grundriss dürfte die Weerer Kirche im wesentlichen auf den spätgotischen Vorgänger zurückzuführen sein, mit etwas eingezogenem Chor im 5/8-Schluss und Saal-Langhaus. Das Innere ist durch die systematisch pilastergegliederten Wände mit kräftigem umlaufenden Gebälk geprägt. In das Gewölbe darüber schneiden hohe Schildbögen ein, so dass sich je vier Bögen ergeben, die die gemalten Scheinkuppeln über Chor und Langhaus zu tragen scheinen. Als Baumeister, der lange nicht bekannt war, wird heute Johann Michael Umlauf identifiziert, ein vormaliger Mitarbeiter des Franz de Paula Penz.

Der am Rand des Dorfes gelegene, äußerlich sehr schlichte Bau mit gotischem Turm überrascht im Inneren durch seine Prachtentfaltung, die vor allem von den großen Kuppelfresken Zeillers ausgeht. Die relative Strenge der Architektur wird durch die Rokoko-Stukkatur gemildert, während die Altarausstattung in schwererem spätbarocken Stil gehalten ist.
artist:
Architektur: Johann Michael Umhauser (1731-1784);  
Fresken und Altarbilder: Franz Anton Zeiller (1716-1794)
history: Das erst 1954 zur Pfarrei erhobene Weer war ursprünglich eine Expositur der Pfarre Kolsass und dem Stift Fiecht bei Schwaz unterstellt. Schon im 8. Jahrhundert bestand wohl eine erste, zu einem Hof gehörende Eigenkirche. Vermutet wird ein Neubau im 13. Jahrhundert. Im letzten Drittel des 15. Jahrhunderts wurde dann eine größere spätgotische Kirche errichtet, von der der Turm im südlichen Chorwinkel und die Chorfundamente in den barocken Neubau von 1778 übernommen worden sind. Dieser wurde am 5. Juli 1781 geweiht.
keywords: Spätbarock; Rokoko; Pfarrkirche; Saalkirche; Deckenmalerei

en.name: Catholic Parish Church of St. Gall
description: The ground plan of the Weer church can largely be traced back to that of its Late Gothic predecessor, with a somewhat retracted choir and a 5/8 choir termination and hall nave. The interior is characterised by the systematically arranged pilaster walls with powerful entablature throughout. The vault above it is divided by high formerets (wall-ribs) resulting in four arches which appear to support the illusionistic painted cupolas above the choir and nave. The master builder, who long remained unknown, has now been identified as Michael Umlauf, a former employee of Franz de Paula Penz.

The extremely plain building with its gothic tower situated at the edge of the village holds a surprise in store with its splendid interior, most notably the large cupola frescos from Zeiller. The relatively austere architecture is moderated by the Rococo stuccowork, while the altar décor is executed in the rich style of the Late Baroque.
type: Ecclesiastical architecture (parish church), originally a succursal church
artist: Architecture: Johann Michael Umhauser (1731–1784); frescos and altarpieces: Franz Anton Zeiller (1716–1794)
history: Weer, first elevated to the status of a parish in 1954, was originally a branch of the parish of Kolsass and was under the administration of Fiecht Monastery near Schwaz. The first church, belonging to a farm, dates from the 8th century. It is assumed that a new building was erected in the 13th century. In the last third of the 15th century a larger Late Gothic church was erected. The tower in the southern corner of the choir and the choir’s foundations were incorporated into the new Baroque building of 1778 which was consecrated on 5 July 1781.
keywords: Late Baroque; Rococo; parish church; hall church; ceiling paintings

de.name: Gestühl
description: Das Kirchengestühl mit seinen 80 in szenischer Schnitzarbeit verzierten Wangen ist ein Werk des aus Fügen im Zillertal stammenden Bildhauers Franz Xaver Nißl, wohl ein Schüler des Johann Baptist Straub. An den vorderen kürzeren Kirchenbänken, die dem Konvent dienten, sind Symbole Christi, Mariens und der Geistlichkeit dargestellt, die hinteren weisen unter anderem Motive aus der Vita der hl. Benedikt und Josef sowie einiger Nothelfer auf, daneben auch Wappen der Stifter.

en.name: Pews
description: The church pews, with their 80 dividing panels decorated with carvings, are the work of the sculptor Franz Xaver Nißl from Fügen in Zillertal, a student of Johann Baptist Straub. The shorter, front convent pews are decorated with symbols of Christ, Mary and the clergy, the rear pews feature, amongst other motifs, the life of St. Benedict and Joseph and a number of Holy Helpers alongside the coat of arms of the benefactor.

en.name: "Amr has the Infidels Thrown into the Sea"
names: Folio from a Khavarannama (The Book of the East) of ibn Husam al-Din
description: This painting, with its vibrant color palette and lively action, is taken from a manuscript of the Khavarannama (Book of the East), a gathering of tales relating the adventures of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad. These mostly imaginary accounts of the exploits of 'Ali and his companions against demons, dragons, and kings were composed in emulation of the great Persian poet Firdausi’s Shahnama, but have the important religious figure of 'Ali as their main protagonist.
artist: Maulana Muhammad Ibn Husam ad Din
materials: Ink, opaque watercolor, and gold on paper
tags: Ink, opaque watercolor, and gold on paper

en.name: *Dans le harem: Divertissement Arabe.* For piano.
short_description: Musical composers' fascination with the "Orient" manifested itself in their music and their titles. The sphinx, for example, was a recurring symbol of "Egyptomania".
keywords: Music; Orientalism; harem

fr.name: *Dans le harem : divertissement arabe : piano*
short_description: Le goût de l'Orient gagne les compositeurs de musique soit dans leurs thèmes musicaux soit dans leurs titres de pièces. Le sphinx est un élément d'iconographie récurrent, très utilisé dans l'égyptomania.
keywords: Musique; orientalisme; harem

en.name: Sword with scabbard
description: A sword and scabbard decorated with geometric and floral motifs and crafted in southern Morocco in the 19th century. Sword blades were imported from Europe, especially from Toledo in Spain, or from Damascus in Syria.
keywords: Trade; arms; armours; metalwork; geometric motifs; geometric decoration; floral decoration; vegetal motifs; vegetal decoration; craftsmanship; war; warfare; military objects
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate for Cultural Heritage

cs.name: Oslava císaře Karla VI.
description: Hejtman Kounic byl přívržencem Karla VI. a propagátorem pragmatické sankce. Prováděl systematicky modernizaci země a reformy veřejné správy. S podporou císaře sjednotil stavovskou správu s královským tribunálem v Zemské hejtmanství, což se stalo popudem k výstavbě nového vstupního křídla (M. Grimm), ústředním rizalitem s dvojicí průchodů symbolicky zvýrazňujícího nový úřad. Schodiště i nový zasedací sál byly vyzdobeny místními umělci. F. Ř. Eckstein se ucházel také o výmalbu Sněmovního sálu. Odmítnut odešel tento přední brněnský malíř do služeb jezuitů do Lvova, kde zemřel.
artist: František Řehoř Ignác Eckstein (1689? Židovice u Žatce – 1741 Lvov)

en.name: Celebration of Emperor Charles VI
description:
Governor Kounic was a follower of Charles VI and a promoter of the “pragmatic sanction”. He systematically addressed the modernisation of the country and reforms in public administration. With the emperor’s support Kounic unified the administration and the royal tribunal into a Provincial Governorate, which spurred the construction of a new entrance wing by M. Grimm, its central bay with two passageways symbolising the new office. The staircase and the new Assembly Hall were decorated by local artists.  
The artist, F. Ř. I. Eckstein also tendered for the commission to decorate the Assembly Hall but he was spurned and left Brno to work for the Jesuits in Lviv where he later died.
artist: František Řehoř Ignác Eckstein (1689? Židovice u Žatce – 1741 Lviv)

en.name: Church of San Girolamo della Carità, Spada Chapel
description:
The most spectacular element of the chapel consists of its walls, entirely covered with intarsia alternated with marble slabs that imitate damask, in antique yellow for the vegetal decorations and for the emblems of the Spada (lilies, stars and swords, in the upper band) and in dark onyx for the mirrors, made by Giovan Battista Scala, known as il Napoletano (the Neapolitan), Giovanni Maria della Monaca and Giovanni Somazzi. The traditional balustrade is here replaced by two kneeling angels holding a jasper drape, imitating the Eucharistic tablecloth, a work of Antonio Giorgetti, pupil of Bernini. The wings of the angel on the left are made of wood and are mobile, so as to allow access to the chapel. The altar also has a fake damask altar frontal, made with marble inlays of flowering branches and lilies. The detached fresco of the Madonna and Child is framed by polychrome marble, namely a laurel wreath in antique green and two palm branches in light marble. On the sides there are two relief medallions with the faces of Saints Francis and Bonaventure by Paolo Naldini.  
On the side walls there are two sofas in black marble, with armrests in yellow marble, on which two sleeping figures lie between alabaster cushions and drapes: on the left Bernardino Lorenzo Spada, bishop of Calvi (died 1543), by Ercole Ferrata, and on the right Giovanni Spada (died 1247), chaplain of Innocent IV, sculpted by Cosimo Fancelli between 1656 and 1659. Above the two monuments, medallions with the effigies of the most illustrious members of the Spada family hang from bronze ropes: *Amadore I Spada and his brother Aleramo* by Paolo Naldini, *Pietro di Cecco and Serrone di Pietro Spada,* also by Naldini, *Amadore Spada and his son Mengo* by Antonio Raggi, *Amadore II Spada* by Francesco Baratta, *Mutio Spada and his nephew Antonello* by Ercole Ferrata and *Ghino di Mengo Spada* by Giuseppe Perone. The floor is also decorated with similar inlay motifs, while the barrel vault is frescoed with the dove of the Holy Spirit and the personification of Faith and Charity.

Highly scenographical chapel: its inlaid marbles simulate damask. Two angels by Giorgetti (Bernini’s follower) bear the jasper cloth referring to the Eucharistic altar-cloth. The left angel has movable wooden-made wings to allow the entrance to the chapel. Tombs: Bernardino Lorenzo Spada (by  E. Ferrata) and G. Spada (C. Fancelli).
artist: Francesco Righi (architect); Antonio Giorgetti; Paolo Naldini; Ercole Ferrata; Cosimo Fancelli; Giovan Battista Scala, called il Napoletano; Giovanni Maria della Monaca; Giovanni Somazzi
history:
San Girolamo della Carità was the seat of the homonymous Confraternity, known for its charitable works which had been particularly encouraged under San Filippo Neri, who had lived there since 1551 for over thirty years and had established the Oratory.  
The chapel, dedicated to the Madonna as depicted in a late 15th century fresco, was granted on 17 October 1595 to Orazio Spada, but there is no information on how it originally looked. After the death of Paolo Spada, brother and heir of Orazio, embellishment works were carried out in the fourth decade of the 17th century. In 1654 Virgilio Spada, grandson of Orazio, Oratorian father and secret almsgiver of pope Innocent X and then of Alexander VII, had the work resumed with the aim of transforming the chapel into the family mausoleum, thus celebrating the most illustrious ancestors of his family. According to the sources, Francesco Righi designed the chapel, but Virgilio Spada, also an amateur architect, contributed with his original inputs. He personally followed the work, including the construction of the balustrade. Spada was also very close to Borromini, to whom he had also given advice for the symbolic and religious aspects of some of his projects, such as that of the Oratory of Santa Maria in Vallicella: for this reason, the Spada chapel was considered for a long time the work of the famous Ticino architect.

it.name: Chiesa di San Girolamo della Carità, Cappella Spada
description:
L'elemento più scenografico della cappella è costituito dalle sue pareti rivestite integralmente di tarsie alternate a lastre marmoree che imitano damaschi, in giallo antico per le decorazioni vegetali e per gli emblemi degli Spada (gigli, stelle e spade, nella fascia superiore) e in onice scuro per le specchiature, eseguite da Giovan Battista Scala, detto il Napoletano, Giovanni Maria della Monaca e Giovanni Somazzi.   
La tradizionale balaustra d'accesso alla cappella è qui sostituita da due angeli inginocchiati che sorreggono un drappo in diaspro a imitazione della tovaglia eucaristica, il tutto opera di Antonio Giorgetti, allievo di Bernini. Le ali dell'angelo di sinistra sono in legno e mobili, in modo da consentire l'accesso alla cappella. Anche l'altare presenta un finto paliotto damascato, realizzato con intarsi marmorei di rami fioriti e gigli. L'affresco staccato della Madonna con Bambino è incorniciato a sua volta da marmi policromi: una corona di alloro in verde antico e due rami di palma in marmo chiaro. Ai lati sono posti due medaglioni in rilievo con i volti di San Francesco e San Bonaventura realizzati da Paolo Naldini.  
Sulle pareti laterali si trovano due divani in marmo nero, con braccioli in marmo giallo, su cui giacciono, tra cuscini e drappi in alabastro, a sinistra la figura dormiente di Bernardino Lorenzo Spada vescovo di Calvi (morto nel 1543), opera di Ercole Ferrata, e a destra Giovanni Spada (morto nel 1247), cappellano di Innocenzo IV, eseguito da Cosimo Fancelli tra il 1656 e il 1659.  
Al di sopra dei due monumenti pendono, da corde bronzee, alcuni medaglioni con le effigi dei più illustri membri della famiglia Spada: *Amadore I Spada e suo fratello Aleramo* di Paolo Naldini, *Pietro di Cecco e Serrone di Pietro Spada*, sempre del Naldini, *Amadore Spada e sue figlio Mengo* di Antonio Raggi, *Amadore II Spada* di Francesco Baratta, *Mutio Spada e suo nipote Antonello* di Ercole Ferrata e *Ghino di Mengo Spada* di Giuseppe Perone.  
Anche il pavimento è costituito da analoghi motivi ad intarsio mentre la volta a botte è affrescata con la colomba dello Spirito Santo e le figure della Fede e della Carità.

La cappella, altamente scenografica, è completamente decorata da tarsie marmoree che simulano stoffe di damasco alle pareti. Due angeli del Giorgetti, allievo di Bernini, recano una tovaglia eucaristica in diaspro; l’angelo di sinistra è provvisto di ali mobili lignee, a imitazione del marmo, che consentono l’accesso alla cappella.
artist: Francesco Righi (architetto); Antonio Giorgetti; Paolo Naldini; Ercole Ferrata; Cosimo Fancelli; Giovan Battista Scala, detto il Napoletano; Giovanni Maria della Monaca; Giovanni Somazzi
history:
San Girolamo della Carità era la chiesa sede dell’omonima Confraternita, celebre per le sue opere caritative cui diede un impulso decisivo San Filippo Neri che qui visse per oltre trent’anni, a partire dal 1551, istituendovi l’Oratorio.  
La cappella, dedicata alla Madonna raffigurata nell’affresco di fine Quattrocento, fu concessa il 17 ottobre 1595 a Orazio Spada, ma non si hanno notizie sul suo aspetto originario. Dopo la morte di Paolo Spada, fratello ed erede di Orazio, furono eseguite, nel quarto decennio del Seicento, delle opere di abbellimento.  
Nel 1654 Virgilio Spada, nipote di Orazio, padre oratoriano nonché elemosiniere segreto di Innocenzo X e poi di Alessandro VII, fece riprendere i lavori con lo scopo di trasformare la cappella nel mausoleo di famiglia, celebrando in questo modo gli antenati più illustri del suo casato. Il disegno della cappella è opera di Francesco Righi, come testimoniato dalle fonti d’archivio, mentre per la parte ideativa diede il suo contributo lo stesso Virgilio Spada, architetto dilettante, che seguì in prima persona i lavori, compresa la realizzazione della balaustrata. Spada era tra l’altro molto legato a Borromini, cui aveva anche elargito consigli per gli aspetti simbolico-religiosi di alcune delle sue fabbriche, come quella dell’Oratorio di Santa Maria in Vallicella: questo è il motivo per cui si è ritenuto a lungo che la cappella Spada fosse opera del celebre architetto ticinese.
keywords: Illusionismo

en.name: 'The Paths of Paradise'
description:
The miniature, which like 13/2012 and 14/2012 comes from a manuscript describing Muhammad’s mystical ascension to heaven (*miraj*), shows the Prophet and the Archangel Gabriel (*Jibril*) at the pond of al-Kawthar before one of Paradise’s richly ornamented gates. Both the ribbed domes and tiled walls are covered with rich vegetal ornamentation of various types, in keeping with contemporary architecture from Central Asia. Beside the pond are countless vessels of gold and jade and celadon-glazed ceramics from which the believer can quench his thirst after the tribulations of the Day of Judgment.  
  
The Garden of Paradise itself, with its many spiritual and sensual delights, is not depicted in this beautiful painting, and no artist would probably have been able to describe it to the believer as intensely as accounts in the Koran and later writings.  
  
Of the museum’s seven paintings from this manuscript, the refined ‘Gates of Paradise’ is the one that most clearly points toward the artistic zenith of Timurid painting at the end of the AH 9th / AD 15th century.
keywords: Water; miniature; folio; Herat; Timurids

en.name: Village school in Apulia run by the Società Umanitaria, which was participating in a drive against illiteracy
Tile Bowl
description: The bowl’s surface is coated in white clay and slip and decorated in blue and white under a transparent colourless glaze. On the exterior a dark grey-blue ivy branch, reminiscent of a Chinese cloud, is adorned with large stylised flowers and shoots in cobalt blue. The contours are grey-blue. The exterior of the rim is encircled by a band of short angled lines, and the interior by a band of half rosettes. Inside the bowl is a medallion featuring a large stylised flower with six petals in the centre. This is a unique example of the influence of Chinese porcelain.
dates: Hegira second quarter of the 10th century / AD second quarter of the 16th century

ar.name: قصر اشبيلية.
description:
ينتصب القصر المدجن لاشبيلية فوق آثار قصور أخرى تعود لفترات سابقة. كان موضعه مُحتلاً منذ الفترة الرومانية، وتوالت فيه بنايات أموية ومرابطية وموحدية، عرفنا عدداً من بينها من خلال الحفريات الأثرية. خصَّت تعديلاتُ ألفونس العاشر القصرَ الموحدي، وتمثلت في توسيعات للفضاءات السابقة، وجاءت كلها ذات طراز قوطي. وبعد معركة صالادو (طريفة) (1340)، أعاد ألفونس الحادي عشر تكييف صحن الجص الذي أُسنِدَت عليه قبةٌ مربعة الشكل ذات عقود ثلاثية من الجص على كل جانب، ومغطاة بسقف ذي قمتين، وهو الفضاء الذي عرف تحت اسم قاعة العدالة.  
يستند قصر بيير الأول إلى قصر ألوفونس العاشر، وبُني اعتماداً على تصميم جديد مابين عامي 1364 و 1366. أثرت الواجهة المفتوحة على صحن لامونتيريا (صحن الصيد بمساعدة الكلاب المطاردة) في قصور طورديسياس (بلد الوليد)، وعلى قماريش (غرناطة) والجانب الداخلي لبيعة طرانزيت (طليطلة). في الداخل، نُميز بوضوح منطقة عمومية وأخرى خاصة؛ وقد كانت منطقة صحن لاس دونسيلاس (صحن الوصيفات) مخصصة لأنشطة الاستقبالات، إلى جانب صالة السفراء وصالة السقف لفيليب الثاني. ويُقال إن الملك محمد الخامس، الحليف السياسي لبيير الأول، قد أرسل إليه حرفيين من أجل تزيين قصوره. وبعد زيارة لقصر اشبيلية، قام بتشييد قصر قماريش في غرناطة.  
وفي عام 1427، وخلال حكم جوان الثاني، أنجز دييجو رويز القبة المضلعة لصالة السفراء؛ ووسع الملوك الكاثوليكيون الطابق العلوي، وخصصوا للملك لاكمارا ريال ألتا (الغرفة الملكية العلوية). وفي الوقت نفسه، شيدوا قاعة الانتظار والغرفة وحنية الملكة والكنيسة وقاعة المأدبة. كما تم تعويض أسقف المستوى السفلي ذات المنحدرات الثنائية بأسقف منبسطة.

القصر (لالكازار)مثالٌ لتعقد الطراز المدجن خلال القرن 8 الهجري / القرن 14 الميلادي، ولهذا الصنف من العمارة البلاطية، ونتيجة لعمل مشترك لحرفيين من طليطلة وغرناطة وإشبيلية؛ فهو يمثل تركيبا للتقليد المدجن الطليطلي والفن النصري المعاصر له، وللفن الموحدي الإشبيلي السابق عليه؛ وتعتبر هذه القلعة كأهم معلمة للفن المدجن؛ وتبقى الواجهة الضخمة وصحن الوصيفات بقصر بيير الأول بارزة بشكل خاص.
dynasty: فترة المدجنين، القرنان الثالث عشر والخامس عشر.
artist: ألفونس العاشر (حكم مابين 1252 – 1284)؛ الفونس الحادي عشر (حكم مابين 1312 – 1350)؛ بيير الأول من قشتالة (حكم مابين 1350 – 1369)؛ جون الثاني (حكم مابين 1406 – 1454)؛ إيزابيل الأولى من قشتالة (حكمت مابين 1474 – 1504) وفيرديناند الثاني من أراجون وفيرديناند الخامس من قشتالة (حكم مابين 1474 – 1516).
شارك في بنائه بناؤون طليطليون وغرناطيون واشبيليون.
keywords: قبة؛ قصر اشبيلية؛ قمم مزدوجة؛ مدجن.
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Fine Arts

en.name: Seville Citadel.
description:
The Mudéjar citadel of Seville rises beside the remains of other palaces of former ages. The site has been occupied since Roman times by successive Umayyad, Almohad and Almoravid buildings, many of which are known to us through archaeological excavations. Alterations were made by Alfonso X to the Almohad palace, consisting of extensions to existing spaces, all in the Gothic style. Following the battle of Salado (1340), Alfonso XI remodelled the Courtyard of the Plasterwork (Yeso), adding a square-plan *qubba* (dome) with triple plaster arches on each side covered with a *moamar* (paired beam) roof. This space is known as the Hall of Justice.  
The Palace of Pedro I backs onto the Palace of Alfonso X and was built from scratch between 1364 and 1366. Its façade, opening onto the Courtyard of the Hunt (Montería), influenced the palaces at Tordesillas (Valladolid) and Comares (Granada) and the interior of the Tránsito Synagogue (Toledo). The inside is clearly divided into two areas, one private and one public. The area around the Courtyard of the Maidens (Doncellas) was used for representations along with the Ambassadors' Room, the Room of the Half Cane or the Room of the Ceiling of Felipe II.  
It is said that King Muhammad IV, a political ally of Pedro I, sent craftsmen to decorate his palaces and that, following a visit to the Seville Citadel, he ordered the construction of the Comares Palace in Granada.  
In 1427, during the reign of Juan II, Diego Ruiz completed the hemispherical cupola of the Ambassadors' Room. The Catholic Kings extended the upper storey and the Upper Royal Chamber was taken by the king. The antechamber, room and bedroom of the queen were built at the same time, along with the chapel and the anteroom to the banqueting hall. The gabled roofs in the lower storey were replaced with flat roofs.

A paradigm of the complexity of the Mudéjar style in the AH 8th / AD 14th century, and the palatial architecture of this style, the citadel was the result of the combined work of craftsmen from Toledo, Granada and Seville itself. It is a synthesis of Toledan Mudéjar tradition, earlier Almohad art in Seville and contemporary Nasrid art from Granada, and is considered to be the most important monument in Mudéjar art. Its imposing façade and the Courtyard of the Maidens (Doncellas) in the Palace of Pedro I are particularly noteworthy.
artist: Alfonso X (r. 1252–84); Alfonso XI (r. 1312–50); Pedro I of Castile (r. 1350–69); Juan II (r. 1406–54); Isabel I of Castile (r. 1474–1504) and Fernando II of Aragon and V of Castile (r. 1474–1516).
Master builders from Toledo, Granada and Seville were involved in its construction.
keywords: Seville Citadel; Mudéjar; Alfonso X; Alfonso XI; Pedro I of Castile; Juan II; rafter structure; qubba
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Fine Arts

es.name: Alcázar de Sevilla.
description:
El alcázar mudéjar de Sevilla se alza junto a los restos de otros palacios de épocas anteriores. Ocupado su emplazamiento desde época romana, se suceden construcciones omeyas, almohades y almorávides, muchas de las cuales conocemos a través de excavaciones arqueológicas. Las reformas de Alfonso X tienen lugar sobre el palacio almohade y se caracterizan por ser ampliaciones de los espacios precedentes. Todas ellas son de estilo gótico. Tras la batalla del Salado (1340), Alfonso XI remodela el patio del Yeso, al que le adosa una *qubba* de planta cuadrada con triples arcos de yesería a cada lado y cubierta por una armadura de limas moamares. Este espacio es conocido como Sala de Justicia.  
  
El palacio de Pedro I se adosa al de Alfonso X y se construye de nueva planta entre 1364 y 1366. La fachada, abierta al patio de la Montería, influyó en los palacios de Tordesillas (Valladolid), Comares (Granada) y el interior de la Sinagoga del Tránsito (Toledo). En el interior se distingue claramente una zona pública y otra privada. El área del patio de las Doncellas estaba destinada a actividades de representación con el salón de Embajadores, la sala de la media caña o salón del Techo de Felipe II.  
  
Se dice que el rey Muhammad IV, aliado político de Pedro I, le envió artesanos para que embelleciesen sus palacios. Tras una vista al Alcázar de Sevilla, mandó construir en Granada el palacio de Comares.  
  
En 1427, durante el reinado de Juan II, Diego Ruiz realiza la cúpula de media naranja del salón de Embajadores. Los Reyes Católicos amplían la planta superior y destinan para el rey la Cámara Real Alta. Al mismo tiempo construyen la antecámara, el cuarto y la alcoba de la Reina, la capilla y el antecomedor de Gala. Sustituyen las cubiertas a dos aguas del piso inferior por techumbres planas.

Paradigma de la complejidad del mudéjar del siglo VIII H. / XIV d.C. y de la arquitectura palaciega de este estilo, el Alcázar fue el resultado del trabajo conjunto de artesanos de Toledo, Granada y la propia Sevilla. Representa una síntesis de la tradición mudéjar toledana, del arte almohade sevillano precedente y del contemporáneo arte nazarí granadino, y está considerado el monumento más importante de todo el arte mudéjar. Destacan en él la imponente fachada y el patio de las Doncellas del palacio de Pedro I.
artist: Alfonso X (r. 1252-1284), Alfonso XI (r. 1312-1350), Pedro I de Castilla (r. 1350-1369), Juan II (r. 1406-1454), Isabel I de Castilla (r. 1474-1504) y Fernando II de Aragón y V de Castilla (r. 1474-1516).
Participaron en su construcción alarifes toledanos, granadinos y sevillanos.
keywords: Alcázar de Sevilla; mudéjar; Alfonso X; Alfonso XI; Pedro I de Castilla; Juan II; armadura de limas; qubba
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Fine Arts

fr.name: Alcázar de Séville.
description:
L'Alcázar mudéjar de Séville se dresse sur les vestiges d'autres palais d'époques antérieures. Son emplacement était occupé depuis l'époque romaine et des constructions omeyyades, almoravides et almohades s'y succédèrent, nombre d'entre d'elles nous étant connues par des fouilles archéologiques. Les transformations d'Alphonse X concernent le palais almohade et consistent en agrandissements des espaces antérieurs. Toutes sont de style gothique. Après la bataille de Salado (1340), Alphonse XI remodèle le Patio del Yeso (du plâtre) auquel il adosse une *qubba* de plan carré avec des arcs triples en plâtre de chaque côté et recouverte d'une charpente à doubles arêtiers. Cet espace est connu sous le nom de Salle de Justice.  
La palais de Pierre Ier est adossé à celui d'Alphonse X et il est construit selon un plan nouveau entre 1364 et 1366. La façade, ouverte sur le Patio de la Montería (de la chasse à courre), influença les palais de Tordesillas (Valladolid), Comares (Grenade) et l'intérieur de la synagogue du Transit(Tolède). À l'intérieur, on distingue nettement une zone publique et une autre, privée. La zone du Patio de las Doncellas (cour des demoiselles) était destinée à des activités de réception avec le Salon des Ambassadeurs et le Salon du Toit de Philippe II.  
On dit que le roi Mohammed V, allié politique de Pierre Ier, lui envoya des artisans pour embellir ses palais. Après une visite à l'Alcázar de Séville, il fit construire le palais de Comares à Grenade.  
En 1427, durant le règne de Jean II, Diego Ruiz réalise la coupole côtelée du Salon des Ambassadeurs. Les Rois catholiques agrandissent l'étage supérieur et destinent au roi la Cámara Real Alta (“Chambre royale haute”). Ils construisent en même temps l'antichambre, la chambre et l'alcôve de la Reine, la chapelle et la Salle du Festin. Les couvertures à deux pentes du niveau inférieur sont remplacées par des plafonds plats.

Paradigme de la complexité du genre mudéjar du VIIIe siècle H (XIVe siècle J.-C.) et de l'architecture palatiale de ce style, l'alcazar est le résultat d'un travail commun d'artisans de Tolède, de Grenade et de Séville. Il représente une synthèse de la tradition mudéjare tolédane, de l'art nasride grenadin, son contemporain, et de l'art almohade sévillan qui lui est antérieur. Cette citadelle est considérée comme le monument le plus important de l'art mudéjar. L'imposante façade et le Patio de las Doncellas (cour des demoiselles) du palais de Pierre Ier sont particulièrement remarquables.
artist: Alphonse X (r. 1252-1284), Alphonse XI (r. 1312-1350), Pierre Ier de Castille (r. 1350-1369), Jean II (r. 1406-1454), Isabelle Ire de Castille (r. 1474-1504) et Ferdinand II d’Aragon et V de Castille (r. 1474-1516).
Des maçons tolédans, grenadins et sévillans participèrent à sa construction.
keywords: Alcázar de Séville ; mudéjar ; Alphonse X ; Alphonse XI ; Pierre Ier de castille ; Jean II ; arêtiers en paires ; qubba
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Fine Arts

en.name: *Klemens Wenzel Lother of Metternich-Winneburg (1773–1859)*
short_description: Klemens Wenzel Lothar of Metternich was the leading diplomat at the Congress of Vienna (1815) who organized the balance of power between the European states. The core of Metternich's policy was supporting Austrian hegemony in Italy and preventing Russian hegemony in Germany. In the German Confederation, there existed an equilibrium between Austria and Prussian influences. Metternich's so-called "balance of power" politics ensured peace in Central Europe for a generation.

ar.name: جرة.
description: لاتتوفر هذه الجرة ذات الجوف البيضوي على قاعدة ولا على عنق، إذ تستند على قاع قطره صغير، وتقوم حشوة مقام الشفة. تمكن الآثار التي خلفها نزع العروات من الافتراض بأنها كانت مسطحة، وربما اتخذت شكل أجنحة، كما هو الحال بالنسبة لعروات الجرار الشهيرة لقصر الحمراء. تزين أربعة أشرطة أفقية مغطاة بطلاء زجاجي ذو لون أخضر برونزي الثلثَ العلوي من الجوف. تضم هذه الأخيرة عناصر زخرفية مختومة، محددة بشرائط بارزة من العجينة، حزت عليها زخارف متكسرة الشكل. استلهمت هذه العناصر الزخرفية المكررة التي تزخرف الأشرطة من عناصر نباتية (سعيفات نخيلية وزهيرات) أو عناصر كتابية. وتبدو على الشريط العلوي أشكال زخرفية مبسطة ترسم كلمة الله أو كلمة اليُمن (الهناء) للتعبير عن كلية وجود الله وطلب عونه وحمايته للمنتجات الغذائية المحفوظة في الجرة. وقد شاع هذا الشكل من الجرار ذات الطابع الزخرفي في المواقع الأثرية خلال فترة بني نصر في الأندلس.

كانت هذه الجرة البيضاوية الشكل تستعمل لتخزين المواد الغذائية. وقد سمحت العلامات المتبقية بسبب اقتلاع العروات بالافتراض بأن هذه الأخيرة كانت مسطحة، وربما على شكل أجنحة، على شاكلة "جرات الحمراء" الشهيرة.
keywords: ماء؛ زخرفة نباتية؛ زخرفة زهرية؛ زخرفة هندسية؛ زخرفة كتابية؛ خزف / فخار مختوم ومنقوش؛ طلاء زجاجي.

en.name: Jar.
description: Jar with an ovoid belly, with no neck or foot, resting on a narrow base. A roll acts as a spout. The marks left by the removal of the handles suggest that they were flat and perhaps wing-shaped like the famous jars of the Alhambra. The upper third of the belly is decorated with four horizontal strips covered with a green-bronze glaze. These strips have stamped motifs and are delimited by clay cordons with incised chevron patterns. The repetitive motifs that decorate the strips are plant-like (palm leaves and fleurons) or epigraphic. On the top strip, stylised patterns seem to reproduce the word 'Allah' or *al-yumn* (happiness), to express God's omnipresence and to have it protect the food kept in the jar. This form of decorative jar is frequently found on the archaeological sites from the Nasrid period of al-Andalus.
This egg-shaped jar was used to store foodstuffs. The marks left when the handles were removed suggest that they were flat, possibly wing-shaped, like the famous 'Alhambra jars'.
keywords: water; vegetal decoration; floral decoration; geometric decoration; epigraphic decoration
materials: Clay-coil ceramic stamped and engraved, with a trace of glaze.

es.name: Tinaja.
description:
Esta tinaja de panza ovoide, sin pie ni cuello, descansa sobre una reducida base. Los labios presentan anulares. Las señales de la extracción de las asas sugieren que éstas eran planas e incluso en forma de alas, como los famosos jarrones de la Alhambra. El tercio superior de la panza está decorado con cuatro frisos horizontales con recubrimiento vidriado en verde bronce; éstos lucen motivos estampados y están enmarcados con cordones de espiguillas incisas.  
Los motivos repetitivos que adornan los frisos presentan motivos vegetales (palmas y florones) o epigráficos. En el friso superior, unos diseños estilizados parecen reproducir la palabra Allah, o *al-yumna* (la felicidad), para expresar la omnipresencia de Dios y obtener su protección para los alimentos conservados en la tinaja. Este tipo de recipiente decorativo es común en los yacimientos arqueológicos de la época nazarí de al-Andalus.

Esta tinaja de panza ovoide se empleaba para conservar alimentos. De las marcas de la extracción de las asas se deduce que eran planas, incluso en forma de alas, como las de los famosos “jarrones de la Alhambra”.
dates: Siglos VII-VIII de la Hégira/XIII-XIV d. C.

fr.name: Jarre.
description: Cette jarre à panse ovoïde, sans pieds, reposant sur un fond de faible diamètre, est dépourvue de col. Un bourrelet fait office de lèvres. Les marques laissées par l'arrachage des anses permettent de supposer que ces dernières étaient plates et peut-être en forme d'ailes, comme les fameuses jarres de l'Alhambra. Le tiers supérieur de la panse est décoré de quatre bandeaux horizontaux recouverts d'une glaçure vert bronze. Ces bandeaux portent des motifs estampés et sont délimités par des cordons de pâte sur lesquels sont incisés des chevrons. Les motifs répétitifs qui meublent les bandeaux sont d'inspiration végétale (palmes et fleurons) ou épigraphique. Sur le bandeau supérieur en effet, des motifs stylisés semblent reproduire le mot *Allah*, ou *alyoumne* (la félicité),pour exprimer l'omniprésence de Dieu et attirer sa protection sur les produits alimentaires conservés dans la jarre. Cette forme de jarre à caractère décoratif est fréquente sur les sites archéologiques d'époque nasride d'al-Andalus.

Cette jarre à panse ovoïde était utilisée pour stocker les denrées alimentaires. Les marques laissées par l'arrachage des anses permettent de supposer que celles-ci étaient plates, peut-être en forme d'ailes, comme les fameuses “jarres de l'Alhambra”.
dates: VIIe-VIIIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIIIe-XIVe siècle J.-C.).

en.name: Sufi assembly
description: The miniature features a nocturnal landscape with a dervish surrounded by six male characters wearing costumes typical of the age of Shah Abbas I (1588-1629). The exquisite finesse of the drawing is enhanced by the subdued colour range, the gold highlights and the beautiful *nasta'liq* calligraphy of the Persian verses: ‘Don’t drink the wine-cup, for every drop is a king’s blood,/Don’t listen to the music, for every tune is just a tale of sorrow./The night has fallen; the drunken feast has neither lamp nor candle; /Join us, for the gathering of maids most fair is pleasant.’ (Translated into English from the Romanian version by Viorel Bageacu, 1987). The verses, as well as the image, are replete with Sufi symbolism.

names: Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico 'L. Pigorini', Sala Espositiva
short_description: The origins, in terms of scientific activity and conservation, of the Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome, can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the “Regio Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico di Roma" (Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography). Initially the museum was located in a wing of the Palazzo del Collegio Romano built in the late 16th century by the Society of Jesus. This rare image represents the old arrangement of one of the rooms of the Roman College, where the collection of antiquities and curiosities gathered together by Father Athanasius Kircher was kept after the foundation of the museum. According to the intentions of its founder, Luigi Pigorini, the purpose of this new institution was not only to gather together the remains of Italian prehistoric culture and the "primitive" cultures of other European and non-European peoples in a central museum located in the new capital of the Kingdom, but above all to support, promote and participate in research by palethnologists in Italy.
