en.name: Museum of Raqqada
description:
Whilst the second section of the museum is awaiting completion, several rooms have already been opened to the public.  
The ceramics’ room is distinct for the variety of its collection, which brings together objects that have come mainly from archaeological digs on the sites of Raqqada – the Aghlabid Capital during the 3rd/9th century – and Sabra al-Mansuriya, the Fatimid and Zirid Capital during the 4th/10th–5th/11th century. Several beautiful specimens of Egyptian, Syrian and Iranian (Persian) ceramics add to, and embellish, the exhibition. The Kairouanese potter, certainly inspired by Berber decorations, demonstrates his rich and creative imagination through the creation of clever compositions in which stereotyped flora and timeless fauna are mixed together, interwoven or placed next to geometric patterns.  
The medals’ room presents an exhaustive display of Islamic money in Tunisia. This display allows one to follow its evolution and its typology during a period of over 1000 years. Generally genuine in worth, the Ifriqiyan *dinar* has seen its weight vary from 4.25g. – in accordance with official metrology of the Aghlabid, Fatimid and Zirid periods – to 4.76g. during the Hafsid period. A map showing the main centres of coin stamping is also displayed within this window.  
The money collection is exhibited in chronological order, divided into dynasties:  
— Aghlabid coinage, which was minted and stamped along the lines of eastern models, is characterised by the presence of the sovereign emblem, the *ghalaba*. It also carries the name of the prince and, in certain cases, the name of the servant, *mawla*.  
— Fatimid coinage reflects the Shi‘ite religious beliefs of the new masters of Ifriqiya, and changed in appearance when al-Mu‘izz came to power (341/953): the number of circles that figure is brought to three, on the right and on the reverse, and its features become more obviously Shi‘ite. Fatimid money was greatly sought after during the Middle Ages, denoting a flourishing economy.  
— Zirid coinage: the Zirid princes did not implement any changes to Fatimid coinage, they just added their names to it. But in 440/1049, al-Mu‘izz Ibn Badis repudiated his allegiance to the Fatimids and proceeded to change the coinage through incorporating Qur‘anic verses extolling his return to Sunnism.  
— Almohad and Hafsid money differs from the rest in terms of shape, a square inscribed within a circle, its diameter, ranging from 26–31mm., and weight, ranging from 4.61 to 4.76g. Its form reflects the Almohad and Sunnite creed, which states that the Mahdi is the Caliph of God.  
Finally, the dome room houses the crowns of light that once served to illuminate the Great Mosque of Kairouan. Dating from the 4th/10th to the beginning of the 5th/11th century, this extremely rare collection presents a sort of analogy to earlier Coptic chandeliers, but the crosses here take a floral and heart-shaped form, marking a change within the faith.  
Lastly, a variety of other collections are exhibited in the museum.  
Most of the glass objects originate from two fortuitous discoveries made on the site of Sabra al-Mansuriya in 1922 and 1983.  
The weights and measuring tools presented next to a modest panel of general information date from the 2nd/8th to the 4th/10th century and were used to set the monetary standard and to weigh pharmaceutical products. An interesting collection of lead weights, discovered on the site of Raqqada, dating from the end of the Aghlabid period and from the beginning of al-Mahdi’s reign (end of 3rd/9th–beginning of 4th/10th century), constitutes evidence of the highest scientific importance on Ifriqiyan metrology of the Middle Ages. The weights are engraved with a *kufic* inscription carrying the name of the reigning prince or his *qadi*, and calling for equity and generosity.  
The Qur‘an room holds a display of parchments from Kairouan. It consists of one of the most important and most famous collections of parchments of the Muslim world. This collection was put together through the use of endowments, *habus*, donated to the Great Mosque of Kairouan. The specimens on display cover a period that extends from the end of the 2nd/8th century to the middle of the 5th/11th century. It allows one to trace the development of calligraphy and gilding, illumination, binding and writing techniques employed in Ifriqiya for over three centuries. Writing, which was generally done in *kufic* script, evolved to give birth to a Maghrebi *kufic* script (window display 2), *rayhani* (windows 3 and 4), represented most eloquently by the Qur‘an of Fatima, the wet-nurse, *alhadina*, of the Zirid prince Badis. This Qur‘an was written using diacritical signs, and was then gilded and bound by ‘Ali, son of Ahmad al-Warraq the librarian, in 412/1022. The diacritical signs are generally highlighted, according to an elaborate system conceived by Abu al-’Aswad in the 1st/7th century, by using red dots, in line with the Iraqi method (windows 5 and 2), or by using multicoloured dots in line with the Andalusian method.

es.name: Museo de Raqqada
description:
A la espera del acondicionamiento de la segunda parte del museo, ya han sido abiertas al público cuatro salas.  
La sala de la cerámica reúne objetos que provienen esencialmente de las excavaciones del enclave de Raqqada, capital de los aglabíes en el siglo III/IX, y de Sabra el-Mansuriya, capital de los fatimíes y de los ziríes en los siglos IV/X y V/XI. Algunos objetos de cerámica egipcia, siria e iraní aportan su belleza igualmente a esta exposición. Los alfareros de Kairuán, que se inspiraban ciertamente en el repertorio decorativo beréber, mostraron una fecunda imaginación que nos ofrece sabias composiciones en las que se mezclan, entrelazan o simplemente se unen la geometría con una flora estereotipada y una fauna figurativa.  
Por otra parte, la sala de numismática presenta un exhaustivo muestrario de monedas islámicas tunecinas. Este muestrario permite seguir su evolución y tipología durante más de mil años. Generalmente de buena aleación, el dinar de Ifriqiya ha visto variar su peso entre los 4,25 g de la metrología oficial de las épocas aglabíes, fatimí y zirí, hasta los 4,76 g de la época hafsí. Un cuadro de los principales centros de acuñación de Túnez aparece expuesto en la vitrina 1.  
La colección de monedas está organizada siguiendo las diferentes dinastías y según un orden cronológico:  
— La moneda aglabí, acuñada según los modelos orientales, se caracteriza por la presencia del emblema de los soberanos (*galaba*). Suele incluir también el nombre del príncipe y, en algunos casos, el de su siervo.  
— La moneda fatimí refleja las creencias religiosas chiíes de los nuevos dueños de Ifriqiya. A partir del reinado de el-Muizz (341/953) cambia de aspecto y se convierte en una moneda completamente chií. La moneda fatimí fue muy codiciada en la Edad Media y refleja una floreciente actividad económica.  
— Respecto a la moneda zirí, podemos decir que los príncipes ziríes no aportan ningún cambio al contenido de la moneda fatimí y simplemente se limitan a añadir sus nombres. Sin embargo, el-Mu‘izz ben Badis, que se negaba a obedecer a los fatimíes en el año 440/1049, procedió a cambiar la moneda incorporando versos coránicos que mostraban su vuelta al sunnismo.  
— La moneda almohade y hafsí difiere de otras monedas por su forma, puesto que se trata de un cuadrado inscrito en un círculo. Su calibre es de 26 a 31 mm y su peso va de los 4,61 a los 4,76 g. Las fórmulas que aparecen en estas monedas reflejan el credo almohade sunní en el que se atestigua que el Mahdi es el califa de Dios.  
La sala de la cúpula conserva aún las lámparas que en su día sirvieron para iluminar la Mezquita Mayor de Kairuán. Esta curiosa y rara colección data del siglo IV/X y principios del V/XI, y presenta una clara analogía con las arañas coptas, aunque las cruces que hay en ellas toman aquí formas florales y cordiformes para reflejar las diferentes creencias.  
En el museo se exponen también otras colecciones, como un lote de piezas de cristal tomadas esencialmente de dos descubrimientos casuales en el enclave de Sabra el-Mansuriya en 1922 y 1983.  
Los utensilios de pesos y medidas, presentados cerca de un modesto panel con diversos elementos, datables en los siglos II/VIII al IV/X y que servían como escala monetaria, eran también utilizados para pesar productos farmacéuticos. Una interesante colección de pesas de plomo descubiertas en el enclave de Raqqada y datables a finales de la época aglabí y principios del reinado de el-Mahdi (finales del siglo III/IX y principios del IV/X), constituye un testimonio de la mayor importancia científica para la metrología ifriqí de la Edad Media. Los pesos están grabados con una inscripción cúfica con el nombre del príncipe reinante o de su cadí y llaman a la equidad y la generosidad.  
La sala del Corán contiene una colección de pergaminos de Kairuán. Se trata de una de las más importantes y famosas colecciones de pergaminos del mundo musulmán. Esta colección fue formándose a través de legados (*habus*) hechos a la Mezquita Mayor de Kairuán. Los ejemplares que se han expuesto cubren un período que se extiende desde finales del siglo II/VIII hasta mediados del V/XI. Permiten seguir la evolución de la caligrafía y las técnicas del dorado, el iluminado, la encuadernación y la escritura en Ifriqiya durante más de tres siglos. La caligrafía, generalmente cúfica, ha evolucionado para dar nacimiento a la cúfica magrebí (vitrina 2 a la izquierda) y rayhaní (vitrinas 3 y 4), que queda representada claramente en el Corán de Fátima, la nodriza (*el-hadina*) del príncipe zirí Badis. Este Corán fue “vocalizado”, dorado y encuadernado por Alí, hijo de Ahmad el-Warraq (el librero) en 412/1022. Los signos diacríticos están indicados según el sistema elaborado por Abu el-Aswad en el siglo I/VII, mediante puntos rojos, según el método iraquí (vitrinas 5 y 2), o mediante puntos multicolores, según el método andalusí.

fr.name: Musée de Raqqada
description:
En attendant l’aménagement de la deuxième partie du musée, plusieurs salles ont déjà été ouvertes au public. La salle de la céramique se distingue par une collection variée qui réunit des objets provenant essentiellement des fouilles des sites de Raqqada, capitale des Aghlabides au IIIe/IXe siècle et de Sabra el-Mansouriyya, capitale des Fatimides et des Zirides aux IVe/Xe-Ve/XIe siècles. Quelques beaux spécimens de la céramique égyptienne, syrienne et iranienne viennent embellir l’exposition. Le potier kairouanais, qui s’inspire certainement du répertoire décoratif berbère, y fait preuve d’une imagination féconde et créatrice qui nous introduit dans de savantes compositions où se mêlent, s’entrecroisent ou voisinent la géométrie, la flore stéréotypée et la faune figée.  
La salle des médailles présente quant à elle un tableau exhaustif de la monnaie musulmane en Tunisie. Ce tableau permet de suivre son évolution et sa typologie pendant plus de mille ans. Généralement de bon aloi, le dinar ifriqiyen a vu son poids varier entre 4,25 g, conformément à la métrologie officielle aux époques aghlabide, fatimide et ziride, et 4,76 g à l’époque hafside. Une carte des principaux centres de frappe de Tunis est exposée dans cette vitrine.  
La collection des monnaies est exposée par dynastie et selon un ordre chronologique:  
\- La monnaie aghlabide qui fut frappée selon les modèles orientaux se caractérise par la présence de l’emblème de la souveraineté, *ghalaba*. Elle porte aussi le nom du prince et dans quelques cas du serviteur, *mawla*.  
\- La monnaie fatimide reflète les croyances religieuses chiites des nouveaux maîtres de l’Ifriqiya et, à partir du règne d’el-Mou‘izz (341/953), elle change d’aspect: le nombre de cercles y figurant est porté à trois au droit et au revers et son contenu devient plus nettement chiite. La monnaie fatimide fut très convoitée au Moyen Âge; elle dénote une activité économique florissante.  
\- La monnaie ziride: les princes zirides n’apportèrent pas de changement au contenu de la monnaie fatimide; ils se limitèrent à y ajouter leurs noms. Mais el-Mou‘izz Ibn Badis répudia en 440/1049 l’obédience fatimide et procéda à des changements sur la monnaie en y incorporant des versets coraniques annonçant son retour au sunnisme.  
\- La monnaie almohade et hafside diffère des autres monnaies par sa forme, un carré inscrit dans un cercle, son calibre, de 26 à 31 mm et son poids, de 4,61 à 4,76 g. Le formulaire reflète le credo almohade et sunnite qui atteste que le Mahdi est le calife de Dieu.  
La salle de la coupole enfin renferme les couronnes de lumière qui servaient jadis à éclairer la Grande Mosquée de Kairouan. Datable du IVe/Xe au début du Ve/XIe siècle, cette collection, très rare, présente une analogie certaine avec les lustres coptes antérieurs, mais les croix prennent ici des formes florales et cordiformes marquant le changement dans la croyance. Diverses autres collections sont enfin exposées sur le musée.  
Le lot de pièces en verre provient essentiellement de deux découvertes fortuites faites sur le site de Sabra el-Mansouriyya en 1922 et en 1983.  
Les éléments de poids et mesures présentés à côté d’un modeste panneau de généraux, datables du IIe/VIIIe siècle au IVe/Xe siècle, servaient d’étalon monétaire et étaient utilisés pour peser les produits pharmaceutiques. Une collection intéressante de poids en plomb, découverts dans le site de Raqqada et datables de la fin de l’époque aghlabide et du début du règne d’el-Mahdi, fin IIIe/IXe siècle-début IVe/Xe siècle, constitue un document de la plus haute importance scientifique sur la métrologie ifriqiyenne au Moyen Âge. Les poids sont gravés d’une inscription coufique portant le nom du prince régnant ou de son cadi et appelant à l’équité et à la générosité.  
La salle du Coran propose une collection de parchemins de Kairouan. Elle comprend l’une des plus importantes et des plus célèbres collections de parchemins du monde musulman. Cette collection fut constituée en legs, *habous*, au profit de la Grande Mosquée de Kairouan. Les spécimens exposés couvrent une période qui s’étend de la fin du IIe/VIIIe siècle jusqu’au milieu du Ve/XIe siècle. Elle permet de suivre la calligraphie et les techniques de dorure, d’enluminure, de reliure et de l’écriture en Ifriqiya pendant plus de trois siècles. L’écriture, généralement coufique, a évolué pour donner naissance à une écriture coufique maghrébine (vitrine 2), *rayhani* (vitrines 3 et 4), que représente de la façon la plus éloquente le Coran de Fatima, la nourrice, *elhadhina* du prince ziride Badis. Ce Coran fut écrit avec les signes diacritiques, doré et relié par Ali fils d’Ahmad el-Warraq le libraire, en 412/1022. Les signes diacritiques sont généralement indiqués selon le système élaboré par Abou el-Aswad au Ier/VIIe siècle, par des points rouges, selon la méthode irakienne (vitrines 5 et 2), ou par des points multicolores, selon la méthode andalouse.

cs.name: Klášter augustiniánů – poustevníků sv. Tomáše apoštola, Brno
description: Východiskem do stran roztažené fasády kostela se zdůrazněním střední osy je italská manýristická architektura. O. a. J. K. Erna byli předními staviteli v 17. století na jižní Moravě. Dvouvrstvé reliéfní členění doplňují niky se sochami vlámského vakantního sochaře J. v. d. Furth, který vyvořil také sochy některých bočních oltářů a pracoval i pro brněnskou radnici. Původně dle funkcí jednotlivých částí kláštera rozlišené fasádování bylo sjednoceno až v moderní době.

Středověký klášter, upravovaný po škodách Třicetileté války, byl v 18. století přestavován. Stal se dějištěm jedné z největších církevních slavností, ale i sídlem gymnázia a univerzity. Světský charakter staveb byl využit koncem 18. století pro státní správu. V části dnes sídlí Moravská galerie. Kostel si uchoval z velké části stav ze 17. století. Hlavní oltář nese slavný obraz  F. A. Maulbertsche. Vybavení kláštera bylo dílem v Brně činných mistrů, jež však vzalo za své při bombardování  Brna r. 1945. Dochovala se jen knihovna přesunutá při zrušení kláštera na Staré Brno, kde studoval také J. G. Mendl, zakladatel genetiky.

Přestavbu provedl v 1. polovině 18. století M. Grimm. R. 1736 byl klášter dějištěm jedné z největších církevních slavností, korunovace zázračného obrazu P. Marie (Starobrněnské). Po zrušení jezuitského řádu sem bylo přeloženo gymnázium, jež se stalo jedním z nejlepších v habsburské monarchii. Od r. 1778 zde sídlila také univerzita.  R. 1783 byl konvent přesunut na Staré Brno, kostel se stal farním a budovy kláštera byly upraveny pro státní správu.

en.name: Augustinian Monastery, Hermits of St. Thomas the Apostle, Brno
names: Augustinian Monastery, Hermits of St. Thomas the Apostle
description: The horizontally spread frontage of the church, with its accentuated central axis, is an example of Italian mannerist architecture. The architects, O. Erna and J. K. Erna, were leading lights of Moravian architecture in the 17th century. Two-layered relief segmentation is supplemented by niches that hold statues by the itinerant Flemish sculptor, J. van der Furth who also created the statues for some of the side altars and worked for Brno Town Council. The original frontages differed according to the various functions of the monastery buildings, but these have been unified in modern times.

This medieval monastery, restored after damage sustained in the Thirty Years’ War, was reconstructed in the 18th century. It hosted religious festivals and also housed a grammar school and university. During the late 18th century, the buildings were used by the state administration. The late 17th-century appearance of the church is largely preserved. The high altar is adorned by a famous altarpiece by F. A. Maulbertsch. The contents of the monastery, partially the work of masters settled in Brno, were destroyed by bombing in 1945. Only the library (where later the geneticist J. G. Mendel studied) survived.
artist: Augustinian Monastery, Hermits of St. Thomas the Apostle, Provost Ondřej Zirkl, Abbot Matthäus Pertscher, Count Jan Křtitel Mittrovský

history: The monastery by the town walls was destroyed during the Hussite Wars and particularly during the siege of Brno by the Swedes in the 17th century. Its restoration was undertaken in 1665, when J. K. Erna started to build a new church nave. The reconstruction was completed in the first half of 18th century under the guidance of M. Grimm. In 1736 the monastery hosted one of the greatest religious festivities, the Coronation of the Miraculous Picture of the Virgin Mary (of Old Brno). After the dissolution of the Jesuit order locally, one of the monastery buildings became a grammar school, and became known among the best in the Habsburg monarchy. From 1778 the monastery also housed a university. In 1783 the monastery was transferred to Old Brno, the church became a parish church, and the monastery buildings were adapted for the state administration.

en.name: Stag glass
description:
The conspicuously shaped drinking glass has an inserted attachment in the shape of a stag with a peacock on its back. The hollow shaft and hollow body of the animal are used as a suction pipe via the stag’s muzzle. It required a great deal of skill to be able to drink from this glass successfully.  
There were no limits to the range of forms of trick-puzzle glasses. Producing them must have been a great pleasure for glass-blowers. Popular motifs included pigs, dogs, boots and pistols, as well as phallic glasses, which are evidence of hilarious drinking games in the 16th and 17th centuries.
materials: Colourless glass *à la façon de Venise*

de.name: Jesuitenkirche Innsbruck
description: Die Innsbrucker Jesuitenkirche wurde in Anlehnung an den Salzburger Dom errichtet, zu dem sie gewisse Verwandtschaft zeigt. Das zweijochige Langhaus ist ein von Doppelpilastern gegliederter Abseitensaal mit Emporen. Im Zentrum des Baus steht die von einer mächtigen achteckigen Tambourkuppel überwölbte Vierung mit Kreuzarmen in der Tiefe der Langhaus-Abseiten. Der Chor schließt mit einer halbrunden Apsis. Manche ungelenke Züge der Formenverwendung lassen darauf schließen, dass wesentliche Teile der Planung von den Jesuitenpater Fontaner stammen könnten.

Die Innsbrucker Dreifaltigkeitskirche, einer der wenigen großen Kirchenbauten in der Zeit des Dreißigjährigen Krieges im deutschsprachigen Raum, veranschaulicht die hohe Bedeutung, die der von Kaiser Ferdinand I. nach Tirol berufene Jesuitenorden in Staat und Gesellschaft erlangt hatte. Der monumentale Bau mit Doppelturmfassade und Vierungskuppel entstand unter dem Patronat von Erzherzog Leopold V. und seiner Gemahlin Claudia de’ Medici als geistlicher Mittelpunkt des Kollegs im Zentrum der Konventsbauten.
artist:
Architektur, 1. Bauphase: Matthias Kager (1575-1634, Planung); Hans Alberthal(er) (um 1575 – 1675, Maurermeister)  
Architektur, 2. Bauphase: Santino Solari (1576-1646) Karl Fontaner, Hans Schor (1585-1674) und Christoph Gumpp d. J. (1600-1672, Planung); Adrian Pfefferle (Maurermeister)  
Stuck: Georg Braun
history: Das Innsbrucker Jesuitenkolleg wurde 1561 gegründet. Als Kirche diente zunächst eine gotische Kapelle. Ein Neubau erfolgte 1619-22 nach Planung von Matthias Karger durch den Dillinger Maurermeister Johann Alberthaler, doch stürzte dieser 1626 wieder ein. Für den 1627-40 ausgeführten Neubau wurde der Baumeister des Salzburger Domes, Santino Solari, beratend hinzugezogen, die Bauleitung hatte bis 1635 der Jesuitenpater Karl Fontaner. Auch war Christoph Gumpp an der Planung beteiligt (u. a. die Fassade). Der Bau konnte 1646 geweiht werden. Fertigstellung der Fassade 1900/01. Nach schwerem Bombenschaden 1946-53 wiederhergestellt.
keywords: Gegenreformation; Jesuiten; Ordenskirche; Frühbarock; Kuppelkirche; Wandpfeilerkirche

en.name: Jesuit Church Innsbruck
description: The Innsbruck Jesuit College was built with reference to the Salzburg Dome, to which it displays certain similarities. The two-bay nave is a hall with side aisles and galleries structured by double pilasters. In the centre there is a crossing with cross-arms extending into the nave aisles, vaulted by an octagonal dome resting on a drum. The choir terminates in a semi-circular apse. Some ungainly forms indicate that the main parts probably originate from the Jesuit priest Fontaner.

The Holy Trinity Church in Innsbruck, one of the few large ecclesiastical buildings constructed during the Thirty Years’ War, illustrates the high standing which the Jesuit order attained within state and society following its summons to Tyrol by Emperor Ferdinand I. The monumental construction with its double-tower façade and crossing dome were built under the patronage of Archduke Leopold V and his wife Claudia de’ Medici as the college’s spiritual centrepiece.
dates: 1619–1622/1627–1640 (Early Baroque building and interior work phases)
artist:
Architecture, 1st building phase, planning: Matthias Kager (1575–1634); master mason: Hans Alberthal(er) (c. 1575–1675);  
Architecture, 2nd building phase, planning: Santino Solari (1576–1646), Karl Fontaner \[n.d.\], Hans Schor (1585–1674), Christoph Gumpp the younger (1600–1672); master mason: Adrian Pfefferle \[n.d.\]; stuccowork: Georg Braun \[n.d.\], Hans Schor (1585–1674), Florian Nut \[n.d.\], Frair Oswald Kaiser \[n.d.\]; altarpiece: Antonio Balestra (1666–1740)
history: The Jesuit College Innsbruck was founded in 1561. A Gothic chapel initially served as a church. A new building was constructed between 1619 and 1622 by the master mason Johan Alberthaler from Dillingen according to the plans of Matthias Karger, however, this collapsed in 1626. For the new construction executed between 1627 and 1640, the master builder Santino Solari, who was responsible for the Salzburg Dome, was appointed advisor. Up until 1635 the construction was supervised by the Jesuit priest Karl Fontaner. Christoph Gumpp was also involved in the planning. Consecrated in 1646, the façade was completed in 1900/01. The building was then reconstructed between 1946 and 1953 following severe bomb damage.
keywords: Counter-reformation; Jesuits; church of an order; Early Baroque; domed church; pilaster church

en.name: Sword Hilt with Design of Lion Heads, Arabesque Scrollwork, and Arabic Inscription
description: A gold sword hilt worked in repoussé and elaborately engraved with panels of scrollwork and a band of inscription highlighted with niello (a black metallic alloy of sulfur, copper, silver, and lead that was laid into the engraved area and heated to create the contrasting background). The inscription surrounds the blade opening. Lion heads adorn the quillions (the horizontal element of the handle which protects the hand). The handle and blade openings are surrounded by finely worked gold twisted rope rings. The handle socket is octagonal, its panels alternating between sides of overall-engraved scrollwork, with single delicate arabesque designs in the center. The cross-section of the handle socket is octagonal.
place: Made: Anatolia, Turkey, Asia; Excavated: Hamadan, Iran, Asia

en.name: Altar of St. Dionisius (Altar of the Holy Martyrs)
description: The Altar of St. Dionisius combines sculptures by the early Baroque sculptor from Varasdin, Ivan Jakob Altenbach, and paintings by the Slovenina painter, Hans Georg Geiger. The first domestic sculptor of major artistic note, Ivan Jakob Altenbach appeared in the mid-1670s. His work shows essentially that he overcame the surviving forms of Mannerism to achieve the stylistic features of the Baroque. The Jesuit church in Leoben, Styria, influenced the conservative, two-storey structure of the wooden retable.
place: The side chapel of St. Martyrs (St. Dionisius) on the right-hand (south) side of the nave
artist: Ivan Jakob Altenbach (active c. 1675–d. before 1692), Hans Georg Geiger (active 1639–d. 1681)

en.name: Station de Hijaz, Damas (The Hijaz Station, Damascus)
description: The Hijaz Railway Station is located on the western side of the Old City of Damascus, west of Bab al Nasr, near the entrance to Souq al Hamidiyah. It is situated at the intersection of al Nasr Street, Saadallah al Jabiri leading to al Halbouni area, and Muslim al Baroudi Street, which leads towards the Baramkeh district. The site where the station was built had previously served as the gathering place for pilgrims arriving from across Asia. Pilgrims assembled in Damascus before departing in a ceremonial caravan led by the Ottoman Governor of Damascus. The procession followed a route through the Midan district toward Qadam and continuing south toward the Hijaz.
keywords: Syria; Train; Pilgrimage; Hajj; Travel

ar.name: لوحة كتابية.
description: تتكون القطعة من لوحة من العاج داخل إطار خشبي ذي لون داكن يحيط به من الخارج شريط رفيع من العاج يليه إطار خشبي ذو لون فاتح. وتتألف الزخرفة الرئيسية للوحة من كتابة بخط النسخ نفذت بالحفر البارز تحمل اسم السلطان قايتباي وألقابه نصها "مولانا السلطان الملك الأشرف قايتباي عز نصره." وزخرفت خلفية اللوحة بأفرع نباتية ذات براعم مستدقة مفصصة وأوراق مشقوقة. وقد استخدم العاج والخشب معاً بشكل كبير في العصر المملوكي، إذ كان الخشب يُطعّم بلوحات مستطيلة من العاج أو بقطع عاجية نجمية أو مضلعة. وكانت هذه التقنية تستخدم في المباني الدينية والسكنية لتزينها بزخارف نباتية من الأرابسك أو بنقوش تحمل أسماء رعاة المباني وأصحاب الفضل وتثني عليهم. ويعتبر السلطان قايتباي (872 – 901 هـ / 1468 – 1496 م) من أبرز سلاطين المماليك الجراكسة. وكان من رعاة الفنون البارزين، وقد أمر ببناء عدد من العمائر الجديدة في العاصمة القاهرة وفي غيرها من المدن، مثل مكة والمدينة المنورة ودمشق. ومن المرجّح أن هذه اللوحة كانت حشوة ضمن باب أو منبر في مدرسته أو مسجده.

تحمل هذه الحشوة اسم السلطان قايتباي، وألقابه، منقوشةً بالخط النسخ، البارز على خلفية من الفروع والبراعم والأوراق النباتية. وقد استُخدمت هذه المادة النفيسة في تطعيم الأخشاب، وصنع التماثيل الدقيقة، وقطع الشطرنج، والعلب المزخرفة لحفظ الأشياء الثمينة، والمصاحف.
keywords: تطعيم؛ خط؛ خط النسخ؛ زخرفة كتابية؛ زخرفة نباتية؛ عاج؛ لوحة؛ لوحة كتابية.
materials: عاج  بزخارف من الحفر البارز وإطار من الخشب.

en.name: Epigraphic panel.
description:
An ivory panel set within a dark-coloured wooden frame. The panel itself has a thin strip of ivory around the outside of it and this is placed within a frame of lighter wood. The principle ornamentation of the panel consists of an epigraphic inscription in *naskhi* script. The inscription is carved in high relief, bearing the name of Sultan Qaytbay and his titles, it reads: 'Our Sovereign, the Sultan al-Malik al-Ashraf Qaytbay. May his victory be Glorious'. The background of the panel is decorated with vegetal motifs such as tendrils with tapering, lobed buds and split leaves.  
The use of ivory and wood together was an extremely popular technique in the Mamluk period, when wood was inlaid with rectangular panels of ivory or ivory pieces in star or polygonal shapes. This technique was used to decorate religious and residential buildings; it was employed to create vegetal ornamentation of arabesque designs, or made part of inscriptions bearing the name of the patrons or favoured owners, as well as laudatory praises to them.  
Sultan Qaytbay (r. AH 872–901 / AD 1468-1496) is considered amongst the most prominent of the Circassian Mamluk rulers and one of the foremost patrons of the arts. He ordered the building of a number of new edifices in the capital, Cairo, as well as in other cities such as Mecca, Medina and Damascus. It is likely that this panel was once part of a door or *minbar* in the mosque or *madrasa* that he ordered built.

This ivory panel bears the name and titles of Sultan Qaytbay in high-relief *naskhi* script on a background of stems, buds and leaves. Ivory was used in wood inlay, in carvings of fine figurines and chess pieces, and in decorated boxes for storing Qur'ans and other precious objects.
keywords: Inlay; inscription; naskhi script; epigraphic decoration; vegetal decoration; ivory; panel.
materials: Ivory; carved in high relief and set within a wooden frame.
tags: carved in high relief and set within a wooden frame.

es.name: Placa epigráfica.
description:
Placa de marfil con marco de madera oscura. La propia placa tiene una franja estrecha de marfil por fuera, que está situada dentro de un marco de madera más clara. La ornamentación principal es una inscripción epigráfica en letra *nasji*. La inscripción está tallada en altorrelieve y en ella figuran el nombre del sultán Qaytbay y sus títulos: "Nuestro soberano, el sultán al-Malik al-Ashraf Qaytbay. Que su victoria sea gloriosa". El fondo está decorado con motivos vegetales, como zarcillos con brotes lobulados y afilados, y hojas partidas.  
El uso conjunto de marfil y madera fue una técnica muy popular en el periodo mameluco; en la madera se incrustaban placas rectangulares, poligonales o estrelladas de marfil o piezas de marfil. Esta técnica se usaba en edificios religiosos y viviendas, que se adornaban con motivos vegetales con dibujos arabescos o con inscripciones que mencionaban los nombres de los patrocinadores o los propietarios, así como alabanzas a ellos.  
El sultán Qaytbay (r. 872-901 / 1468-1496) se considera uno de los gobernantes mamelucos circasianos más destacados y uno de los principales mecenas de las artes. Encargó la construcción de varios edificios nuevos en la capital, El Cairo, y en otras ciudades como La Meca, Medina y Damasco. Es muy probable que esta placa formase parte de una puerta o del *minbar* de alguna mezquita o madrasa construida por orden del sultán.

Placa de marfil con el nombre y los títulos del sultán Qaytbay en altorrelieve, en letra *nasji* sobre un fondo de tallos, brotes y hojas. En la madera se hacían incrustaciones de marfil para esculpir figuras y piezas de ajedrez con las que se decoraban cajas para guardar coranes y objetos valiosos.
keywords: incrustación; inscripción; caligrafía nasji; inscripción epigráfica; decoración vegetal; marfil; decoración epigráfica; panel
materials: Marfil; talla en altorrelieve con marco de madera.
tags: talla en altorrelieve con marco de madera.

fr.name: Panneau épigraphique.
description:
Panneau d'ivoire dans un cadre de bois de couleur foncée. Le panneau, lui-même entouré d'une fine bordure d'ivoire, est placé dans un cadre plus clair. Il comporte essentiellement une inscription épigraphique en écriture *naskhi*. Sculptée en haut relief, elle reproduit le nom du sultan Qaytbay et ses titres : “Notre souverain, le sultan al-Malik al-Achraf Qaytbay. Que sa victoire soit glorieuse.” Le fond du panneau est décoré de motifs végétaux, parmi lesquels des tiges à boutons évasés et lobés et des feuilles fendues.  
L'association de l'ivoire et du bois était une technique extrêmement populaire au cours de la période mamelouke : incrustation dans le bois de panneaux rectangulaires en ivoire ou de petites pièces d'ivoire en forme d'étoiles ou de polygones, sculpture d'ornements d'arabesques ou d'inscriptions au nom des commanditaires associés à des louanges. Cet usage était aussi répandu dans les édifices religieux que résidentiels.  
Le sultan Qaytbay (r. 872-901 H / 1468-1496 J.-C.), l'un des principaux souverains mamelouks d'origine circassienne, fut un éminent protecteur des arts. Il ordonna la construction d'un certain nombre d'édifices dans sa capitale du Caire, mais aussi à La Mecque, Médine et Damas. Il est probable que ce panneau faisait jadis partie d'une porte de *minbar* dans la mosquée ou la *madrasa* que le sultan avait fait construire.

Ce panneau d'ivoire porte le nom et les titres du sultan Qaytbay en écriture *naskhi* traitée en haut relief sur un fond de feuilles, de bourgeons et de tiges. L'ivoire était utilisé en incrustation du bois pour sculpter de belles figurines ou des pièces de jeu d'échecs et pour décorer les boîtes destinées à conserver des corans et autres objets précieux.
dates: Règne du sultan Qaytbay (872-901 de l’Hégire / 1468-1496 J.-C.).
keywords: Incrustation ; inscription ; écriture naskhi ; décoration végétale ; panneaux ; ivoire ; décoration épigraphique
materials: Ivoire sculpté en haut relief dans un cadre de bois.
tags: Ivoire sculpté en haut relief dans un cadre de bois.

en.name: *St. Francis of Assisi* Azulejos
names: *St. Francis of Assisi* Blue-and-white tile panel
description:
Our Lady of the Visitation Convent in Vila Verde dos Francos is a Franciscan Convent of the third order and, therefore, part of a noble residence where a few Franciscan friars lived a monastic life. D. António de Noronha, the owner of the residence, along with other nobles – both men and women – often went there to retreat.  
Society life necessarily followed strict social rules, which were taken very seriously. As part of the social mores was the struggle of the Christian soul against the Devil – Psychomachy – fundamental to salvation. Updated continuously up until the end of the Baroque period, the Hagiography (example of life) of St. Francis of Assisi was used as a didactic tale to explain to men, and especially to women, how to behave in society. As shown here, St. Francis was a sinner during his youth and, like him, people have the opportunity to resist temptation.  
The remarkable blue-and-white tile composition, by an artist from the Oliveira Bernardes' workshop circle, reveals a sophisticated technique and an artistic capacity to transform these moralising figurative *azulejos* into impressive iconographic themes.  
Handling the use of engravings in a most creative way, the artist adapted those compositions: pilasters with angels and *albarradas* (vases with flowers), to the wall covering as if it were a scenic architectural stage.  
This particular chancel panel recounts the episode of St. Francis converting Muslims in Syria during the Fifth Crusade. On this journey a woman with a lovely body but a "filthy soul" tried to tempt him. Feigning acceptance of her sinful offer, he took off his clothes and leaped into a fire, inviting her to follow him. He miraculously survived, having overcome the temptation and led the woman to salvation.
In this *azulejos* panel, St. Francis of Assisi is tempted by Evil, symbol of vanity and lust, one of the most regrettable sins of women. Evil Is conveyed here by a half-naked, half-devil woman.
holder: Sociedade Agrícola da Quinta do Convento da Visitação – SAG
place: Our Lady of the Visitation Convent, Vila Verde dos Francos
keywords: Women; education; Female education; still-life, Franciscan convent of the third order, Counter-Reformation
tags: still-life, Franciscan convent of the third order, Counter-Reformation

pt.name: *Painel de Azulejos* de S. Francisco de Assis
description:
Construído para albergar uma pequena comunidade de frades franciscanos da Ordem Terceira, o Convento de Nossa Senhora da Visitação de Vila Verde dos Francos ocupava parte do domínio de uma das residências de campo da família nobre Albuquerque Noronha, no século XVI uma das mais importantes da região, onde também está sepultado o seu fundador D. Pedro de Noronha. Muitos elementos dessa família - de que se destaca D. Catarina de Ataíde, a "eterna Natércia de Camões"- passavam grandes períodos no Convento em recolhimento.  
A sociedade regia-se por valores morais e religiosos muito específicos.  
A figura do Diabo foi muito representada durante o período da Contra-Reforma, como forma de evidenciar a luta constante travada pelo indivíduo contra os valores materiais e superação de si mesmo, para encontrar a virtude e a salvação da alma. A hagiografia de S. Francisco de Assis foi uma das temáticas mais utilizadas até ao fim do período Barroco, como instrumento didáctico e pedagógico, para fazer lembrar aos homens e explicar às mulheres como se deviam comportar em sociedade.  
Neste painel, S. Francisco de Assis, ainda jovem e pecador, é tentado por uma mulher, representada pelo Diabo. A magnífica composição barroca de azulejos azuis e brancos, atribuídos ao *Ciclo dos Grandes Mestres*, revela um exímio domínio técnico e artístico, capaz de transformar uma história moralizante pintada em azulejo numa impressionante obra de arte. Fazendo uso de gravuras de modo muito criativo, o artista adaptou doze painéis sobre a vida do santo e um sobre a vida de Santo António de Lisboa, articulando-os com outras composições com anjos, pilastras e albarradas (vasos com flores), cobrindo quase totalmente as paredes para criar uma cenografia no eixo visual do observador. Em estreita relação com o espaço exterior ajardinado, as jarras de flores e frutos azuis e brancos, delimitados por barras de volutas, reflectem a reverberação da luminosidade que incide sobre a superfície esmaltada.  
Este painel, em particular, conta o episódio de S. Francisco de Assis convertendo os infiéis na Síria, durante a V cruzada, período durante o qual terá sido abordado por uma mulher muito bela. Fingindo ter sido seduzido, o santo terá tirado a roupa e ter-se-á atirado para a fogueira, convidando a mulher a segui-lo. Tendo sobrevivido miraculosamente, S. Francisco de Assis mostrou ter superado a tentação, salvando também a alma da mulher pecadora.

Neste painel de azulejos azuis e brancos, S. Francisco de Assis é tentado pelo Diabo, símbolo da vaidade e da luxúria, dois dos mais graves pecados atribuídos às mulheres. Curiosamente, este Diabo, meio-nú, meio-mulher, foi realizado para a igreja deste convento masculino da Ordem Terceira.

en.name: Spontaneous feast for a *shaykh* at Tall Tishrin in northeast Syria
description: Unexpected important guests are also lavishly served, such as the tribal *shaykh* in the photo; his visit is considered an honour for the host family. Although the women, assisted by the elder children, immediately start to prepare, it might take at least two hours until the feast is ready. The family might own the chicken to be slaughtered, or its meat can be bought from a nearby butcher. In the meantime, the host chats with the guests, drinking tea or coffee with them. When the meal is ready, the bigger boys will carry in the food, taking meticulous care to place the big plate in the middle and the small bowls in such a way that everyone will help themselves, and therefore is on an equal level. Only then does the host invite the guests to eat.

en.name: Archaeological Museum
description:
The Silves Archaeological Museum was inaugurated in 1989. Built around a cistern from the Almohad period, it houses a collection relating to the local area, displayed chronologically. The most significant section is undoubtedly that which covers the Islamic period, represented by a wide variety of domestic artefacts, used in the most varied aspects of daily life. Quite apart from two capitals from the period of the *Caliph*s, originating from the city and belonging to the National Archaeological Museum, there are some other treats in store for the visitor. The most interesting pieces, either discovered in archaeological excavations or donated to the museum, are the mouth of a well, an apotropaic plaque and a small glass bottle, a quite unique piece in the context of Islamic archaeology in Portugal.  
The main exhibit is most definitely the cistern, which served as the museum’s emblem and around which the museum building was constructed. The well is a rare piece from the Almohad period, built in stone and surrounded on the outside by a spiral staircase providing easy and direct access to the phreatic waters; each flight of stairs is covered by a small, segmented tunnel vault.  
The Silves cistern was classified as a National Monument in 1990.

es.name: Museo Municipal de Arqueología de Silves
description:
El Museo Arqueológico Municipal de Silves se inauguró en 1989. Construido en torno a un pozo-cisterna de época almohade, alberga una colección de materiales del propio municipio que se presentan según criterios cronológicos. La parte más significativa es, sin duda, la que abarca el periodo islámico, representado por una gran variedad de utensilios domésticos que se usaban en los más variados ámbitos de la vida cotidiana. Además de dos capiteles califales provenientes de la ciudad y propiedad del Museo Nacional de Arqueología, destacan, fruto de excavaciones arqueológicas o de donaciones, un brocal de pozo, una placa *apotropaica* (contra maleficios) y una pequeña botella de vidrio, pieza única en el contexto de la arqueología islámica en Portugal.  
La principal pieza de este museo es, sin ninguna duda, el pozo-cisterna que le dio nombre y en torno al cual se construyó el edificio. El pozo es un raro vestigio del periodo almohade, construido en albañilería de piedra y rodeado por fuera de una escalera helicoidal que permite un acceso fácil y directo a las aguas freáticas. Cada tramo de escalera está cubierto por una pequeña y segmentada bóveda esquifada. El pozo-cisterna de Silves está catalogado como Monumento Nacional desde 1990.

ar.name: قطعة نقدية أو وزن زجاجي.
description:
قطعة نقدية من الزجاج الأخضر، مستديرة، حافتها الخارجية مرتفعة، مازالت في حالة مقبولة، وزنها قريب من الدرهم الذي يزن 2.97 غرام. وعلى وجهها عبارة في ثلاثة أسطر بخط كوفي؛ على السطر الأول: "الإمام الظاهر"، والسطر الثاني "المعز دين الله"، والثالث:" أمير المؤمنين". ويزاد في بعض تلك القطع اسم الخزنة التي سكتها.  
النقود الزجاجية قطع ابتدعها البيزنطيون الذين استخدموها أيضا للوزن، وانتقلت إلى العرب المسلمين في عصر الخلفاء الأمويين والعباسيين والطولونيين في مصر والأغالبة في شمال أفريقيا لافتقار تلك البلاد إلى معدن البرونز.  
أما الخلفاء الشيعة فقد استعملوا قطع النقود هذه لأغراض أخرى وخاصة في بداية عصر المعز لدين الله الفاطمي (341/953-365/975) وكانت تلك القطع النقدية تستعمل (كنقد أمانة) بدل القطع النقدية المعدنية البرونزية لأن البرونز كان نادر الوجود في تلك الحقبة في مصر. وكان يكتب على النقود الزجاجية من طرف واحد.  
وقد اهتم أكثر الخلفاء الفاطميين بهذا النوع من النقود كالحاكم بأمر الله (386/996-411/1021) والمستنصر (427/1036-487/1094) والظاهر وغيرهم. وعلى الرغم من أن سورية كانت غنية بمعدن البرونز ومتقدمة في صناعة الزجاج فإننا لم نعثر على نقود زجاجية فيها.
صنجة من الزجاج من المحتمل أنها استعملت  "كنقد إئتماني".

en.name: Token or weight.
description:
Green glass token with a relief border, in a reasonable state of conservation, weighing slightly less than one whole *dirham*, which is 2.97 g. The token is marked only with a three-line inscription in *kufic* characters within a circle in the middle of the front face. The first line reads ‘*al-imâm al-Zâhir*’, the second ‘*al azaz din Allâh*’ and the third ‘*amîr al-mu minin*’.  
Traditional Byzantine glass tokens were generally used as monetary weights, and this use was particularly common among Umayyad and Abbasid caliphs as well as among the Egyptian Tulunids and the Aglabids of North Africa. Shi’ite caliphs also used tokens for other means, particularly from the time of al-Mu’izz (AH 341–65 / AD 953–75). The fact that many of the tokens found are of identical weight suggests that they were used as ‘fiduciary coins’ in place of bronze coins, particularly as bronze was extremely rare in Egypt at that time. This hypothesis is supported by the fact that no glass tokens have ever been found in Syria, where bronze was abundantly available. These tokens are inscribed on at least one of their faces, bearing the name of the caliph and sometimes even the mint. Most Fatimid tokens come from the time of two caliphs in particular, Abu ‘Ali al-Hakim (AH 386–411 / AD 996–1021) and al-Mustansir (AH 427–87 / AD 1036–94), although a large number also come from the time of al-Zahir, al-Amir and other caliphs.
Glass token probably used as a fiduciary coin in place of bronze coin.

es.name: Ponderal o pesa monetaria.
description:
Ponderal de vidrio verde con borde en relieve, en regular estado de conservación, de peso ligeramente inferior al del dirham entero (2,97 g). Lleva solamente una inscripción una inscripción en el centro del anverso, en caracteres cúficos y dispuesta en tres líneas inscritas en una circunferencia. En la primera línea se lee “al-imam al-Zahir”; en la segunda, “al azaz din Allah”; y en la tercera, “amir al-mu‘minin”.  
Los ponderales de vidrio, de tradición bizantina, solían usarse como pesas monetarias, no sólo entre los califas omeyas y abbasíes, sino también entre los tuluníes de Egipto y los agglabíes del norte de África. Los califas shiíes utilizaban este tipo de piezas con distintos fines, sobre todo a partir de la época de al-Mu’ izz (341-365 / 953-975). De hecho, el que coincida el peso de muchos de los ponderales encontrados hace pensar que se usaron como “moneda fiduciaria” en lugar de las monedas de bronce, metal muy escaso en Egipto en aquella época. Esta hipótesis queda avalada, además, por el hecho de que en Siria, región rica en bronce, no se hayan encontrado ponderales de vidrio.  
Estas pesas suelen presentar inscripciones por lo menos en una cara, y en ellas se hace constar el nombre del califa y a veces incluso el de la ceca. La mayoría de las pesas de vidrio fatimíes pertenecen al mandato de dos califas, al-Hakim (386-411 / 996-1021) y al- Mustansir (427/1036-487/1094), si bien son también numerosas las que se remontan a la época de al-Zahir, al-Amir y otros califas.
Ponderal o pesa de vidrio que casi con toda probabilidad se utilizó como “moneda fiduciaria”.

fr.name: Jeton ou poids.
description:
Jeton en verre vert avec bord en relief, en assez bon état de conservation, de poids légèrement inférieur à celui du dirham entier, qui équivaut à 2,97 gr. Ce jeton présente, uniquement côté pile, au centre, une inscription en caractères coufiques, disposée sur deux lignes et inscrite à l'intérieur d'un cercle. Sur la première ligne, on lit : “al-imam al-Zahir” ; sur la deuxième : “al-azaz din Allah” ; sur la troisième : “amir al-mu-minin”.  
Les jetons en verre, de tradition byzantine, étaient généralement utilisés en guise de poids monétaires ; cet usage était courant, en particulier chez les califes omeyyades et abbassides, mais aussi ches les Toulounides et les Aghlabides d'Afrique du Nord. Les califes chiites utilisaient également les jetons pour divers usages, ceci surtout à partir de l'époque d'al-Mouiz (341-365 H / 953-975 J.-C). Le fait que de nombreux jetons retrouvés présentent un poids identique fait supposer que ceux-ci étaient utilisés en guise de “monnaie fiduciaire”, pour remplacer les pièces en bronze. Ce dernier, du reste, était très rare en Égypte, à l'époque. Cette hypothèse est corroborée par le fait qu'en Syrie, où le bronze abondait, on n'a jamais retrouvé de jetons en verre. En général, les jetons portent des inscriptions sur au moins une face ; le nom du calife est mentionné et, parfois, le nom de l'atelier de frappe. La plupart des jetons fatimides appartiennent à l'époque du règne de deux califes, en particulier al-Hakim (386-411 H / 996-1021 J.-C.) et al-Moustansir (427-487 H / 1036-1094 J.-C.). Mais nombreux sont aussi ceux qui remontent à l'époque d'al-Zahir, d'al-Amir et d'autres califes.
Jeton en verre très probablement utilisé comme “monnaie fiduciaire”.
holder: Musée des civilisations | Musée d'art oriental “Giuseppe Tucci”
keywords: jeton ; poids ; monnaies ; Fatimides ; inscriptions; numismatique
partner: Musée des civilisations | Musée d'art oriental “Giuseppe Tucci”

it.name: Gettone o peso.
description: Gettone in vetro verde con bordo in rilievo in discreto stato di conservazione, di peso poco inferiore rispetto al dihrâm intero, che equivale a gr 2,97. Il gettone presenta soltanto sul recto, al centro, un'iscrizione in caratteri cufici, disposta su due righe e iscritta entro un cerchio. Sulla prima riga si legge “al-imâm al-Zâhir; sulla seconda: “al ̀azaz din Allâh”; sulla terza: “amîr al- mu ̀ minin”. I gettoni in vetro, di tradizione bizantina, venivano generalmente adoperati come dei pesi monetari; in particolare tale uso era diffuso presso i califfi omayyadi ed abbasidi, ma anche presso i Tulunidi d'Egitto e gli Aghlabiti del Nord Africa. I califfi sciiti utilizzarono i gettoni anche per scopi diversi, e ciò soprattutto a partire dall'epoca di al-Mu' izz (341/953-365/975). In particolare, il medesimo peso di molti dei gettoni rinvenuti fa pensare che questi fossero usati come “moneta fiduciaria” in sostituzione delle monete bronzee. Il bronzo, del resto, era molto raro in quell'epoca in Egitto. Questa ipotesi è inoltre suffragata dal fatto che in Siria, ove il bronzo abbondava, non vennero mai rinvenuti gettoni in vetro. Generalmente i gettoni sono iscritti su almeno una delle facce, recano il nome del califfo e, talvolta, anche il nome della zecca. La maggior parte dei gettoni fatimidi appartiene all'epoca del regno di due califfi, in particolare, al –Hakîm (386/996-411/1021) ed al- Mustansir (427/1036-487/1094). Numerosi sono, però, anche quelli risalenti all'epoca di al-Zâhir, al-Âmir ed altri califfi.
Gettone in vetro utilizzato molto probabilmente come “moneta fiduciaria”.

partner: Museo delle Civiltà | Museo d’arte orientale “Giuseppe Tucci”

ar.name: دراويش تركستان ( تركستان قلندر) صورة : ف. اوردين
description: الصورة الفوتوغرافية منذ أواخر القرن التاسع عشر تصور مجموعة من الدراويش الجوالين الذين يرفضون العالم والذين شكلهم الخارجي يوحي أنهم ليسوا معنيين بالتقاليد الاجتماعية ويحمل عنصر من هذه المجموعة من الدراويش وعاءا – حيث يسترزق من التسول.  ومن الواضح أن الصوفية معروفون في أوربا باسم الفقير أو الدرويش وفي العربية والفارسية تعني فقير.وإن الفقر وعدم وجود ممتلكات هي المزايا الجوهرية لحياتهم. وهم ورعون متنكرون للحياة الذين ينظرون لكل شيء باعتباره مؤقتا وزائلا ويرفضون التقاليد القائمة والأصول والمبادئ وهدف هؤلاء الأفراد هو أن يصلوا ويفهموا الله كحقيقة نهائية ووفق برنامجهم فإن هؤلاء هم أصدقاء الله والذين أسهموا بشكل كبير في نشر الإسلام منذ العصور الوسطى. وإلى أينما ذهبوا كانوا يبشرون ويدعون لأفكارهم – بدون سفسطة دينية –  وتفسيرهم المنفتح عقليا للبشرية والإسلام وكانوا دائما ما يدفعون ثمن تصرفاتهم من حياتهم وذلك حتى اليوم.

en.name: “Sartian Dervishes“ [Turkestan Qalandars]
description: A photograph from the late 19th century depicts a group of wandering dervishes who reject the world, and whose external appearance suggests that they are not concerned with social conventions. A number of these mystics carry a begging bowl – they live from begging. Revealingly, the Sufis are known in Europe by the name of fakir and dervish, Arabic and Persian for "poor." Poverty and lack of possessions are the core features of their way of life. They are pious ascetics who scorn everything temporal and reject existing conventions, rules, and dogmata. The goal of these individuals is to experience God as the final reality. Following this programme, these "friends of God" have already contributed to the dissemination of Islam since the Middle Ages. Wherever they go, they preach – beyond all theological sophistry – their interpretation of an open-minded, and humane Islam. Not infrequently they pay for this with their lives – even today.

en.name: Historic Centre
description:
The old part of the town is similar to that of Vila do Conde or Viana, having been based on a rectangular grid of dwellings with narrow but straight streets. The fortress changed the area around the Parish Church, the façade of which faces the fort’s parade ground instead of the usual square.  
The built-up area was, and still is, the main street known as Rua Direita, which begins by the old keep, today the clock tower, Torre do Relógio, at the southern edge of the Mediaeval enclosure. On the other side was the Porta do Sol; the other two parallel streets are Rua do Poço and Rua dos Cavaleiros.  
Another important spot in times gone by was the Campo da Feira, where the market was held, originally founded by D. Dinis in 1291. This place marks the site of the town’s first great expansion.  
In Rua Direita, a number of houses with typically chamfered lintels in the doors and windows have been conserved from the Manueline period.

en.name: Floral Rug
description: One of the very few Mughal carpets the Budapest Museum of Applied Arts owns dates from the late 17th century and was probably made in Lahore. The museum bought it from an unknown person for 15,000 crowns between 1915 and 1924 and showed it at the 1924 exhibition together with two other Indian carpets. The central field features the small scrolling vine-and-blossom pattern common on *Herat* carpets, while the ornamentation and colouring bears the traits of Mughal carpets; sickle-shaped wisteria among flowers and palmettes and *ton-sur-ton* colouring (areas lighter than the ground without contours). The main border consists of red, undyed and ochre round and oblong cartouches with little floral decorations on a dark blue ground. There is an analogue of the irregular cartouches on a late 16th-century or early 17th-century Lahore carpet from the collection of Vojtech Blau, Inc., New York City, formerly in the von Pannwitz Collection, Heemstede. The Lahore carpet is the same size and with similar ornamentation, but earlier, from the second quarter of the 17th century. It was formerly held in the collection of the Corcoran Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C., William A. Clark Collection (26.297). The carpet was auctioned in 2013.

en.name: Breguet travel clock
description: Organisers of major sporting events, mountaineers, and even astronauts rely on Swiss timepieces today. In the past, military strategists who made history swore by Swiss clocks. For example, Napoleon Bonaparte used a pocket watch by Abraham-Louis Breguet at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815. The clients of the watchmaker from the canton of Neuchâtel included not only the French general, but also his opponents: Both the Duke of Wellington and Field Marshal Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher devised their battle strategies with Breguet watches in their pockets. Apparently Breguet was more concerned with sales than with Swiss neutrality! Incidentally, Napoleon was a real Breguet fan and owned a total of three Breguet timepieces. The only one that has survived, however, is a travel clock kept in the Swiss National Museum.
keywords: Napoleon Bonaparte; Abraham-Louis Breguet; Clock; Paris

en.name: Alleyways
description: The town of Asilah has not kept the rectilinear urban plan of the Portuguese town. The Moroccans, in repossessing their town, redressed the size of the streets to enlarge them once more, created *derb*s and impasses, and returned to the town its Islamic character, through incorporating a *qaysariya*, winding roads, *hammam*s and bakers’ ovens as well as craft, and in particular, weaving workshops.

es.name: Callejuelas
description: La ciudad de Asilah no ha conservado el trazado rectilíneo de la época portuguesa. Los marroquíes, al recobrarla, estrecharon las calles, crearon *derb*s y callejones sin salida, y volvieron a darle el aspecto de ciudad islámica, con una *qaysariyya*, calles tortuosas, baños y hornos, así como talleres de artesanos, en especial tejedores.

fr.name: Ruelles
description: La ville d’Asilah n’a pas gardé l’urbanisme rectiligne de la ville portugaise. Les Marocains, en reprenant possession de leur ville, ont rétréci la largeur des rues, créé des *derb*s et des impasses et redonné à la ville l’aspect de cité islamique, avec une *qaysariya*, des rues tortueuses, des bains et des fours ainsi que des ateliers d’artisans, en particulier des tisserands.

en.name: Pile carpet fragment
description: This long, narrow fragment appears to comprise approximately one-eighth of a small carpet-cushion, whose original dimensions were approximately 42cm square, as indicated by the two surviving outer selvedges which establish its width. The few small patterns found in the narrow main border (width 7.5 cm.) – bands, lozenges, and white cotton dots – are the standard form of decoration on small carpet-cushions. There was originally a perimetric *tiraz*, as evidenced by the word *Allah* which is woven in undyed cotton, as in Benaki 16151. The thickness of the pile is 4-5 mm and microscopic examination shows it to have been roughly handled, as with Benaki 16148. A possible explanation is that the carpets underwent a scraping in a fuller’s workshop.
keywords: Fustat fragment; geometric; kufic script; inscription band; linen; wool

de.name: Mittleres Deckenfresko im Riesensaal
description: Die Ausmalung des Plafonds im Riesensaal, die einschließlich des gemalten Stucks eine Fläche von ca. 500 Quadratmetern bedeckt, ist ein Hauptwerk des berühmten Freskanten Franz Anton Maulbertsch, am Programm wirkte die Kaiserin teils selbst mit. Das große Mittelfresko stellt eine Allegorie der Verbindung des österreichischen und des lothringischen Fürstenhauses, die flankierenden Ovale veranschaulichen die Regalien Tirols. Die Vermählung der Häuser Österreich und Lothringen wird als Triumphwagen dargestellt, begleitet von Personifikationen der Herrschertugenden.

en.name: Central ceiling fresco in the Riesensaal
description: The painted ceiling, including the painted stucco, covers an area of c. 500 square metres and is one of Franz Anton Maulbertsch’s major works. The empress personally contributed to its design. The central fresco shows an allegory of the union of the royal houses of Austria and Lorraine, the flanking ovals depict the regalia of Tyrol. The marriage of the houses of Austria and Lorraine is depicted as a chariot, accompanied by personifications of the sovereign’s virtues.

en.name: Sprinkler Bottle
description:
This little sprinkler bottle is a fine sample of the use of the mould-blown glass forming technique. After the free-blowing technique has been found, possibly around in the first quarter of the 1st century BC, the mould-blowing technique has developed and the desired glass forms and patterns were obtained by blowing into glass, terracotta, stone, metal or wood moulds. The use of angular and patterned moulds has usually made it unnecessary to apply additional ornaments. With this technique, mass production of glasses with the same form, measurement, and decoration can be produced by using a single mould.  
The sprinkler bottle has a pale yellow-green body, light green rim, and a very short cylindrical neck. Its rim is broad and flaring; folded over, in and flattened with cut-out underneath and there is a constriction inside at the junction with the body. The body was most possibly blown in a two-part mould; the rim and the neck were blown separately and added to the body. There is a small jagged pontil scar towards the edge of the flattish bottom. Its globular body is almost in an intact situation, except for one small, later filled hole. Zig-zag pattern of elongated, hollow lozenges and two raised concentric circles are clearly seen on the body and on the bottom. The body is partly covered with enamel-like weathering which mostly flaked off and left iridescence and faint pitting on the surface. There are also many large and pinprick bubbles on the surface.
keywords: Glass in Asia Minor; Roman period; casting; blowing; mould-blowing

en.name: Glass vessel
description: Professor Joseph Black, 1728-1799, was a distinguished researcher and teacher of chemistry at the University of Edinburgh. He was the first to identify carbon dioxide within the air and is understood to have used this large glassware in his classroom.  It is believed that this glassware was a special commission from Archibald Geddes’ glass factory in Leith, which more usually made bottles, and that Joseph Black’s chemical expertise made him a valuable consultant for his friend Geddes on glass composition and manufacture. These piece of apparatus were used for distillation, and the functional elegance of their forms reflects the skill of the blower to free blow a form beyond a bottle mould that was aesthetically pleasing and practical.
keywords: Glass artistry; scientific glass

en.name: Azulejo (glazed tile)
short_description: Apart from its utility function and use for cladding façades, the azulejo is, at the beginning of the 20th century, an iconic expression of Portuguese art. This panel, produced by the Faience Factory of Caldas da Rainha, depicts tiles made in Seville in the 16th century for the Palace of Sintra.
keywords: Azulejo; glaze tile; armillary sphere; National identity

en.name: Cecilia Cuţescu-Storc – *Scenes from the history of Romanian commerce*
The Dietrichstein Carpet
description:
An 18th century, or possibly 19th century, Iranian pile carpet with a large lobbed pink medallion dominating the centre of a dark blue field, framed by a yellow ground border. The central medallion is decorated with an ivory arabesque scroll amongst which are multi-coloured flowers joined by a network of blue stems. The centre-field is crammed with rows of large palmettes, some of which have sharply cerates edges so much so that they look like flames. Between the palmettes are pairs of elongated and wavy Chinese cloud bands in various colours. The border is decorated with three different sizes of multi-coloured palmettes spread in a repeat pattern on a scrolling network of vegetal stems.  
  
The Dietrichstein carpet came from a princely castle that belonged to the Bohemian and Austrian Dietrichstein family, whose seat was in the city of Nikolsburg in southern Moravia and near the Austrian border (known today as Mikulov in the Czech Republic). A descendent of the Dietrichsteins, and the man who sold it in 1929, claimed that the carpet had lain in the throne room of Nikolsburg Castle up to then. The Dietrichsteins were an important noble family during the 17th and 18th centuries, with connections and positions in the Austrian court. When the carpet was sold in 1929 by the then incumbent Prince Alexander Dietrichstein (1899 – 1964), he claimed that the carpet had been a gift to one of his ancestors by the Empress Maria Theresa (r. 1748 – 1780), who had in turn received it as a gift from the Shah of Persia. This story is now thought to be most probably fanciful family lore.
keywords: medallion; vegetal arabesque; cloud pattern; palmette; diplomatic gift
materials: Cotton warp and weft; wool pile

description: A capsule-charge gun called *Ida o Semlale* and crafted in southern Morocco in the early 19th century.

en.name: Altarpiece: The Builder Shows King Ladislav (St. Ladislaus) the Drawings of the Cathedral
description:
The large wooden winged altarpiece of St. Ladislav (St. Ladislaus) held a cycle of 12 paintings depicting the Life of St Ladislav; 10 of them are extant today. The winged doors, painted on both sides with eight surfaces, closed off the main niche of the retable.  
Hungarian-Croatian King Ladislav I of the Arpad dynasty (c.1040–1095) founded the Zagreb diocese in 1094.  
The iconographic programme of the paintings is outstanding, mixing traditional scenes from the history of Ladislav, with a post-Trent interpretation, reinterpreted by the painter who depicts the king as a saint; a merciful saint who was canonised in 1192.  
According to the wishes of the bishop who commissioned it, most of the cycle refers to the domestic milieu – referring to its history – contemporary aspirations relating to the unification of the country and the establishment of the diocese of Zagreb.  
The painting, *The Builder Shows King Ladislav the Drawings of the Cathedral* depicts King Ladislav wearing a crown, and the builder showing the king a drawing of the cathedral roof as it is being built. Two barely visible male figures also take part. A large cathedral (later demolished) was built in the 12th century on the site of a smaller one from Ladislav's time. A similar scene, *St. Ladislav Shows a Cathedral with Two Towers to the Virgin*, embellishes the Chapter's oldest seal dating to the 13th century.

A painted scene from the Life of St. Ladislav cycle, which links the legend of King Ladislav I of the Arpad Dynasty (around 1040–1095) with Croatian history, and accentuates the foundation of the diocese of Zagreb in about 1094.
type: Painting, part of a cycle for the winged altarpiece of St. Ladislav
keywords: Religious object; altarpiece; painting

ar.name: ركنيّة عقد.
description:
ركنيّة عقد مصنوعة من الرخام المادي المنحوت. تزيّن محيط الركنيّة عناصر زخرفية خطوطيّة على هيئة معينات مزينة بدورها بحبيبات. وزخرفت زاوية الركنيّة بوُريدة ذات ستّ بتلات، زُوِّق طرفاها بغصنيات تنتهي بزهيرة. كما حدد جزء العقد الواقع تحت الوُرَيدة بزخرفة مكونة من فصوص متشابكة.  
يحتمل أن تعود هذه الركنيّة إلى مدخل قاعة قصر.
ركنية عقد منقوشة كانت تزين مدخل إحدى قاعات القصر. زخرف المحيط بأشكال تسطيرية على شكل معينات مزينة بحبيبات. وزخرفت زاوية الركنية  بوريدة ذات ستة بتلات زخرف طرفاها بسويقات تنتهي على شكل زهيرة.

en.name: Cornerstone of an arch.
description:
Cornerstone of an arch sculpted from grey marble. Its perimeter is decorated with a linear motif in the form of a granulated chain links. The corner of the cornerstone is ornamented with a six-petal rosette that is decorated on each side with foliage ending in a fleuron. The segment of arch below the rosette is emphasised by a design composed of interlacing foils.  
This archway cornerstone probably belonged to the entrance of a palace room.

Sculpted spandrel of an arch that decorated the entrance of a palace room. Its perimeter is decorated with linear motifs in the form of granulated chain links. The corner of the spandrel is decorated with a six-petal rosette, the edges of which are decorated with foliage ending in a fleuron.

es.name: Albanega.
description:
Esta albanega de mármol gris esculpido muestra en su perímetro una decoración con motivos lineales en forma de eslabones entrelazados, ornamentados a su vez con orlas. El centro lo ocupa un rosetón de seis pétalos, mientras que los ángulos están decorados con un follaje rematado por un florón. El segmento de arco situado bajo el rosetón está realzado por una serie de arcos de medio punto entrelazados y en cuya base se suceden lóbulos.  
Esta albanega perteneció probablemente a la entrada de la sala de un palacio.

Albanega esculpida que decoraba la entrada de la sala de un palacio. El perímetro está decorado con motivos lineales en forma de eslabones entrelazados y ornamentados con una línea de cuentas. El centro está adornado con un rosetón de seis pétalos y, en los ángulos libres, con follaje rematado por un florón.

fr.name: Écoinçon d’un arc.
description:
écoinçon d'arc en marbre gris sculpté. Son pourtour est décoré de motifs linéaires sous forme de mailles elles-mêmes garnies de grènetis. L'angle de l'écoinçon est orné d'une rosace à six pétales dont les deux extrémités sont décorées de rinceaux qui se terminent par un fleuron. Au-dessous de la rosace, le segment d'arc est souligné par un décor de lobes entrelacés.  
  
Cet écoinçon d'arc appartenait probablement à une entrée de salle de palais.

en.name: Vase
short_description: In 1891 Sultan Abdülhamid II founded the Yıldız Çini Fabrika-i Hümâyûnu (Yıldız Royal Tile Factory) in the garden of Yıldız Palace for the purpose of reviving Turkish tile art and giving it a new direction and momentum. Vases, hanging wall plates and many sorts of daily-use wares were produced in the factory, including writing and dinner table utensils, card plates, lidded bowls, pans, *aşure* (a kind of dessert) trays, sugar bowls, tea and coffee cups. A vase with conical body with wide mouth and round foot. There is a landscape painted on its body. The rest of its body has an intricate floral design painted on a green base. On the base a stamp of the star and crescent and dates of 1312-13 written in Arabic can be seen.
keywords: yıldız ceramic; Turkish decorative arts

ar.name: تاج
description: القطعة هي تاج / إكليل زفاف مغربي  مرصع بشكل غني بالجواهر ومزين بالزمرد والأحجار الكريمة ويظهر وجه ذو شكل هرمي وخلفية مفتوحة.تقدم المجوهرات الذهبية المغربية غالبا  كهدايا مرتبطة بالسيدات من الفئة الحاكمة وربما كانت تستخدم في مناسبات الأعراس ويتم ارتداؤها من قبل كل من العروس المسلمة واليهودية ومكتوب على هذا الإكليل ""العزة لله و لرسوله"".
