en.name: Blossoming almond trees.
description:
One of Portugal's most well-known legends tells of how it was that almond trees came to be part of the landscape of the southern region of the country. An Arab prince, married to a Christian from the north, noticed that his wife lived in a permanent state of melancholy, and so one day he asked her for the reason for this enduring mood. She told him that she missed the snow, frequent in the north of the Peninsula, but which rarely fell in the more southerly regions. The prince then ordered the planting of almond trees, whose blossoming at the end of the winter would create the illusion of fields covered with snow.  
This romantic and highly lyrical legend does nevertheless contain some basis of truth and demonstrates deep links with the Portuguese land.  
Al-Mu'tamid, a poet and lord of the Abbadid dynasty (AH 461–84 / AD 1069–91), one day set a challenge to Ibn Amar, as they were travelling along the Guadalquivir: 'The breeze turns the river / into a coat of mail'. The response came from Itimad, a slave woman of Romaik: 'A better coat of mail cannot be found / since the river freezes it'. Impressed by the slave's beauty and by her poetic inspiration, al-Mu'tamid took her as his wife and made her queen. The family and geographical origins of Itimad were confined to helping construct the legend. Although the story told relates to the region of Seville, al-Mu'tamid was born in Beja and was a lord of Silves, having later governed a large part of the south of the Iberian Peninsula.  
Deposed from power, al-Mu'tamid ended up living in exile in Morocco, where he died on 30 Dhu'l-Hijja 487 / 10 January 1095. Itimad lies at his side in a mausoleum in Agmat.

Towards the end of the winter, the landscape of the Algarve is marked by blossoming almond trees. Legend has it that they were planted by an Arab prince in homage to his beloved, who came from the north, in order to create the illusion of snow, which is rare in the south. The legend is based on the romance between the Abbadid prince Al-Mu‘tamid and the slave girl Itimad. Impressed by her beauty and poetic inspiration, Al-Mu‘tamid married her and made her queen. Itimad’s geographical and family background helped to create the legend.
dates: From the earliest Muslim presence in the region.
keywords: almond trees; Southern Portugal; landscape; legend; traditions; al-Mu'tamid
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

es.name: Almendros en flor.
description:
Una de las más conocidas leyendas portuguesas narra cómo los almendros pasaron a formar parte del paisaje de la región sur de Portugal. Un príncipe árabe, casado con una cristiana del norte, se extrañaba de la permanente tristeza en que vivía su esposa, por lo que un día le preguntó a que se debía aquel estado de ánimo. Ella le contestó que sentía la falta de la nieve, tan frecuente en el norte de la Península y que tan pocas veces caía en las regiones más al sur. El príncipe mandó entonces plantar almendros, cuya floración al final del invierno crea la ilusión de campos cubiertos de nieve.  
La leyenda, romántica y llena de lirismo, tiene con todo un fondo de verdad y está profundamente ligada al territorio portugués.  
Al-Mutamid, poeta y señor de la dinastía abádí (461-484 / 1069-1091), un día lanzó un desafío poético a Ibn Amar mientras paseaban junto al Guadalquivir: “La brisa convierte el río / en una cota de malla”. La respuesta vino de Itimad, esclava de Romaik: “Mejor cota no se hallará / desde que la congele el río”. Impresionado por la belleza de la esclava y por su inspiración poética, al-Mutamid la tomó por mujer y la hizo reina. Los orígenes familiares y geográficos de Itimad ayudaron simplemente a construir la leyenda. Aunque los hechos narrados se refieren a la región de Sevilla, al-Mutamid nació en Beja, fue señor de Silves y gobernó después gran parte del sur de la Península Ibérica.  
Derrocado del poder, al-Mutamid fue desterrado a Marruecos, donde falleció el 30 de du’l-hiyya de 487 / 10 de enero de 1095. Itimad yace a su lado en un mausoleo de Agmat.

Los almendros en flor señalan el final del invierno en el paisaje de Algarve. Fueron plantados, según la leyenda, por un príncipe árabe en homenaje a su amada, oriunda del norte. De este modo se creaba la ilusión de la nieve, rara en el sur. La leyenda hunde sus raíces en el romance entre el príncipe abadí al-Mutamid y su esclava Itimad. Impresionado por su belleza y su inspiración poética, al-Mutamid la tomó por esposa y la hizo reina. Los orígenes familiares y geográficos de Itimad ayudaron simplemente a construir la leyenda.
dates: Desde la presencia musulmana en la región (siglo II de la Hégira / VIII d. C).
keywords: Paisaje; leyenda; tradiciones; al-Mutamid
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

fr.name: Amandiers en fleur.
description:
L'une des légendes portugaises les plus connues raconte la façon dont les amandiers sont devenus partie intégrante du paysage du Sud portugais. Un prince arabe, marié à une chrétienne du Nord, ne comprenant pas la tristesse permanente dans laquelle vivait son épouse, en vint à lui demander les raisons de cet état d'esprit permanent. Elle lui répondit que la neige, fréquente dans le nord de la Péninsule et rare dans les régions méridionales, lui manquait. Le prince fit alors planter des amandiers dont la floraison, à la fin de l'hiver, crée l'illusion des champs enneigés.  
Cette légende, romantique et empreinte de lyrisme, a toutefois un fond de vérité et présente de profonds liens avec le territoire portugais.  
Al-Moutamid, poète et seigneur de la dynastie abbadide (461-484 H / 1069-1091 J.-C.), lança un jour un défi à Ibn Amar, pendant une promenade le long du Guadalquivir : “La brise transforme le fleuve / en une cotte de mailles.” La réponse vint d'Itimad, esclave de Romaik : “Meilleure cotte ne se trouve pas/ dès le fleuve congelé.” Impressionné par la beauté de l'esclave et par son inspiration poétique, al-Moutamid la prit comme femme et la fit reine. Les origines familiales et géographiques d'Itimad ont contribué à bâtir la légende. Bien que les faits narrés se rapportent à la région de Séville, al-Moutamid est né à Beja et a été seigneur de Silves, ayant ensuite gouverné une grande partie du sud de la péninsule Ibérique.  
Dépossédé du pouvoir, al-Moutamid allait finit par s'exiler au Maroc où il est décédé le 30 *dhu'l-hijja* de 487 / 10 janvier 1095. Itimad gît à ses côtés, dans un mausolée à Agmat.

Vers la fin de l'hiver, le paysage de l'Algarve est marqué par des amandiers en fleurs. La légende veut qu'ils aient été plantés par un prince arabe en hommage à sa bien-aimée, originaire du Nord, de façon à créer l'illusion de la neige, qui est rare dans le Sud. La légende s'inspire de l'histoire d'amour entre le prince abbadide al-Moutamid et l'esclave Itimad. Impressionné par sa beauté et son inspiration poétique, al-Moutamid la prit pour épouse et la fit reine. Les origines familiales et géographiques d'Itimad ont contribué à bâtir la légende.
dates: Depuis la présence musulmane dans la région, IIe siècle de l’Hégire (VIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: amandiers ; sud du Portugal ; paysage ; légende ; traditions ; al-Moutamid
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

pt.name: Amendoeiras em flor.
description:
Uma das mais conhecidas lendas portuguesa narra a forma como as amendoeiras passaram a fazer parte da paisagem da região sul de Portugal. Um príncipe árabe, casado com uma cristã do Norte, estranhava a permanente tristeza em que a esposa vivia, pelo que um dia perguntou-lhe a que se devia aquele permanente estado de espírito. Foi-lhe então respondido que sentia a falta da neve, frequente no Norte da Península, mas que raramente cai nas regiões mais a Sul. O princípe mandou então plantar amendoeiras, cujo florescimento, no final do Inverno, cria a ilusão dos campos cobertos de neve.  
  
A lenda, romântica e plena de lirismo, tem, contudo, um fundo de verdade e apresenta ligações profundas ao território português.  
  
Al-Mutamid, poeta e senhor da dinastia abádida (461-484 AH / 1069-1091 AD) lançou um dia um repto a Ibn Amar, enquanto passeavam ao longo do Guadalquivir: “A brisa converte o rio / numa cota de malha”. A resposta veio de Itimad, escrava de Romaik: “Melhor cota não se acha / desde que a congele o rio”. Impressionado pela beleza da escrava e pela sua inspiração poética, al-Mutamid tomou-a por mulher e fê-la rainha. As origens familiares e geográficas de Itimad limitaram-se a ajudar a construir a lenda. Embora os factos narrados se reportem à região de Sevilha, al-Mutamid nasceu em Beja e foi senhor de Silves, tendo depois governado grande parte do sul da Península Ibérica.  
  
Apeado do poder, al-Mutamid, viria a ser exilado em Marrocos, onde faleceu em 30 de Dhu'l-Hijja de 487 /10 de Janeiro de 1095. Itimad jaz a seu lado, num mausoléu em Agmat.

As amendoeiras em flor marcam, no final do Inverno, a paisagem algarvia. Teriam sido plantadas, segundo a lenda, por um príncipe árabe em homenagem à sua amada, oriunda do norte. Assim se criaria a ilusão da neve, rara no sul. A lenda mergulha as suas raízes no romance entre o princípe abádida Al-Mutamid e  e a escrava Itimad. Impressionado pela sua beleza e pela sua inspiração poética, al-Mutamid tomou-a por mulher e fê-la rainha. As origens familiares e geográficas de Itimad limitaram-se a ajudar a construir a lenda.
dates: Desde presença muçulmana na região (séc. II AH / VIII AD).
keywords: amendoeiras; Sul de Portugal; paisagem; lenda; tradições; al-Mutamid
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

en.name: Calligraphy
description:
This composition features the Qur’anic declaration:  
Arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ  
Transliteration: *Ve cealnâ mine’l-mâ’i kulle şey’in hayy*  
English: “And We created every living thing from water.”  
Renowned calligrapher Hasan Çelebi presents the verse with his characteristic mastery of classical Ottoman *sülüs* and *nesih* forms. The sweeping curves and disciplined strokes create a rhythmic visual structure that mirrors the verse’s theme: the emergence and vitality of life through water.  
The work’s balanced layout and refined linework reflect the artist’s dedication to traditional aesthetics, while the verse’s universal message invites viewers to contemplate the sacred origins of life and the sustaining role of water in the natural world.
holder: İstanbul Su Müzesi / Istanbul Water Museum
keywords: Calligraphy; Qur'an; Verse; Water

en.name: Antigo Hospital de Nossa Senhora da Piedade
description:
Also known as the Misericórdia Hospital as it belonged to that charitable institution, the building was probably completed about 1511.The Manueline cloister has tall, narrow wings with elegant ribbed vaulting, prismatic corbels and decorative naturalist bosses.  
The former Private Chapel, dedicated to St Mark, is an architectural jewel, with Gothic ribbed vaulting and a most elegant entrance arch with naturalist decorations.  
The old hospital wards are very impressive, with their cruciform pillars supporting strong vaulting and pointed arches, although there is a total lack of decorative detailing as befits a building of this type. The bosses on the vaulting bear the royal arms of D. Manuel I, who was the patron of the institution.

en.name: *The Chapel at Bethlehem*
short_description: This drawing shows the chapel as it appeared in 1899. It was a typical destination for Christian pilgrims travelling from Europe and Russia. Christian pilgrimage was often seen as a starting point to describe "exotic" places and the "Eastern" culture. Some Christian pilgrims described in their writings historical and cultural details and curiosities and their impressions of 19th century Palestinian society, the increasing number of pilgrims – especially Russian and Jews – and the institutions such as the Russian consulate, English and German churches and Latin monks that accommodated the Christian pilgrims.
keywords: Pilgrimage; pilgrims; Christian pilgrimage; Jewish pilgrimage; Palestine; Holy Land; Jerusalem; sacred places; travel; travel book; Ottoman Palestine; local Jewish community

en.name: Islamic Loulé
description:
All that now remains of Islamic Loulé is the name (*al-‘Ulya* - the hill), the layout of the walls, the location of the mosque and little more besides. The walls enclosed an area of roughly five hectares and show that the town played an important role during that period, even though this is not mentioned in written sources. Some other architectural features also underline the importance of the spread of Islam in Loulé, and the memory of that period was later continued with the building of the municipal market, which is a fine example of neo-Moorish Revivalist architecture.  
Of particular note are the *tabiyya* or dry-mud turrets seen in the southern area of the old fortification. Next, note the minaret of the city’s mosque, over which was built the bell tower of the Church of São Clemente. Although there are iconographical references to the mosque’s minaret at Mértola and the foundation stone of Moura’s is also known, in Loulé we witness a rare sight: a minaret where the base has remained unchanged until the present day. Such an interpretation is made possible both by the arrangement of the masonry, (which follows an ancient building tradition) the location of the tower in relation to the church and the very fact that the orientation of the church itself is not at all in keeping with established canons.

es.name: Loulé islámica
description:
De la Loulé islámica hemos mantenido el nombre (al-Ulya, “el otero”), el trazado de las murallas, la ubicación de la mezquita y poco más. Cerca de 5 ha de área amurallada evidencian, con todo, una importancia que los textos escritos en aquel periodo no reflejan.  
Algunos elementos arquitectónicos dan fe de la importancia de la islamización en Loulé, y de hecho el recuerdo de aquel pasado se ha prolongado hasta la construcción del mercado municipal, una pieza revivalista neoárabe.  
Hay que llamar la atención, en primer lugar, sobre los torreones de *tapial* visibles en la zona sur de la antigua fortificación. Nótese, a continuación, la presencia del alminar de la mezquita de la ciudad, sobre el que se construyó el campanario de São Clemente. Aunque del minarete de la mezquita de Mértola hay referencias iconográficas y de la mezquita de Moura se conoce la lápida fundacional, en Loulé estamos ante el único alminar cuyo basamento ha llegado hasta nuestros días. Apuntan en ese sentido tanto la colocación de los sillares (que obedece a una tradición constructiva antigua) como la ubicación de la torre respecto a la iglesia, y el hecho mismo de que el templo tenga una orientación que escapa a los cánones establecidos.

en.name: Palazzo Barberini (National Museum of Archaeology)
description:
The palace is characterised by the coexistence of ancient structures - the concave dual-ring terminal portico of the sanctuary whose column bases can be seen on the floor at the entrance - and the structures built between the late middle ages and the time of the Barberini tenure. The inscription of the main portal, dated 1498, and the coat of the arms of the Colonna family on the well are evidence of the significant work commissioned by the Colonna family. Two central flights of stairs in the *cavea* and the installation of the well give the palace the character of an urban development, enhanced by the axiality of the entire complex, and underlined by the fusion between the ancient and modern structures.  
The Barberini family (Taddeo and his son Maffeo) highlighted the penetration with antiquity scenically through the internal restructuring of the central hall, by the inclusion of the covered roof terrace to the front, and the addition of a cruciform *nymphaeum* to the rear (designed by Francesco Contini in 1660), as if intending to display symbolically – in a sort of ideal appropriation of antique and Roman history – the new status acquired by the family.  
This continuous dialogue with "reused" antiquity was further accentuated by some of the outstanding objects from the region that were housed within the palace by Taddeo's brother Cardinal Francesco Barberini (1597–1679). Most notable among these is the famous multicoloured mosaic of a Nile scene that was originally the floor of a basin, which was found in the apse-room of the lower temple. It remains one of the most interesting and peculiar items in the museum.  
The interior of the palace is richly decorated with frescos of mythological, biblical and historical scenes that are attributed to artists from Zuccari's circle and which date, therefore, to between the late 16th and first-half of the 17th century. The final urban development, undertaken by Maffeo Barberini in 1656, was the introduction of a road connecting the lower and upper sanctuaries, the palace and the church.

The palace is characterised by the coexistence of ancient structures of the 2nd-century BC Roman sanctuary and structures built on top of them between the late middle ages and the time of the Barberini family's tenure. It was this link with antiquity and Roman history that the Barberini family highlighted in their scenically penetrative plan for the palace, which was intended to display symbolically the new status acquired by the family, by means of a sort of ideal appropriation of antiquity and Roman history.
artist: Taddeo Barberini (1603, Rome – 1647, Paris), Prefect of Rome, and his son Maffeo (1630–85), from his marriage to Anna Colonna
history: The town and Palace of Palestrina had been owned by the ancient feudal family of Prince Francesco Colonna until it was acquired by Pope Urban VIII (1623–44) in 1630 as a gift for his brother Carlo Barberini. The Barberinis, originally from Barberino in Val d’Elsa, were based initially in Florence where they were landowners and then merchants. In the 16th century the first prelate, Francesco (1528–1600) moved to Rome, and it was Taddeo Barberini, son of Carlo who died in 1630, who was responsible for the reorganisation and elevation of the palace. The palace crowns the slopes where a 2nd-century BC sanctuary dedicated to Fortuna Primigenia – famous in antiquity for her oracles – once stood. Having suffered bomb damage during the last war, in 1956, some ancient structures were revealed beneath the palace, which was then given to the State and turned into the National Museum of Archaeology.
keywords: Feudal palace, scenic, antiquity, Baroque, archaeology, museum, *nymphaeum*, water theatre
tags: Feudal palace, scenic, antiquity, Baroque, archaeology, museum, nymphaeum, water theatre
partner: Province of Rome (Città metropolitana di Roma Capitale)

it.name: Palazzo Barberini (Museo Archeologico Nazionale)
description: Il palazzo è contraddistinto dalla coincidenza tra strutture antiche - il concavo doppio portico anulare terminale del santuario, del quale sono visibili nel pavimento dell’ingresso le basi delle colonne – e le fasi costruttive che si sono sovrapposte dall’alto Medioevo fino ai Barberini. L’iscrizione del portale principale, datata 1498, e lo stemma dei Colonna sul pozzo testimoniano gli ingenti lavori commissionati dai Colonna che hanno dato al palazzo, attraverso la scala centrale a due rampe nella cavea e la sistemazione del pozzo, una connotazione urbanistica di assialità dell’intero complesso e di fusione tra le strutture antiche e moderne. Tale compenetrazione in senso scenografico con l’antichità è stata sottolineata dai Barberini – Taddeo e il figlio Maffeo – con la ristrutturazione della sala centrale all’interno e la realizzazione dell’altana sul fronte e del ninfeo cruciforme sul retro (1660 su disegno di Francesco Contini), quasi ad evidenziare in senso simbolico il nuovo “status” acquisito dalla famiglia in una sorta di appropriazione ideale dell’antichità e della storia romana. Questo dialogo costante con l’antico “riutilizzato” è ulteriormente accentuato dalla destinazione del palazzo a contenitore del cospicuo materiale proveniente dal territorio, tra cui si segnala in particolare il celebre mosaico policromo con scena nilotica, in origine pavimento di una vasca, rinvenuto nell’aula absidata del tempio inferiore e fatto collocare nel palazzo dal cardinale Francesco Barberini (1597-1679), fratello di Taddeo, ancora oggi una delle opere più interessanti e particolari del Museo. Il palazzo presenta inoltre all’interno una ricca ed interessante decorazione ad affresco con scene mitologiche, bibliche e storiche attribuita ad artisti della cerchia degli Zuccari e quindi databile tra la fine del 500 e la prima metà del 600. Un ulteriore intervento urbanistico promosso nel 1656 da Maffeo Barberini è costituito dalla strada di collegamento tra santuario inferiore e superiore, palazzo e chiesa.

Il palazzo è contraddistinto dalla coincidenza tra le strutture antiche del santuario romano del II secolo a.C.  e le fasi costruttive che si sono sovrapposte dall’alto Medioevo fino ai Barberini. Tale compenetrazione in senso scenografico con l’antichità è stata sottolineata dai Barberini con i loro interventi architettonici tesi ad evidenziare in senso simbolico il nuovo “status” acquisito dalla famiglia anche attraverso una sorta di appropriazione ideale dell’antichità e della storia romana.
artist: Taddeo Barberini (1603, Roma – 1647, Parigi), Prefetto di Roma, e il figlio Maffeo (1630-1685), nato dal matrimonio con Anna Colonna
history: Il palazzo e l’intero feudo di Palestrina, di proprietà del principe Francesco Colonna di antica famiglia feudale,  fu acquistato nel 1630 da papa Urbano VIII (1623-1644) per donarlo al fratello Carlo Barberini. La famiglia, originaria di Barberino in Val d’Elsa, era costituita da piccoli proprietari terrieri poi mercanti stabilitisi inizialmente a Firenze e nel corso del 500 con il primo prelato Francesco (1528-1600) anche a Roma. A Taddeo Barberini, figlio di Carlo morto in quello stesso 1630, si devono la risistemazione e la sopraelevazione del palazzo che corona la sommità dell’altura sulle cui pendici sorgeva lo scenografico santuario del II secolo a.C. dedicato alla Fortuna Primigenia, famoso nell’antichità per i suoi oracoli. Il Palazzo dopo i bombardamenti dell’ultima guerra -  che hanno riportato in luce alcune strutture antiche - è stato donato allo Stato nel 1956 ed adibito a Museo Archeologico Nazionale.
keywords: Palazzo di impianto feudale rimaneggiato in senso scenografico in rapporto con l’antichità in epoca barocca; museo archeologico
tags: Palazzo di impianto feudale rimaneggiato in senso scenografico in rapporto con l’antichità in epoca barocca
partner: Provincia di Roma (Città metropolitana di Roma Capitale)

en.name: Praça do Comércio
description: Praça do Comércio overlooking the River Tejo is an emblematic part of the *Baixa*. According to the engraving attributed to Gaspar Froes Machado, the initial plans were not entirely fulfilled; the triumphal arch was finally built in 1873 according to the design of Veríssimo José da Costa.
place: Facing the estuary of the River Tagus
artist: Initial plans of Praça do Comércio: Manuel da Maia (1677–1766), Eugénio dos Santos (1711–1760); Carlos Mardel (c. 1695–1763); triumphal arch: Veríssimo José da Costa [n.d.] assisted by Vítor Bastos (1830–1894) and Anatole C. Calmels (1822–1906)
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: Praça do Comércio
description: A Praça do Comércio, debruçada sobre o Tejo, é uma das peças emblemáticas da Baixa Pombalina. De acordo com a gravura atribuída a G. Fróis Machado, os planos iniciais não foram totalmente cumpridos. O Arco só foi edificado em 1873, segundo um projecto posterior de Veríssimo José da Costa.
place: Frente ao estuário do rio Tejo
artist: Planos iniciais da Praça do Comércio: Manuel da Maia (1677–1766), Eugénio dos Santos (1711–1760); Carlos Mardel (c.1695–1763). Arco triunfal: Veríssimo José da Costa [n.d.], coadjuvado por Vítor Bastos (1830–1894) e Anatole C. Calmels (1822–1906)

de.name: Gnadenaltar
description: Die bei Loreto-Kapellen übliche, das Gnadenbild vom Betvolk separierende Gitterwand ist in Birkenstein zu einer marianischen Bildwand umgedeutet. Das Gitter wurde entfernt, um einen freien Blick auf das zu einer Loreto-Madonna umgedeutete Kultbild zu erlauben. Der dieses umgebende Strahlenkranz evoziert zusammen mit dem figurenreichen Engelreigen eine Erscheinung Mariens als Himmelskönigin. Dies geschieht im Beisein der Trinität, wobei Christus als Kind dargestellt ist, denn aus den Himmlischen Heerscharen stechen die Erzengel heraus, von denen oberhalb der Türen Gabriel die Verkündigung vollzieht. Auf die Türblätter sind Josef und Johannes der Täufer gemalt, ans Antependium die Geburt Mariens. Die Tabernakelfiguren stehen für die sieben Gaben des Hl. Geistes: Weisheit, Verstand, Rat, Stärke, Wissenschaft, Frömmigkeit und Gottesfurcht, gemäß dem Spruch 9/1 der Lauretanischen Litanei: „Maria hat sich ein Haus auf sieben Säulen gebaut.“
artist: Skulpturen der Erzengel, Verkündigung und Trinität: Joseph Götsch (1728-1793); Engelsfiguren: Josef Anton Fröhlich; Gemälde: Sebastian Troger (um 1745-1792)

en.name: Altar of Grace
description: The church’s lattice wall — common in Loreto chapels to separate the praying individuals from the miraculous image — had been reintroduced as a Marian picture wall. The lattice was removed to allow an unobstructed view of the devotional picture, which was reinterpreted as an image of The Madonna of Loreto. It is framed by a nimbus. In combination with the set of angels, it evokes an appearance of Mary as the Queen of Heaven. This takes place in the presence of the Trinity, as archangels stick out from the heavenly hosts, whereby Christ is depicted as a child. Above the doors, Archangel Gabriel carries out the proclamation. The door panels are painted with images of St. Joseph and St. John the Baptist. The antependium, on the other hand, displays a painting of The Birth of Mary. The figures of the tabernacle stand for the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit: Wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety, and fear of the Lord; in accordance with Proverb 9:1 from the Litany of Loreto: “Wisdom has built her house; she has set up her seven columns.”
artist: Sculptures of the Archangels, Proclamation, and Trinity: Joseph Götsch (1728—93); angel figures: Josef Anton Fröhlich; paintings: Sebastian Troger (c. 1745—92)

en.name: Quinta da Regaleira
short_description: A man of inquiring scientific mind and vast culture, Carvalho Monteiro left imprinted in stone his cosmological vision, a synthesis of the spiritual memory of mankind stemmed in the Portuguese Mythical Tradition.  The art and architecture of the mansion and the chapel, built in neo-Manueline style, were conjugated with other buildings in the bosom of an Edenic garden. A “Philosopher's Dwelling” par excellence, conveying a message adressed to those who are are fit to engage in the Adventure of self-knowledge, Quinta da Regaleira emerges from the Sintra Cultural Landscape as an example of the Total Oeuvre and as expression of a new mythical territory, where Philosophy, Art and Nature come together.
type: Palace and Gardens; Unesco Cultural Heritage Classification
holder: Sintra Parks Monte da Lua, Conservation Company
artist: António Carvalho Monteiro (1848–1920); architect Luigi Manini (1848–1936)
history:
António Augusto Carvalho Monteiro (1848–1920) assisted by Italian architect Luigi Manini conceived The Garden of Quinta da Regaleira as a sacred and symbolic space,  
inspired by the Garden of the Desert de Retz in Marly; Torrigiani Garden in Florence amongst others. The choice of its location in Sintra, in the Monte da Lua, was relevant as a sacred site since the Neolithic, associated with legends and rituals of underground worlds.  
Carvalho Monteiro as a Mason filled his home with various symbolic references namely Christian, pagan, Neo - Templars and classical literature as Dante\`s Divine Comedy. The visiting trail, beyond the ludic aspect aims to recreate the theme of “death and resurrection” like the descent to the darkness before returning to the light.
keywords: Neomanueline; Romanticism; Nature; Garden; Spirituality; Mistery; Alchemy

en.name: Sanctuary and Altarpiece of the Transit of St. Bernard
description:
The Cistercian Monastery of Alcobaça was founded as a gift to St. Bernard of Clairvaux shortly before his death on an estate granted by King Afonso Henriques (the first King of Portugal) in 1153. Having just conquered the Arabs, Afonso Henriques wanted to commemorate his victory, and foundation of the monastery was part of his strategy to consolidate his authority in the new kingdom. The Monastery is considered to be one of the best preserved medieval monastery complexes in Europe besides being a bastion of the Portuguese nationality.  
Sanctuary: as part of the New Sacristy, this Chapel was called the “Mirror of Heaven” by the eminent Portuguese art historian, Reinaldo dos Santos, due to its supreme beauty and spirituality. Building began in 1670 when Frei Constantino Sampaio was Abbot of the Monastery (1669–1672).  
With an octagonal plan, the interior is fully covered with gilded wood and is lit by a ceiling lantern. This light, filtered and diffused, enhances the theatrical atmosphere of the gilded and polychrome Baroque octagonal structure, which includes six horizontal niches filled by 89 reliquary sculptures.  
Altarpiece of the Transit of St. Bernard: the sculptural ensemble in terracotta represents the Transit of St. Bernard. It was built when Frei Sebastião de Sottomayor was the Abbot of the Monastery (1675–1678). The ensemble can be divided into two groups: at the lower level is a group of free-standing sculptures and another of high-relief figures inserted at the back of the altar. St. Bernard is shown in agony at the centre of the scene, while close to his feet Cistercian monks mourn his death. Close to St. Bernard’s head, the kneeling General Abbot and a group of musician angles glorify his death. At the top, surrounded by two musician-angels and cherubs, the Virgin welcomes the soul of St. Bernard with opened arms. The life-size sculptures are built in overlapping horizontal blocks.

The Monastery of Alcobaça was founded as a gift to St. Bernard of Clairvaux shortly before his death on an estate granted by King Afonso Henriques in 1153. The monastery became powerful due to donations throughout the centuries and contains several treasures, namely the Baroque reliquary Sanctuary and the Altarpiece of the Transit of St. Bernard.
keywords: Terracotta; sculpture; Our Lady of Assumption; Cistercian Order; Counter-Reformation
materials: Sanctuary: chased, polychrome and gilded wood and terracotta. Altarpiece Transit of St. Bernard: terracotta
tags: Sanctuary: chased, polychrome and gilded wood and terracotta. Altarpiece Transit of St. Bernard: terracotta

pt.name: *Santuário e Retábulo do Trânsito de São Bernardo*
description:
Fundado em 1153 sobre um terreno delimitado, conquistado aos Mouros e doado a São Bernardo de Claraval pelo Rei D. Afonso Henriques (primeiro rei de Portugal), o Mosteiro Cisterciense de Alcobaça é considerado um dos complexos monásticos medievais em melhor estado de conservação, na Europa, e um bastião da nacionalidade Portuguesa.  
*Santuário:* Integrada na Sacristia Nova, esta Capela de suprema beleza e espiritualidade, “O Espelho do Céu”, segundo Reinaldo dos Santos, começou a ser construída em 1670, durante o abaciado de Frei Constantino Sampaio (1669–1672).  
A sua planta é octogonal e o interior integralmente revestido de talha dourada. Recebe iluminação proveniente de um lanternim, aberto no tecto cupulado. Esta luz, coada e difusa, acentua ainda mais a ambiência feérica e teatral. O políptico barroco de talha dourada e policromada alberga hoje em dia oitenta e nove esculturas-relicário, recolhidas em nichos, distribuídos por seis níveis.  
*Retábulo do Trânsito de São Bernardo:* Grupo escultórico em barro cozido policromado e estofado, representando a morte de São Bernardo, e construído por encomenda do Abade Sebastião de Sottomayor (1675–1678). O grupo pode dividir-se em dois subgrupos, um inferior, de esculturas de vulto perfeito, e um outro, de esculturas em alto-relevo, fixas ao pano de fundo do altar. Ao centro, está São Bernardo, deitado e agonizante. Aos seus pés, encontram-se monges cistercienses. À cabeceira, acham-se o Dom Abade Geral, ajoelhado, e uma teoria de anjos músicos que glorificam a morte previsível. Por cima de São Bernardo e rodeada por anjos músicos e querubins que a adoram, aparece a Virgem, de braços estendidos, recebendo a alma junto a si. As esculturas são de tamanho natural e executadas em tacelos sobrepostos.

O Mosteiro de Alcobaça foi construído por S. Bernardo de Claraval num terreno doado por D. Afonso Henriques em 1153 à Ordem de Cister. Sendo um mosteiro poderoso devido a doações régias ao longo dos séculos, contém vários tesouros artísticos, entre os quais o *Santuário* *e o Retábulo do Trânsito de S. Bernardo*.
keywords: Escultura em terracota; Nossa Senhora da Imaculada Conceição; Ordem de Cister; Contra-Reforma.
materials: *Santuário*: estrutura em talha dourada e policromada; esculturas em terracota. *Retábulo do Trânsito de São Bernardo*: terracota.

en.name: *A Greek Mountaineer*
short_description: During the Ottoman occupation, Greek peasants who were dispossessed of their property often retreated to impregnable mountain regions, where they engaged in resistance against the Turks. These mountaineers, who both fascinated and frightened European travellers, were romanticised by artists and poets such as Lord Byron. The man depicted here clearly represents the type of mountaineer described by Byron. To emphasize his costume and his swift movement, he appears in full gear, the sleeves of his jacket falling freely to the back as if to underscore his impulsive gesture. Pistols and knives are tucked in his belt. His right hand rests on his musket; his left hand proudly touches the tip of his sword. Haag chose to place the figure in a grand mountainous landscape, complete with a ruined temple. This sacred monument may be identified as the temple of Apollo Epicurius in Arcadia in the central Peloponnese. This enhances the dignity of the figure, whose nobility and heroism are worthy of the principles of his legendary ancestors.
keywords: travels; Greece; Haag

en.name: *Nişan-ı Maarif* (Badge of Education)
short_description: The owner of this medallion was Dr. Mustafa Münif Pasha (1855-1937), who was the founder and director of the Turkish School of Pharmacy, Dentistry, Midwives and Nurses. He worked as an assistant in the anatomy department starting in 1881. Later, he gave classes on surgery. In 1886 he gave courses on midwifery. This medallion (*Nişan- Maarif*) was given to teachers who were successful in science and art. On the front of the medallion, on the left there are olive tree leaves enamelled in green and yellow while on the right we see oak leaves. Those two forms a crescent on top for the ribbon. On the lower part the leaves merge with a pink ribbon pattern. In the middle of the medallion there is a *tuğra* of Mehmed Reşad V. (1909–1918) on red enamelled background. Around the *tuğra* (monogram) there is an inscription that reads, “*ulûm ve fünûn ve sanayi'-i nefîse*” (sciences and knowledge and fine arts).
keywords: Medal; medical history of Turkey

en.name: Tree & Shrub Cartouche Carpet
description:
An 18th century north-west Iranian “tree-and-shrub-cartouche” pile carpet, with a multi-coloured centre-field containing more than fifteen small gardens, one in each of its cartouches. Each of the centre-field’s geometrical cartouches has a different coloured background including red, green, yellow, turquoise and dark blue gardens. The slightly distorted cartouches would have been originally eight-pointed star compartments. Each compartment holds a miniature garden with a variety of flowering shrubs and trees and a small pond or a stream at the foot of the main tree. The carpet is framed by a narrow ivory and dark blue border that contains a repeat arabesque motif.  
  
The multi-garden design of this carpet is inspired by earlier carpets of the “Wagner Garden” carpet type, which is also owned by the Burrell Collection. See carpet no. 9.2.
keywords: geometric compartment; cartouche; garden; tree motif; cypress; floral motif; shrub; water; river
materials: Wool warp and weft; wool pile

en.name: Parish Church of St. John of Nepomuk and former Jesuit Monastery, Székesfehérvár
names: Parish Church of St. John of Nepomuk and former Jesuit Monastery
description:
The church consists of a nave, three adjoining side chapels on both sides, and a sanctuary. Its façade is articulated by wall pillars and a tympanum; the two towers are decorated by windows and clocks. Above the front entrance, which is decorated with volutes, are wall pillars and mouldings; the date 1751 can be seen. The Jesuit coat of arms is placed above the wrought-iron gate.  
The Jesuit working brethren (*fratres operarii*) also participated in the painting of the church under the instruction of renowned masters of the Austrian Baroque movement. Caspar Franz Sambach from Breslau (Wrocław), later the head of the Academy of Fine Arts in Vienna (Vienna's Imperial and Royal Court Academy of Painters, Sculptors and Architecture), painted the fresco in the nave. One part of the fresco on the side of the sanctuary, depicts one of the central themes of the Hungarian Baroque, the so called *Patrona Hungariae* (King St. Stephen offers Hungary to the Virgin Mary). The section of the fresco on the side of the main entrance and the choir, illustrates allegories of Faith, Hope and Love. The painting on the sanctuary wall shows the Apotheosis of St. John of Nepomuk, and, according to legend, the benefactors of the construction, P. Antal Vanossi SJ and Mrs. Antal Amadé, are also represented. The sanctuary fresco depicts the Holy Trinity.  
Michelangelo Unterberger created the side altarpiece paintings, *St. Ignatius of Loyola*, and those of *St. James*, *St. Aloysius Gonzaga* and *St. Francis Xavier*. The *Guardian Angel*, *Holy Cross* and the Loreto Chapel were painted by Jesuit *fratres operarii*, Antal Werle and János F. Magis. On the side wall of the choir, a portrait of Ignác P. Stocker can be seen. The vestry is to the right of the sanctuary, and the Loreto Chapel on the left. The amazingly beautiful church furniture was also carved by Jesuit *fratres operarii* between 1749 and 1760, under the instruction of Bernát F. Baumgartner, an outstanding master of Hungarian Jesuit fretwork and wood carving (the woodwork and wooden decorations of the altars were made in 1757; the pews in 1760; the furniture of the refectory, which disappeared in the 19th century, in 1759; he also made the furniture of the monastery and the apothecary). Of the *fratres operarii*, János Pál Koller and Fülöp Kratz (wood carvers) and József Cordelli, a painter and wood carver who trained in a joiner's workshop and was later naturalised in Fehérvár, are worth particular mention. The Rococo oak furniture of the vestry was made by the Pauline monk János Hyngeller between 1764 and 1767.

The Jesuit Church and Monastery of Székesfehérvár, built between 1745 and 1756, is a marvellous example of the workmanship of the Jesuit artists, masters and “working brethren” (*fratres operarii*) in Hungary. The masterful wooden decorations, carved in the Jesuit joiner's workshop of Bernát Baumgartner, are an outstanding feature of the church interior. Besides the Jesuit Masters, the painter Caspar Franz Sambach also participated in the decoration of the church. The church is dedicated to St. John of Nepomuk, patron saint of the Jesuit order. An icon of obedience, St. John maintained the secrecy of confessions. His good reputation meant that he was popular in countries that were under Austrian Habsburg rule.
artist: Head of the Jesuit province in Austria, P. Antal Vanossi SJ (1688–1757); Mrs. Antal Amadé

Design: Paul Hartzinger; supervisor: Ignác P. Stocker SJ (1694–1761); wood carvers’ supervisor: Bernát F. Baumgartner SJ (1704–after 1773), wood carvers: János Pál Koller (1727–1774), Fülöp Kratz (1693–1764), Paul Hatzinger,  János Hyngeller (active 1764–1767), Károly (Karl) Bebó (1712–1779); painter/wood carver: József Cordelli; sculptor (side altars): Michelangelo Unterberger (1696–1758); painters: Caspar Franz Sambach, (1715–1795) Antal F. Werle SJ (1699–1762), János F. Magis SJ (1720–1758)
history:
Until the Ottoman rule, Fehérvár was the sacral centre of the Hungarian Kingdom: it served as a venue for coronations and a place of burial for Hungarian kings. The city was occupied by the Ottomans in 1543 and remained under their rule until 1688. After the occupation, the Jesuit order, which settled in Fehérvár in 1688, was the driving force behind the re-introduction of Christianity in the city. The Jesuits built their Church (dedicated to St. John of Nepomuk), Monastery and School on the site of the former Church of St. Jacob, which had been turned into a mosque by the Turks. Jesuit artists and the working brethren (*fratres operarii*) played an important role in the design, financing and completion of the church, towards which P. Antal Vanossi SJ, head of the Jesuit province in Austria, was a major benefactor.  
The Church and Monastery were designed by the architect Paul Hartzinger, a disciple of Martin (Athanasius) Wittwer, a Carmelite monk, who was also naturalised in Fehérvár. The patron of the construction was Ignác P. Stocker SJ. Building of the complex began in 1742 but the foundation stone of the church was not laid until 1745. In 1747, the decoration of the interior and exterior of the church began; the pulpit was completed in 1749. Construction work continued until the 1750s (main altar 1750; entrance gate 1751 and consecration of the church in 1756).  
Following dissolution of the Jesuit order, the buildings were used by the Pauline order between 1773 and 1786, and by the Cistercians from 1813 to 1950. After that the church fell under the control of the diocese, and the monastery became the centre of the King St. Stephen Museum.

Baumgartner SJ, Károly Bebo, János Pál Koller, Fülöp Kratz, János Magis SJ, Caspar Franz Sambach, Michelangelo Unterberger, Antal F. Werle SJ, József Cordelli, Paul Hatzinger, Martin (Athanasius) Wittwer, János Hyngeller, Mrs Antal Amadé; P. Antal Vanossi SJ, King St. Stephen Museum, Székesfehérvár, Stuhlweißenburg, Alba Regia

en.name: Hospital of San Miguel
description: The hospital was founded by doña Constancia Osorio; a fact that is verified by her will dated 1480. Although the building has been deteriorating since the beginning of the 20th century, it is still clear how the Chapel of la Magadelena follows the typology of the Islamic *qubbas* described in the Convent of Santa María del Valle, and how the brick arcades of both the chapel and infirmary are in the Mudéjar taste.

es.name: Hospital de San Miguel
description: Fue fundación de doña Constancia Osorio, según figura en su testamento, datado en 1480. Aunque el edificio se conserva en malas condiciones desde principios de siglo, se puede ver cómo la capilla dedicada a la Magdalena sigue la tipología de las *qubba*s islámicas descrita en el convento de Santa María del Valle, y las arquerías de ladrillo conforme al gusto mudéjar en la capilla y sala de enfermos.

en.name: City Walls
description: The first walls built after the Reconquest appear to date from the time of D. Afonso IV, and therefore from the first half of the 14th century, although what is visible today was clearly begun by D. Manuel I, whose architects designed a traditional system of high, thick *curtain walls* with wide battlements, divided by square towers that were reinforced at the corners and gateways. On the Ribeira side, the long front has two towers to defend the main gate of the Porta de São Gonçalo, and a *barbican* was built later on high ground at the far end. The wall facing south is quite impressive with its more modern bastions, undoubtedly built at a later phase.

ar.name: جزء من إفريز خشبي يحمل نقشاً بالخط الكوفي.
description: جزء من إفريز من الخشب محفور بأحرف بالخط الكوفي الكبير، وقد كان الاعتقاد سائداً عندما اقتنى المتحف هذه القطعة أنها من مصر الطولونية، وأن النقش هو: "بركة ويمن وسعادة وغبطة لصاحبه". ولكن، مع الفحص الدقيق، تبين أن الأحرف الموجودة لا تتطابق مع هذه القراءة، وعلى الرغم من أنه لم تتم قراءة الأحرف بعد، ولكن يبدو أنها كانت جزءاً من كتابة قرآنية.

تتميّز الكمية الضئيلة الباقية من الأعمال الخشبية المحفورة، بفن التمثيل النافر المُتقن، وحيوية الزخرف النقشي أو التصويري. أحياناً كانت الألواح النهائية، المُخصَّصة لإضفاء ثوب البهاء والجلال على الجدران الداخلية المعاصرة، تُطلى، وتُلمع، وتُعالج، لتمكينها من مقاومة النار.
holder: المتحف الملكي، المتحف الوطني في اسكتلندا NMS.
dates: أواخر القرن الثاني- الخامس/ التاسع- الحادي عشر.

en.name: Fragment (from a wooden frieze) with an inscription in kufic script.
description: A fragment of a wooden frieze inscribed with large *kufic* characters. When the NMS acquired this piece it was thought to have come from Tulunid Egypt and it was suggested at the time that the inscription read: ‘*baraka wa yumn wa sa’ada wa ghibt lisahibii’* (‘blessing and good fortune and happiness and joy to its owner’). However on closer inspection, the surviving lettering does not stand up to such a reading, and although the inscription has not yet been re-deciphered, it appears more likely that it originally formed part of a quotation from the Qur’an.

The little that survives of Fatimid wood carving is characterised by its intricate high relief technique and the vibrancy of its epigraphic or figurative decoration. Occasionally the final panels, which were meant to grace contemporary interiors, were painted, varnished and treated to be fire retardant.
dates: Hegira, late 2nd–5th century / late AD 9th–11th century.
keywords: Wood; kufic script; epigraphy

es.name: Fragmento de friso de madera con inscripción cúfica.
description: Fragmento de friso de madera con una inscripción en grandes caracteres cúficos. Cuando los Museos Nacionales de Escocia adquirieron esta pieza, se creía que procedía del Egipto tuluní y se propuso un texto para la inscripción: “Bendiciones y buena suerte y felicidad y alegría para su dueño”. Las letras conservadas, observadas con mayor detenimiento, indican que ese no es el texto de la inscripción. Se cree que se trata de una cita del Corán, aunque aún no ha sido descifrada.

Los pocos ejemplos de madera tallada de época fatimí que se conservan se caracterizan por sus intrincados altorrelieves y por la vivacidad de la epigrafía y los motivos figurativos. En ocasiones, los tableros que decoraban interiores se pintaban, barnizaban y trataban para resistir al fuego.
dates: Entre finales del sigo II y el siglo V de la Hégira / principios de siglo IX-siglo XI d. C.
keywords: madera; escritura cúfica; epigrafía

fr.name: Fragment de frise en bois à inscription coufique.
description: Fragment de frise en bois sculptée de grands caractères coufiques. Lors de son acquisition, cette pièce était supposée provenir d'Égypte toulounide, et l'on avait suggéré à l'époque que l'inscription signifiait : “bénédiction, bonne fortune, bonheur et joie à son propriétaire”. Une analyse plus approfondie montre que cette traduction ne correspond pas aux caractères. Même si la ligne n'a pas encore été déchiffrée, il est plus probable qu'elle reprend une citation du Coran.

Peu d’éléments fatimides en bois sculpté sont parvenus jusqu’à nous. Ils sont caractérisés par leur complexe technique en haut relief et la  vigueur de leur décoration épigraphique ou figurative. Parfois, les panneaux finis, dont le rôle était d’embellir des intérieurs de l’époque, étaient peints, vernis et traités afin de retarder la propagation des flammes.
dates: Fin IIe-Ve siècle de l’Hégire (fin IXe-XIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: bois ; coufique ; épigraphie

ar.name: خنجر
description: هذا الخنجر هو خنجر ديوان تركي يوضع على الصدر. وفي البلاط العثماني فإن الأسلحة التذكارية الفخمة كانت توضع من قبل أشخاص رفيعي المستوى في البلاط في اجتماعات المجلس التي تعقد بوجود السلطان. والصنعة الدقيقة تقول بأن الفنان الصانع هو فارسي. وفي عام 1874 قدّم السلاح للإمبراطور فرانتز جوزيف (1830 – 1916 ميلادي) من قبل الدكتور أوتوكار فرايهر فون شليشتا الكبير ، مدير الأكاديمية الشرقية ورئيس المترجمين في إنترن يونيتير في الباب العالي العثماني.
keywords: خنجر ، بلاد فارس

de.name: Krummdolch
description: Bei diesem Dolch handelt es sich um einen türkischen Diwandolch, der vorne an der Brust befestigt wurde. Prunkvolle Waffen dieser Art waren am osmanischen Hof ein standesgemäßes Accessoire höchster Würdenträger, das bei Ratssitzungen im Beisein des Sultans getragen wurde. Die Feinheit der Ausführung des vorliegenden Dolches lässt auf einen persischen Handwerker schließen. Die Waffe wurde 1874 von Dr. Ottokar Freiherr von Schlechta sen., dem Leiter der orientalischen Akademie und Hauptdolmetscher der Internuntiatur bei der Hohen Pforte, Kaiser Franz Josef I. (1830-1916) geschenkt.
keywords: Dolch; Persien
