en.name: Dagger
description: This dagger is a Turkish divan dagger worn on the chest. At the Ottoman court sumptuous ceremonial arms were worn by high-ranking courtiers at council meetings held in the presence of the Sultan. The delicate craftsmanship suggests a Persian artist. In 1874 the weapon was presented to Emperor Franz Josef I (AD 1830–1916) by Dr Ottokar Freiherr von Schlechta the elder, the director of the Oriental Academy and chief translator at the Internuntiature at the Ottoman Porte.
keywords: Ottoman arms; court life; metalwork; damascening; costumes; Persian influence; Habsburg; Ottoman-Austrian relations; diplomacy; weapon; dagger; Persia

ar.name: قطعة من قماش.
description: يظهر في القطعة قسمان متقابلان بلون أزرق داكن طُرزت عليهما كتابات بالخط الكوفي الأبيض، محاطة بأغصان وردية اللون ذات أزهار بيضاء، ويفصل بين القسمين المطرزين بالكتابة نطاق من ورود حمراء عليه أزهار بيضاء ذات أربع وريقات تمتد على جوانب الأغصان البنية المتموجة على أرضية خضراء. وهذه القطعة الصغيرة، التي هي بالأصل جزء من قطعة مطرزة أكبر، تمت مقارنتها مع كتابة اكتشفت على قطعة موجودة في متحف فكتوريا وألبرت في لندن، كانت قد صنعت بتكليف من الأمير الفاطمي المستنصر بالله، وتبين أنهما متشابهتان إلى حد التطابق تقريباً. وتنص الكتابة الكوفية المدونة على القسم الأعلى من القطعة الموجودة في برلين : "بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، لا إله إلا الله محمد رسول الله, علي وليّ الله". وهذا هو نص الشهادة الإسلامية. أما النص الموجود على القسم السفلي فيقول : " …مما أمر بعمله الوزير الأجلُّ…". وقد أتت تسمية القطعة المطرزة من اسم معمل التطريز الذي تطرز فيه الكتابة على النسيج. وكانت الأقمشة تصنع لأردية الخلفاء وعليّة القوم في معامل البلاط العامة. وكان الحكام يهدون هذه الأقمشة المطرزة بالكتابات إلى أشخاص رفيعي المقام، من مواطنيهم أو من الخارج، مقابل خدمات جلّى يقدمونها. وقد كانت هذه الأقمشة المطرزة بالكتابة توصف في مصادر العصور الوسيطة بأنها أغراض ثمينة. وتأتي غالبية هذه الأشرطة القماشية المطرزة من مصر، لأنها تبقى محفوظة بشكل جيد في المناخ الجاف، وحتى إذا ما طمرت في التربة الجافة تبقى محفوظة بشكل جيد أيضاً.

كانت الأقمشة القطنية المطرزة بخيوط الحرير تُنتج في ورشات البلاط بمصر الفاطمية، وكانت تعرف باسم الطراز بسبب النقوش التي كانت في الغالب تبين اسم المشغل والحاكم. درجت العادة على تقديمها في المناسبات الخاصة هدايا لأولئك الذين أدّوا خدمات مميزة للدولة.
keywords: رداء فاخر؛ قطعة مطرزة.
materials: قطن وحرير؛ متموجة الألوان، نص في النسيج.
partner: متحف الفن الإسلامي في متحف بيرغامون ، المتاحف الحكومية

de.name: Gewandfragment.
description: Das Fragment zeigt zwei einander zugekehrte dunkelblaue Friese mit weißen kufischen Inschriften, die von rosafarbenen Ranken mit weißen Blüten umgeben werden. Zwischen den Schriftfriesen verläuft ein Fries aus roten Rosetten mit weißen vierblättrigen Blüten der beidseitig von wellenförmig verlaufenden braunen Ranken auf grünem Grund eingefaßt wird. Dieses kleine Fragment eines ursprünglich viel größeren Tirazstreifens ist durch eine vergleichbare Inschrift von einem fast identischen Stück im Londoner Victoria und Albert Museum als Auftragsarbeit für den fatimidischen Fürsten Al-Mustansir billah zu erkennen. Der Text im oberen Fries im Kufi-Duktus auf dem Berliner Stück lautet „Im Namen Gottes des Barmherzigen und gütigen. Es gibt keinen Gott außer Gott. M(uhammad ist der Gesandte Gottes)“. Es ist also der Wortlaut des islamischen Glaubensbekenntnisses. Der Text im unteren Schriftfries lautet: …Das befahl herzustellen der Verzier, der große… Die Bezeichnung Tirazstreifen leitete sich aus der Bezeichnung der Tiraz-Werkstatt ab, in der die Stoffe mit den Inschriften, den Tirazen gewebt wurden. In den staatlichen Hofwerkstätten wurden die Gewandstoffe für den Kalifen und Hofbediensteten hergestellt. Die Stoffe mit Inschriften (Tiraze) wurden von den Herrschern an hochstehende lokale oder internationale Personen wegen besonderer Verdienste verschenkt. In den mittelalterlichen Quellen wurden sie als Wertobjekte beschrieben. Die meisten Tirazstreifen stammen aus Ägypten, da sich diese Textilien in dem sehr trockenen Klima und, falls sie vergraben wurden, in den sehr trockenen Böden besonders gut erhalten hatten.

Baumwollstoffe mit Silberstickereien wurden in höfischen Werkstätten im fatimidischen Ägypten produziert und hießen Tiraz, weil sie Beschriftungen trugen, die oft den Namen der Werkstätte und des Herrschers angaben. Zu speziellen Anlässen wurden sie Menschen überreicht, die sich in besonderer Weise um den Staat verdient gemacht hatten.
dates: Regierungszeit Al-Mustansir billah 427-487 H./ 1036-1094 n. Chr
keywords: Tirazstreifen; Ehrengewand
materials: Baumwolle und Seide; Schußrips, eingewebter Text.
partner: Museum für Islamische Kunst, Pergamon Museum

en.name: Fragment of a robe.
description:
This fragment shows two dark blue friezes facing each other, each featuring white *kufic* inscriptions surrounded by pink tendrils with white blossoms. A third frieze, composed of red rosettes with white four-petalled flowers, and framed on either side with waves of brown tendrils on a green background, sits between the two inscription friezes.  
This small fragment, which originally formed part of a much larger *tiraz* band, was identified as having been commissioned for the Fatimid ruler Al-Mustansir billah by comparing it with a similar inscription on a nearly identical piece in the Victoria and Albert Museum, London. The *kufic* text in the upper frieze on the Berlin fragment reads ‘In the name of God the merciful and good. There is no God other than God. M(ohammed is the envoy of God)’. This represents, therefore, the message of Islam. The text in the lower frieze reads ‘…this was commissioned by the vizier, the great…’. The term *tiraz* was derived from the name of the workshops where the cloths with the inscriptions, the *tiraz*, were woven. These robes of honour were manufactured for caliphs and high-ranking nobles in the workshops of the royal court. The *tiraz* were given to local or foreign high-ranking persons as a reward for their services. Medieval sources referred to them as valuable objects. The majority of *tiraz* bands come from Egypt, as these fabrics were preserved very well in the very dry climate and, if buried, the extremely dry earth.

Cotton textiles with silk embroidery were produced in court workshops in Fatimid Egypt and were called *tiraz* because of the inscriptions which often gave the name of the workshop and the ruler. On special occasions they were presented to people who had rendered services to the state.
holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum
keywords: Tiraz fabric; robe; kufic; royal workshop; royal manufacture; Fatimid textiles; geometric patterns
materials: Cotton and silk, weft rep, woven-in text.
tags: Cotton and silk, weft rep, woven-in text.
partner: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

es.name: Fragmento de vestidura.
description:
Fragmento textil decorado con dos franjas opuestas con inscripciones cúficas en color blanco sobre fondo azul oscuro y rodeadas de zarcillos rosa con flores blancas. Están separadas por una tercera franja con rosetas rojas y flores blancas de cuatro pétalos, enmarcadas con ondulados tallos marrones sobre fondo verde.  
Este pequeño fragmento formaba parte de un *tiraz* de mayor tamaño encargado por el califa fatimí al-Mustansir Billah. Para su identificación, se comparó con la inscripción de una pieza muy similar conservada en el Museo Victoria & Albert. El texto superior del tejido de Berlín dice: “En el nombre de Dios misericordioso y bueno. No hay más dios que Dios. M\[uhammad es su enviado\]”, que representa el mensaje del Islam. El texto de la franja inferior reza: “...este es un encargo del visir, el grande...”.  
El término *tiraz* deriva del nombre de los talleres donde se tejían estas telas con inscripciones. Los talleres de la corte producían estos ropajes honoríficos para los califas y la alta nobleza, y también se recompensaba con ellos a altos personajes locales o extranjeros por sus servicios. Fuentes medievales se refieren a ellos como objetos valiosos. La mayoría de las bandas de *tiraz* proceden de Egipto, donde el clima muy seco, o la tierra seca en caso de que el dueño fuera enterrado con ellas, ha hecho que se conserven.

Los talleres de la corte fatimí producían telas de algodón con bordados en seda, denominadas *tiraz* por as inscripciones con el nombre del taller y del dueño. En ciertas ocasiones, se regalaban a personas que hubieran prestado algún servicio al Estado.
holder: Museo de Arte Islámico del Museo Pergamon
dates: En tiempos del califa al-Mustansir Billah (427–487 de la Hégira / 1036–1094 d.C.).
keywords: tejido tiraz; vestido de ceremonia
materials: Algodón y seda; reps, texto bordado.
partner: Museo de Arte Islámico en el Museo de Pérgamo, Museos Estatales

fr.name: Fragment de vêtement.
description: Ce fragment présente deux frises opposées, portant en blanc sur fond bleu nuit des inscriptions coufiques, dans un entourage de rinceaux roses à fleurs blanches. Entre ces deux frises calligraphiées court une autre frise agrémentée de rosettes rouges à quatre pétales dans un entourage de rinceaux en vagues brunes sur fond vert. Ce petit fragment d'une bande de *tiraz*, beaucoup plus importante à l'origine, est à rapprocher, à cause de l'inscription presque similaire, d'un exemplaire conservé au Victoria and Albert Museum de Londres, dont le commanditaire est le prince fatimide al-Moustansir. Le texte en ductus coufique porté par la frise supérieure sur cet exemplaire de Berlin dit : “Au nom de Dieu, le Clément, le Miséricordieux. Il n'y a d'autre Dieu que le Dieu. M(ahomet) est son Prophète.” Il s'agit donc de la profession de foi islamique. Sur la frise inférieure, on lit : “Ceci a été fait sur ordre du vizir, le Très Grand.” L'appellation “bande de *tiraz*” vient des ateliers où étaient tissées les étoffes portant des inscriptions (*tiraz*). Dans les ateliers de la cour, elles étaient fabriquées pour le calife et les dignitaires, elles étaient en outre offertes par les princes à des personnalités locales ou étrangères en récompense de leurs services. Les sources médiévales les décrivent comme des objets précieux. Les bandes de *tiraz* proviennent pour la plupart d'Égypte, le climat très sec y ayant permis une bonne conservation, même en cas d'enfouissement.

Des tissus de coton brodés de soie étaient réalisés dans les ateliers de la cour dans l'Égypte fatimide et étaient appelés *tiraz* en raison des inscriptions qui donnaient souvent le nom de l'atelier et du souverain. Lors d'occasions spéciales, ils étaient offerts à des personnes qui avaient rendu des services à l'État.
dates: Règne de al-Moustansir Billah, 427-487 de l’Hégire / 1036-1094 J.-C.
materials: Coton et soie, reps, texte tissé.
tags: Coton et soie, reps, texte tissé.
partner: Musée d’art islamique du Pergamon Museum (Museum für Islamische Kunst)

en.name: *Ensemble d’époque*: Bedroom
description: Installed in the east wing facing the Buxo Garden is a re-creation of an 18th-century bedroom. It is worth mentioning in particular the *azulejos* that line the walls depicting rural themes, romantic scenes and chinoiseries most of which date to 1746.
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: *Ensemble d’époque*: quarto de dormir
description: Instalado na ala nascente do Palácio, dando para o jardim do buxo, encontra-se uma recriação do ambiente palaciano setecentista, com móveis da época. Destaque para o revestimento de azulejos com temas campestres, cenas galantes, *chinoiseries*, na sua maioria datados de 1746.

ar.name: رداء قداس لكاهن ( رداء كبير لرجل دين كاثوليكي ) من قماش حريري عثماني ذو حدود منسوجة أوربية
description: كان بورصة مركزا مهما لتجارة الحرير الإيراني وتحولت إلى مركز متقدم لإنتاج  الأقمشة الحريرية وبسبب هذا فإنها لم تكن تزود البلاط العثماني فقط ولكن الحرير من بورصة كان بضاعة تصدير مرغوبة لأوربا كما يظهر بواسطة الرداء. وفي نفس الوقت فإن الحرير الإيطالي كان مطلوبا جدا في الإمبراطورية العثمانية وإحدى نتائج هذا التبادل الواسع يرى في التأثير المتبادل للأشكال بحيث أن التفاصيل الفنية المتكررة هي المميزات الوحيدة التي تخبرنا أين تم حياكة الحرير ، في إيطاليا أو في الإمبراطورية العثمانية.
dates: الربع الثالث من القرن السادس عشر
materials: حرير ، صفائح ذهب وفضة ، كتان ، لامباس بروشيه ، مفرغ / لانسيه
tags: حرير ، صفائح ذهب وفضة ، كتان ، لامباس بروشيه ، مفرغ / لانسيه
partner: المتحف التمساوي للفنون التطبيقية / الفنون المعاصرة

de.name: Kasel (Messgewand für den katholischen Ritus) aus osmanischem Seidengewebe mit europäischen Webborten
description: Bursa war ein wichtiger Umschlagplatz für iranische Seide und entwickelte sich zu einem bedeutenden Produktionszentrum von Seidenstoffen. Als solches versorgte es nicht nur den osmanischen Hof; Seiden aus Bursa waren gefragtes Exportgut für Europa, wie diese Kasel zeigt. Gleichzeitig waren italienische Seiden im osmanischen Reich sehr begehrt. In der Folge dieses intensiven Austauschs kam es zur gegenseitigen Beeinflussung von Motiven, so dass man oft nur an technischen Details erkennen kann wo der Seidenstoff gewebt wurde, in Italien oder dem osmanischen Reich.
holder: MAK – Österreichisches Museum für angewandte Kunst / Gegenwartskunst
materials: Seide, Gold- und Silberlahn, Leinen; Lampas broschiert, lanciert
partner: MAK – Österreichisches Museum für angewandte Kunst

en.name: Chasuble (Mass vestment for the Catholic liturgy) of Ottoman silk fabric with European woven borders
description: Bursa was an important hub of trade for Iranian silk and developed into a leading centre for the production of silk fabrics. As such, it did not only purvey to the Ottoman Court; silks from Bursa were coveted export goods for Europe, as is shown by this chasuble. At the same time, Italian silks were very much in demand in the Ottoman Empire. One consequence of this intensive exchange is seen in a reciprocal influencing of motifs, so that frequently technical details are the only characteristics that tell us where the silk fabric was woven, in Italy or in the Ottoman Empire.
type: Liturgical garment of Ottoman silk textile, silk, velvet, lampas, lance
keywords: Ottoman textile; trade; Floral motifs; liturgical vestment
materials: Silk, gold and silver lamella, linen; Lampas broché, lancé
tags: Silk, gold and silver lamella, linen
partner: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

en.name: Multiple-niche prayer kilim (*saf*)
description: The multiple-niche prayer carpets, called *saf* (from the Arabic word for “row”), are sometimes improperly referred to as “family” prayer rugs. They were used in mosques, their particular design allowing several people to pray one next to the other. Here, the uneven colour areas in the *mihrab* field, the somewhat irregular shape of the arches, and the stylised vegetal motifs are indicative of its tribal, probably Kurdish, provenance. Unlike most large Anatolian kilims, made of two narrow bands, this one is made of only one piece. The Arabic inscriptions and the fact that the carpet was dated make it all the more valuable.
holder: The National Museum of Art of Romania
keywords: saf; Kurdish
partner: The National Museum of Art of Romania

en.name: Colonial style building
short_description: 114 Rue de Yougoslavie, the former French Embassy and General Residence previously known as the Disegni building, was designed by the famous architect Auguste Peters, who remains a leading figure of eclecticism. The finely carved balconies, ribbed stone corbels, delicate Venetian style mouldings, overhanging arches and columned galleries all add to the building's majestic character. Auguste Peters was a great master of eclecticism in the first decade of the 20th century, and decorative elements like these characterise his work.
history: In Tunis, the capital of the Protectorate imposed by France on Tunisia in 1881, the European quarter built itself right next to the old Arab medina. A new kind of home - the investment property - soon appeared, and the term balas (from the Italian *palazzo*) became widespread. These two or three-storey housing blocks greatly affected the city's urban landscape by introducing many different architectural styles as well as new architects, designers and builders with from different backgrounds. The 19th century was the century of eclecticism in Tunisia (both neo-classical and neo-baroque), whereas the 20th century was most marked by the influence of Art Nouveau.
keywords: Art Nouveau; colonial style; eclecticism; Neo-Baroque
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Immeuble de style colonial
history: A Tunis, capitale du protectorat imposé par la France à la Tunisie en 1881, la ville européenne s’édifia à côté de l’ancienne médina arabe. Une nouvelle forme d’habitation fit son apparition : l’immeuble de rapport. Le *balas* dérivé de l’italien *palazzo* passa dans le langage courant. Cette unité de logement à deux et trois étages changea la structure urbaine avec divers styles architecturaux, du fait de la diversité des origines des architectes, des artisans et des entrepreneurs. De 1880 à 1900, ce fut l’époque de l’éclectisme en Tunisie (néo-classique ou néo-baroque) tandis que l’Art nouveau marqua les premières décennies du XXe siècle.
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

en.name: *Suq al-Hamidiyya, Damascus*
names: Covered market constructed in the shape of an arcade turning it to the worldwide longest arcade of the fin de siecle
short_description: The Suq al-Hamidiyya, built in 1886 and 1894, is by far the biggest and most famous suq in Damascus. This bazaar street also links the two most important historic buildings, the Umayyad Mosque and the Citadel. It was built along its western section by incorporating earlier structures, whereas the eastern part of the street was a completely new construction cutting through the existing buildings. The commercial thoroughfare is 450 metres long and 8.70 to 9.90 metres wide, its enormous size and the high standard of its execution accentuate new design principles. So in various respects, this suq is a very interesting example of structural change in a traditional commercial centre.
holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
partner: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

ar.name: ابزيم خنجر
description: يمكن تعريف مصطلح ""أرابيسك"" بطريقتين ضمن سياق التصميم الإسلامي؛ فالأرابيسك كعنصر زخرفي يتكون من جذع طويل، تتفرع منه أوراق منفصلة كفية الشكل، ومن جهة أخرى، وبصورة أكبر، تستخدم كلمة ""أرابيسك"" للإشارة إلى مجموعة كاملة، ومكررة من التصاميم المتماثلة، والمتشابهة في النسق، التي تستوحى من الأزهار، وأوراق النباتات، والحيوانات؛ لتضفي بعدا جماليا يتسق مع التنظيم المثالي لواقع الطبيعة.وتستخدم أنماط ""الأرابيسك"" بشكل واسع في الصناعات الحرفية العُمانية؛ حيث ترى في الصناعات الخشبية، والجصية، والمعدنية؛ وقد يستعان بها لتغطية الأسطح بشكل كامل، أو بأشكال محددة ضمن إطار هندسي دقيق.
dates: القرن الرابع عشر الهجري / القرن العشرين الميلادي
keywords: إبزيم ، مجوهرات ، أرابيسك ، مشغولة معدنية

en.name: *Ibzim* (Buckle) of Kanjar
description: The term, "Arabesque" can be defined in two ways within the context of Islamic design. The Arabesque as a specific decorative element consists of a continuous branching stem with split palmate leaves. In a larger sense, the word Arabesque is used to refer to an entire range of designs based on stylised floral, foliar and animal motifs, the aesthetics of which are derived from the imposition of order on the natural world. This buckle is one example of the Arabesque patterns used extensively in traditional Omani woodwork, plasterwork and metalwork as a means of covering entire surfaces or precise areas within a defined geometric framework.
keywords: Buckle; Jewellery; Arabesque; Metalwork

en.name: The High Altar
description: Made of Carrara marble with polychrome incrustations, in its dimensions the high altar dominates the other six altars placed in six radial chapels. Extending towards the vault of the chapel with its high central attic “inhabited” with small angels and a central figure of the Holy Father surrounded by rounded clouds, its slanted side “wings” with side passages in the lower part, fills the whole of the sanctuary forming a concave. There is a central wooden Gothic crucifix and in the side-niches are sculptures of St. Vitus and St. Modest.

en.name: A photograph of the Arms Factory in Fez (*Dar al-makina*)
description: A photograph depicting workers at the Arms Factory in Fez.
holder: The Inspection of the Historic Monuments
keywords: Industrialisation; industrialists; Italians in Morocco; social changes; work; labour; workers; machine; technical innovation; urban life; urban space; urbanisation; changes in warfare; protectorate; weapons; arms; armours; firearms; market
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate for Cultural Heritage

en.name: Dhu’l-Nun Prays for Rain for the Egyptians
names: Folio from the Manuscript of Kulliyat (Collected Works) of Sa`di
description: This is the seventh painting to appear in the Bustan, and it is marked as page 124 in the manuscript. It represents the story of Dhu’l-Nun, an Egyptian mystic who died in 861 CE.
keywords: folio; painting; work-on-paper; works-on-paper; Sa‘di; Sadi; Bustan; Persian; Iran; India; Mughal; water; rain; pray; Egyptian; mystic
materials: opaque watercolour, ink, and gold on paper
tags: Opaque watercolour, ink, and gold on paper

en.name: Stengelglas
description: The animal designs covering the cylindrical bowl of this glass are typical for the painter L. H. Jungnickel, as he is well known for his animal print cycles. This particular example features monkeys. Originally, the confined chessboard pattern was supposed to be used for the glass’s stem and foot as well. This stemware was shown at the Exhibition of Works from the Austrian Arts Industry in the Museum of Art and Industry in AD 1911/12 along with Josef Hoffmann´s first Bronzite decorated glasses. It also was one of the objects presented at the Kölner Werkbundausstellung (exhibition of Deutscher Werkbund in Cologne) in AD 1914. For a similarly designed glass with a round bowl also exhibited AD 1911/12, Jungnickel chose different animals set in medallions. Subsequently these designs were used to decorate a jardinière.
artist: Jungnickel, Ludwig Heinrich (design);  Böhmische Manufaktur (manufacturer);  J. & L. Lobmeyr (client / customer)
partner: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

en.name: Kilim, *Smyrna pattern*
description: *Smyrna pattern* (*smirjanska šara*) is a very popular Pirot kilim pattern. The horizontal division of kilim surface through the use of rectangular boxes (*kuveri*) is characteristic for this pattern. The boxes contain rows of rhomboid ornaments, with *bibice* ornaments inside the shape and hooks on the outer borders. The borders of the boxes are decorated with *octopus* (*oktapod*) ornament, flanked with feathers. Between the boxes runs a frieze composed of *glasses* (*očila*) motif. A wide border (*ploča*) contains alternately *turtle* (*kornjača*) and *čurlinjak* ornaments. The colours used are: red, white, blue, green, brown and orange.
keywords: Pirot; Şarköy; kilim; wool; weave

en.name: The Iwan House
description: The house is built around a vestibule, which is flanked on two sides by symmetrical living spaces and open on one end with a tall archway called an *iwan*, or an *'aqd* in the local dialect. It is after this archway that the vestibule is named. The *iwan* archway is usually north facing, for climactic reasons, and built in a broken or curved shape. The vestibule is sometimes T-shaped, with arms at the back leading to two adjacent rooms, or can simply be a wider room, thus becoming more of a central hall.
history: The architecture of the *iwan* was well suited to both its domestic and economic functions. When opened, it allowed the family to work and sit outside whilst remaining protected from the worst of the winter winds and summer sun. It also facilitated the movement of domestic animals, and the storage of produce and agricultural equipment. The house is built with *ramleh* of stone and limestone-marl from Ashrafiyyeh. Although mud was traditionally used, the walls nowadays are usually covered with reinforced concrete.
keywords: Iwan; Architecture; Arc; Bow; Material; Typology

en.name: Loom weight
description: Early loom weights found in the ancient city of Assoss, today known as Behramkale, a small historically rich town in the Ayvacık district of the Çanakkale Province, Turkey. These provide evidence the textile industry existed in the region since the Chalcolithic Period and the Bronze Age. Loom weights prevented tangling by weighting to give tension on individual yarns to enable weaving.

en.name: Bowl with stand
short_description: This bowl with a bulging rim sits on a stand. The decoration is made of two layers of concentric patterns around a central circle, filled with winged motifs. These green and brown patterns are painted on a yellow background. Although this kind of bowl is usually used to serve couscous, in the town Nabeul, and particularly for the occasion of Islamic New Year, each child is presented with a *methred* bowl, filled with golden couscous, dried fruit, dates, a hard-boiled egg and sweets. This all surrounds a statuette made of sugar, moulded and coloured to resemble an animal (such as a rooster or a gazelle) or a figure, like a doll or cavalier.
holder: Musée de la Céramique Sidi Kacem Jelizi
keywords: Floral motifs; winged motifs; cermaics from Nabeul
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Coupe à pied
short_description: Il s’agit d’un plat dont le bord est évasé avec un large pied. Le décor présente deux registres concentriques à motifs floraux avec un cercle central meublé de plusieurs motifs ailés. Ces motifs en vert et brun se détachent d’un fond jaune. Ce plat est essentiellement destiné à servir le couscous. Dans la ville de Nabeul et en particulier le jour de l’an de l’Hégire, chaque enfant reçoit son *methred* avec du couscous doré et des fruits secs, des dattes, un œuf dur, des bonbons. Il est garni au centre d’une statuette de sucre moulée et colorée représentant des animaux (coq, gazelle) ou des personnages tels que la poupée et le cavalier.
holder: Musée de la Céramique Sidi Kacem Jelizi
keywords: Motifs floraux; Motifs ailés; Céramique de Nabeul
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

en.name: Textile fragment
description: This fragment is an exceptional example of Buyid dynasty (945–1055) textiles from both a historical and an aesthetic viewpoint. The frieze is adorned with two-headed eagles carrying a winged creature and with stylized trees. The light-brown motifs are embellished with epigraphs that are particularly noticeable on the tops of the trees and on the band bordering the textile’s upper edge. The fragment’s style and iconography are similar to those of a group of four textiles discovered in the ancient necropolis of Nakhara Khanah, near Rayy. It remains to be determined whether this textile was designed to serve as a shroud or was selected from the belongings of the deceased.
keywords: Persian textile; Buyid art; silks; epigraphs; Islamic textile
partner: The Montreal Museum of Fine Arts

fr.name: Fragment de textile
description: D’un point de vue historique et esthétique, ce fragment est un exemple remarquable des textiles de la dynastie des Bouyides (945–1055). La frise est ornée d’aigles bicéphales portant une créature ailée et d’arbres stylisés. Les motifs marron clair sont rehaussés d’épigraphes, qui se remarquent notamment sur la cime des arbres et sur la bande qui borde le haut du textile. Le style et l’iconographie de ce fragment l’apparentent à un groupe de quatre textiles mis au jour dans la nécropole ancienne de Nakhara Khana près de Rayy. Il reste à déterminer si le textile a été conçu comme un linceul ou s’il a été choisi parmi les biens du défunt.
keywords: Textile perse ; art bouyide, soieries ; épigraphes ; textile islamique

en.name: *A Greek lady of Smyrna*
short_description: The picture probably depicts a bride before being bedecked. Her outfit-one of the two customary types of urban bridal costume during the Ottoman period- consists of one or two pairs of pantaloons, a diaphanous selvedged chemise and a dress with tightly buttoned long sleeves and a sash worn low on the hips. Her overcoat is trimmed with fur, has wide pointed sleeves and the dress appears to have been hitched up, revealing the bottom of the pantaloons. Among the various testimonies bequeathed to us by the foreign artist-travelers who visited Greece in the seventeenth, eighteenth, and nineteenth centuries, the depictions of costumes are particularly important. The imaginative combination of the various garments and accessories that make up the Greek costume and the wealth of jewellery fascinated foreign travellers, who recorded them pictorially, often with a dubitable degree of accuracy.
keywords: travels; Athens

en.name: *Jarrita* vase with two handles
description: This drinking vase has a pear-shaped body and two rounded handles that join a short neck that widens toward the top; it rests on a low base. The decoration, painted in dark blue and a beautiful shade of bronze-gold on the ivory opaque glaze, is placed symmetrically on both sides of the handles. A frieze of pseudo-epigraphy whose drawing seems to recall the word *al-'afiya* (good health)... is drawn in blue on the neck over a glossy background of a wormlike pattern. On the body, eight-lobed medallions in bronze-gold have a blue pseudo-epigraphic pattern in the centre. On each side of the handles is a scalloped almond composition. Directly below each handle is another pseudo-epigraphic motif against a glossy background. A series of horizontal lines rings the lower part of the body. The lustre decoration with metallic reflections is a process peculiar to the arts of Islam. The technique is seen as early as the eighth century on fragments of Egyptian glasses; it was later applied to ceramics, beginning in the ninth century in Mesopotamia under the reign of the Abbasids. It is a decoration painted on a glazed piece that has undergone a first firing. The lustre consists of a mixture of copper and silver oxides to which are added sulphur and red ochre, and a binder to permit a brushed application. A second firing in an oxygen-poor atmosphere results in the incorporation of the oxide particles, now reduced to a metallic state in the softened glaze. Quite characteristic effects are produced when the pieces are observed in light. The secrets of this complex and sometimes unpredictable technique were jealously guarded in pottery workshops. Nevertheless, the process spread to both the East and the Muslim West, and in Spain its development was encouraged by the Nasrid rulers, especially in Malaga. Since the Reconquest, the craze for Hispano-Moorish ceramics (*loza dorada*), continues, since production is exported to Muslim countries and Christian Europe. Cobalt blue and brown lustre, combined in bold compositions, as here, give a characteristic identity to a process that is still used, for example in Manises (in Valencia).
holder: Museum of the Arab World Institute
dates: Hegira last quarter of 8th century or beginning 9th century / AD end of 14th or beginning of 15th century
partner: Museum of the Arab World Institute

fr.name: Vase à deux anses *jarrita*
description:
Ce vase à boire possède une panse piriforme et deux anses arrondies qui rejoignent un col tronconique évasé vers le haut ; il repose sur une courte base également tronconique. Le décor, peint en bleu foncé et dans une belle teinte de lustre mordoré sur la glaçure opaque de couleur ivoire, est posé d’une manière symétrique de part et d’autre des anses. Une frise de pseudo-épigraphie dont le dessin semble rappeler le mot *al-‘afiya* ("bonne santé") est tracée en bleu sur le col, sur un fond de vermicules lustrés. Sur la panse, un médaillon à huit lobes peint au lustre est occupé en son centre par un motif pseudo-épigraphique en bleu avec, de chaque côté des anses, une composition en amande festonnée. Dans l’axe des anses, un autre motif pseudo-épigraphique apparaît en réserve sur le fond lustré. Une suite de lignes horizontales occupe la partie inférieure de la panse.  
Le décor de lustre à reflets métalliques est un procédé propre aux arts de l’Islam. La technique apparaît dès le VIIIe siècle J.-C. sur des fragments de verres égyptiens ; on la rencontre ensuite appliquée sur la céramique à partir du IXe siècle J.-C. en Mésopotamie sous le règne des Abbassides. Il s’agit d’un décor peint sur une pièce couverte d’une glaçure ayant déjà subi une première cuisson. Le lustre se compose d’un mélange d’oxydes de cuivre et d’argent auxquels sont ajoutés du soufre et de l’ocre rouge ainsi qu’un liant qui permet l’emploi du pinceau. Une deuxième cuisson dans une atmosphère pauvre en oxygène a pour résultat d’incorporer les particules d’oxydes réduites à l’état métallique dans la glaçure amollie. Sous l’effet de la lumière naissent des effets tout à fait caractéristiques. Les secrets de cette technique complexe et aux résultats parfois aléatoires étaient jalousement gardés dans les ateliers de potiers qui la pratiquaient. Néanmoins, le procédé se diffusa tant vers l’Orient que l’Occident musulman et, en Espagne, son développement fut encouragé par les souverains nasrides, notamment à Malaga. Après la Reconquête, l’engouement pour la céramique "hispano-mauresque", la *loza dorada*, se poursuit puisque la production est exportée tant vers les pays musulmans que l’Europe chrétienne. Le bleu de cobalt et le lustre brun associés dans des compositions vigoureuses, comme sur cette pièce, donnent une forte identité à cette production qui se perpétue encore de nos jours, par exemple à Manises.
holder: Musée de l'Institut du monde arabe
dates: Fin du VIIIe ou début du IXe siècle de l'Hégire / fin du XIVe ou début du XVe siècle J.-C.

en.name: Beaker
description: This beaker is of conical form with a narrow base extending to a wide opening. Its size and shape suggest that it was a nesting beaker, one of a collection of three other similar examples. The base includes the addition of a thin ring added to provide more stability. This technical feature confirms the beaker’s slightly later production during the second half of the seventh century AH / thirteenth century AD. The beaker is decorated with a central frieze comprised of seated figures interspersed with medallions and flanked by two fine horizontal bands; one with an Arabic calligraphic inscription and the other with a stylized scroll motif. The inscription reads, “al'-izz li-mawlana al-sultan al-malik al-'amil .... al-murabit, al-muthagir, al-mu'ayyad al-muzaffar" (Glory to our Lord, the Sultan, the King, the Diligent, the Defender, the Protector of Frontiers, the One helped [by God], the Triumphant). Benedictory inscriptions such as these naming an unspecified ruler appear frequently on Mamluk glassware. The seated figures – most probably musicians –represent a common decorative feature found on Mamluk glass. Forming part of a visual language known as the "princely cycle", such figures were intended to illustrate a courtly pastime likely enjoyed by a ruler or emir.
dates: AH late 7th century / AD late 13th century
keywords: Glass; Beaker; Free-blown; Enamelled; Mamluk
materials: Glass; free-blown with tooled and enamelled decoration
tags: free-blown with tooled and enamelled decoration

en.name: Grindstone
short_description: The stone grinder was used to pulverise colours or cosmetics. It represents an important relic for the history of the foundation of the Pigorini Museum. Its label, signed by Giglioli, attests that the object was discovered in Thebes by Ernesto Schiaparelli in January 1892 and then donated by him to Giglioli three months later. The grinder cannot be dated as its origins are unknown. As a result of the excavations by W. Petrie and J. De Morgan, who documented the existence of an era preceding the First dynasty, Luigi Pigorini decided to enlarge the Egyptian archaeological collection in the "Museo Preistorico Etnografico e Kircheriano" which he directed at the time. In 1878 he began to acquire important groups, but the main body of the collection was donated by David Randall-MacIver in 1901, from the excavations he carried out on the behalf of the Egypt Exploration Fund in the town of el-Amrah, Upper Egypt. In 1905 Ernesto Schiaparelli, director of the Egyptian Museum in Turin, offered for purchase the excavation of Hammamiye by the Italian Archaeological Mission in Egypt. The last main acquisition took place in 1913 when the Egyptian objects from Enrico Hillyer Giglioli’s collection entered the museum collection.
holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
keywords: Egyptomania; Gaetano Rosellini; university; collector; photograph; anthropology; palaeoethnology; material culture; Florence; Pisa; Egyptology; Nubia; languages; hieroglyph; William Matthew Flinders Petrie; Jacques de Morgan; David Randall-MacIver
partner: MIBACT | National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”

en.name: *Pentecost*
description:
Joseph Ignaz Mildorfer was born into a well-known Tyrolese painter-family and moved at an early date to the imperial city of Vienna to earn his living as did many of his contemporaries from Tyrol. Between 1740 and 1742 he studied at the Academy of Fine Arts in Vienna where, in 1742, he won a competition and in 1751, following the example of his fellow painter, Paul Troger also from Tyrol, he became an academic professor. As a fresco and altarpiece painter, Mildorfer won fame and important commissions in Austria, Bohemia, Moravia and Hungary (Pápa, Sárvár, Fertőd, Holics (Holič) and Máriavölgy (Marianka). His skilfully executed early battle scenes bear witness to an almost unknown chapter in his oeuvre.  
Traditionally, the high altar painting in the Holy Spirit Church in Sopron along with the sketch made for it, were attributed to István Dorffmaister who was a graduate of the Academy of Fine Arts in Vienna and a resident of Sopron from 1782. However, recently, it has become clear that the execution of the high altar painting and the Pietà side-altarpiece are earlier: appearing to be the same age as the structure of the high altar, which together with its plastic decoration, dates to around 1750. The composition of the *Pentecost* altarpiece – the type of figures represented and their formation – are very close to the *Assumption* fresco painted by Mildorfer in the chapel of Castle Milotice in Moravia in the 1750s. Here similar character types swing into ecstasy; the same bearded characters, the use of very strong foreshortening close to caricature, and disproportioned, over-sized hands and feet. The strong light streaming into the picture from the dove of the Holy Spirit almost brightens the whole picture space: the figures of the apostles appearing before it almost as silhouettes.  
The Sopron altarpiece, along with the excellent *bozzetto* (sketch) both of which are attributed to Mildorfer, belong to a group of early Hungarian works from the generation of Viennese painters from the Paul Troger school.

Recently attributed to the excellent Tyrolese painter, Joseph Ignaz Mildorfer, the high altarpiece in Sopron and its expressive *bozzetto* (sketch) belong to a group of early Hungarian works from the generation of Viennese painters from the Paul Troger school. Mildorfer was a master of several frescoes in Hungary (Pápa, Sárvár, Fertőd, Holics (Holič) and Máriavölgy (Marianka).
keywords: Altarpiece; religious object; Christian themes; bozzetto; zoomorphic imagery; Gács; Ödenburg

en.name: Turkish woman
short_description: The Zangaki brothers were a pair of photographers working in Egypt who sold "Orientalist" photos to Western tourists, allowing them to immortalise their trip to the "Orient". This photograph shows a young Turkish woman.

fr.name: Femme turque
short_description: Les frères Zangaki, photographes grecs installés en Égypte, proposent des photographies aux touristes occidentaux pour immortaliser leurs voyages en Orient. Ici une jeune femme turque.

de.name: Ibn-Khairun-Moschee oder Moschee der Drei Tore

en.name: Mosque of the Three Doors
names: Ibn Khayrun Mosque, or Mosque of the Three Gates
description: Although not open to visitors, a visit to this monument is recommended as its main feature of interest lies in its facade. In fact, the Ibn Khayrun Mosque, otherwise called the Mosque of the Three Gates, possesses the oldest sculpted and decorated facade in Islamic art to survive, and is a veritable inventory of the Kairouanese decorative repertoire of the Aghlabid period. The use of soft sculpted stone has conferred a majestic aura to the entire appearance. The facade is composed along the lines of axial symmetry, possessing three gates, the largest of which stands in the middle. Framed by panels of floral and geometric motifs, composed of five or three-lobed leaves, open or folded, it is surmounted by *kufic* writing attributing its foundation to Mohamed Ibn Khayrun (252/866). The mosque has a modest look. It consists of three naves parallel to the wall of the *qibla*. Each of the two columns that support the ceiling is surmounted by semi-circular arches. In the north-east corner stands a minaret that was added during the Hafsid era as stated in the last line of the *kufic* inscription which bares witness to the renovation of the entire oratory in 843/1440. Like all Kairouanese minarets, it has a rectangular base, and is adorned with twin bays framed in *faience* tiles, indicating a clear Andalusian influence.

es.name: Mezquita Ibn Jayrun o de las Tres Puertas
description:
La mezquita Ibn Jayrun, también llamada Mezquita de las Tres Puertas, posee la más antigua fachada esculpida y decorada del arte islámico que nos haya llegado, y constituye un inventario del repertorio decorativo de Kairuán en época aglabí. La utilización de la piedra blanda esculpida confiere un aura majestuosa al aspecto general del edificio. La fachada es una composición axial simétrica con tres puertas y la más grande es la situada en el centro. Encuadrada en paneles con motivos florales y geométricos, compuestos por hojas de tres a cinco lóbulos, abiertas o replegadas, está coronada por una inscripción cúfica en la que se atribuye la fundación de esta mezquita a Mohamed ibn Jayrun el-Ma‘afiri el-Andalusí en el año 252/866.  
La mezquita no es muy grande y está compuesta por tres naves paralelas al muro de la *qibla*. Cada una de las dos columnas que soportan el techo está constituida por arcos de medio punto. En el ángulo noreste se sitúa un alminar añadido en época hafsí, como lo prueba la última línea de la inscripción escrita en cúfico florido muy cuidado y que testimonia la renovación de la totalidad del oratorio en 843/1440. De base rectangular, siguiendo el ejemplo de los alminares de Kairuán, aparece adornado por vanos geminados, enmarcados por paneles de azulejos que testimonian algunas influencias andalusíes.

fr.name: Mosquée Ibn Khayroun ou des Trois Portes
description: Bien que fermé à la visite, ce monument est recommandé car son principal intérêt réside dans sa façade. En effet, la mosquée Ibn Khayroun ou des Trois Portes possède la plus ancienne façade sculptée et décorée de l’art islamique qui nous soit parvenue et constitue un inventaire du répertoire décoratif kairouanais à l’époque aghlabide. L’utilisation de la pierre tendre sculptée a conféré à l’aspect général une aura de majesté. La façade est de composition axiale symétrique avec trois portes dont la plus grande est placée au milieu. Encadrée de panneaux à motifs floraux et géométriques, composés de feuillets à cinq ou trois lobes, ouverts ou repliés, elle est surmontée d’une écriture coufique attribuant la fondation à Mohamed Ibn Khayroun (252/866). La mosquée est d’une superficie modeste. Elle est composée de trois nefs parallèles au mur de la *qibla*. Chacune des deux colonnes, supportant le plafond, est surmontée d’arcs en plein cintre outrepassé. A l’angle nord-est se dresse un minaret qui fut ajouté à l’époque hafside comme le prouve la dernière ligne de l’inscription écrite en caractères coufiques et qui témoigne de la rénovation de tout l’oratoire en 843/1440. De base rectangulaire, à l’exemple des minarets kairouanais, il est orné de baies jumelées, encadrées de carreaux de faïence indiquant des influences andalouses certaines.

it.name: Moschea Ibn Khayrûn o delle Tre Porte

en.name: Buinaniya Madrasa
description:
Named after its founder Abu Inan, the Buinaniya Madrasa, built in 751/1351 and completed in 757/1356, comprises in fact of a group of buildings which include: a mosque, whose *minbar* is today displayed in the Batha museum in Fez; two classrooms facing each other; a large ablutions hall, *dar al-wudu’*, as well as an annexed building, known as the House of Clocks, which stands in front of the *madrasa*’s main gate. In line with other religious monuments of Fez, the Buinaniya Madrasa was endowed with a number of important *habus* gifts whose revenues were intended for the payment of professors and administrators, for the feeding of *tolba*s and for the maintenance of the building’s upkeep and preservation. The most immense *madrasa* built by the Merinids, it is described by Ibn Battuta – who called it the Madrasa *al-Kabira*, the Great Madrasa – as the most beautiful creation of the Sultan Abu Inan: “*Amongst the most beautiful actions of our master Abu Inan, may God help him, we cite the following: the construction of a large college on the site known as ‘castle’, very close to the citadel of Fez, it has no equal in the entire world embodying as it does grandeur, beauty and splendour*.”  
Whilst the whole world is agreed in his recognition of the *madrasa* as one of the most beautiful realisations of the Merinid Dynasty, numerous legends abound as to the reason of its foundation. Alfred Bel reports that “*Abu Inan, having often sinned in his conduct towards his father, had much to be forgiven for. He gathered the scholars of the age and asked them how he could atone for his mistakes and earn Allah’s forgiveness. They counselled him to choose a site situated high up in the town, which was thus used as a rubbish tip, on which to build a house dedicated to prayer and religious sciences. He therefore did this, and the conscience of Abu Inan was purified in the same way as the chosen site was by the foundation of this establishment*”.  
A spectacular architectural creation, the Buinaniya was meant to eclipse all other *madrasa*s. This is what was said to the sultan when he was presented with the list of expenses which he then hastened to throw into the *wadi* after having come to realise the considerable sums spent: “*What is beautiful is not costly, however large the sum*”.  
The *madrasa* underwent several restorations, in particular during the 11th/17th century after the earthquake which affected the town. Under the reign of the ‘Alawite Sultan Mulay Sliman (1206/1792–1237/1822), entire walls were rebuilt. In the 20th century, the restorations concentrated mostly on the plaster, wood and *zellij* decorations.  
On the north side of the *madrasa*, two adjacent doors open out onto the street, *rue Tal‘a Lekbira*; on the south side also, a third door opens onto *rue Tal‘a Sghira*. All three doors offer access to a hallway which leads to a patio, entirely paved in marble and containing at its centre a basin, which today one can only see the remains of, which then leads to a study room.  
The Lamtiyyin *wadi*, a branch of the river of Fez, crosses the south side of the patio, separating it from the mosque. Two small bridges, thrown across the *wadi* here and there, allow one to reach and enter the mosque. The layout of this latter is based on a rectangular design. Its north face opens widely onto the patio through five large bays. The mosque is divided into two rows of benches which run parallel to the south wall. The archway which separates them is composed of five arches resting on six columns of yellowing white marble. The *mihrab*, recessed into the centre of the south wall, is elaborately decorated. The minaret, square in shape, rises up from the north-west corner.  
Exit the medina *via Bab Bujlud*, *near the Batha Museum*.

es.name: Medersa Buinaniya
description:
La *medersa* Buinaniya (llamada así por su fundador, Abu Inan), comenzada a construir en 751/1351 y finalizada en 757/1356, es en realidad un conjunto arquitectónico que comprende: una mezquita, cuyo *mimbar* está hoy expuesto en el Museo Batha; dos salas de clase, dispuestas una frente a otra; una gran sala de abluciones, o *dar al-wudu*, y un edificio anejo, conocido como la Casa de los Relojes, situado frente a la puerta principal. Al igual que otros monumentos religiosos de Fez, la *medersa* Buinaniya fue dotada con un número importante de hábices por los que percibía unos ingresos que se destinaban a pagar a los profesores y empleados de la administración, a satisfacer las necesidades alimenticias de los *tolba*, y a mantener y conservar el edificio.  
Esta *medersa*, la más grande de las construidas por los meriníes, es considerada por Ibn Battuta —que la llama *medersa al-Kebira*, es decir, la Gran Medersa— como la más bella realización del sultán Abu Inan: “Entre las más hermosas realizaciones de nuestro señor Abu Inan, al que Dios asista, citaremos las siguientes: la construcción del gran colegio en las cercanías conocido como el castillo, muy cerca de la ciudadela de Fez, que no tiene parangón en todo el mundo habitado, por su grandeza, belleza y esplendor”.  
Aunque todo el mundo está de acuerdo en reconocer que la Buinaniya es una de las más bellas realizaciones de la dinastía meriní, circulan sin embargo numerosas leyendas acerca de las razones de su fundación. Alfred Bel nos cuenta que “Abu Inan, habiendo pecado mucho en su conducta para con su padre, tenía también mucho de que hacerse perdonar. Reunió a los sabios de su época y les preguntó qué podía hacer para lavar sus faltas y alcanzar el perdón de Alá. Le aconsejaron que eligiera un emplazamiento situado en la ciudad alta, que se dedicaba a depósito de basuras, para construir una casa consagrada a la oración y a la ciencia religiosa. Así lo hizo y su conciencia fue purificada, como lo fue también por la fundación de este establecimiento el lugar elegido”.  
La Buinaniya debía eclipsar a todas las demás *medersa*s por su espectacularidad arquitectónica; esto fue lo que le hizo decir al sultán, cuando le presentaron el registro de las considerables sumas invertidas: “Lo bello no es caro, por elevada que sea la suma”.  
La *medersa* ha experimentado numerosas restauraciones: en concreto, en el siglo XI/XVII, tras el terremoto que asoló la ciudad; bajo el reinado del sultán alauí Mulay Sliman (1206/1792-1237/1822) se rehicieron lienzos enteros; y, ya en el siglo XX, las restauraciones afectaron esencialmente a la ornamentación en estuco, madera y *zelish*.  
En su lado norte se abren dos puertas contiguas a la calle Tal‘a Lakbira; en el lado sur hay una tercera, que da a la calle Tal‘a Sghira. Todas dan acceso a un vestíbulo por el que se entra al patio —pavimentado de mármol y con una pila en el centro, de la que solo quedan vestigios—, que a su vez da a una sala de estudios.  
El *wad* Lamtiyyin, un ramal del *wad* Fez, atraviesa el lado sur del patio y lo separa de la mezquita; dos pequeños puentes que lo cruzan permiten entrar en ella. De planta rectangular, su lado norte se abre al patio por cinco grandes vanos; está dividida en dos naves paralelas al muro sur. La arcada que las separa está formada por cinco arcos que se apoyan en seis columnas de mármol blanco amarillento. El *mihrab*, excavado en mitad del muro sur, está ricamente decorado. El alminar, de forma cuadrada, se alza en el ángulo noroeste.  
Salir de la *medina* por *Bab Bushlud*.

fr.name: Médersa Bouinaniya
description:
Du nom de son fondateur Abou Inan, la médersa Bouinaniya, construite en 751/ 1351 et achevée en 757/1356, est en réalité un ensemble de constructions comprenant: une mosquée dont le *minbar* est aujourd’hui exposé au musée Batha à Fès; deux salles de cours disposées face à face; une grande salle d’ablutions, *dar al-woudou’*, ainsi qu’un édifice annexe, dit la Maison des horloges, faisant face à la porte principale de la médersa. À l’instar des autres monuments religieux de Fès, la médersa Bouinaniya fut dotée d’un nombre important de biens *habous* dont les revenus étaient destinés à payer les professeurs et les agents de l’administration, à satisfaire les besoins alimentaires des *tolba* et à maintenir l’entretien et la préservation de l’édifice.  
Plus vaste médersa construite par les Mérinides, elle est décrite par Ibn Battouta, qui la nomme médersa *al-Kabira*, la Grande Médersa, comme la plus belle réalisation du sultan Abou Inan: “*Parmi les plus belles actions de notre maître Abou Inan, que Dieu l’assiste, nous citerons les suivantes: la construction du grand collège à l’endroit appelé château, tout près de la citadelle de Fès, il n’a pas son pareil dans tout le monde habité par la grandeur, la beauté et la splendeur*”.  
Si tout le monde s’est accordé à la reconnaître comme l’une des plus belles réalisations de la dynastie mérinide, de nombreuses légendes circulent sur la raison de sa fondation. Alfred Bel rapporte que “*Abou Inan, ayant beaucoup péché, dans sa conduite à l’égard de son père, avait beaucoup à se faire pardonner. Il réunit les savants de l’époque et leur demanda comment il pourrait parvenir à laver ses fautes et à mériter d’Allah son pardon. Ils lui conseillèrent de choisir, pour y construire une maison consacrée à la prière et à la science religieuse, un emplacement situé dans la haute ville et qui servait alors de dépôt d’ordures. Il en fut ainsi fait et la conscience d’Abu Inan fut purifiée comme l’avait été par la fondation de cet établissement l’endroit choisi*”.  
Création architecturale spectaculaire, la Bouinaniya devait éclipser toutes les autres médersas; ce qui fit dire au sultan lorsqu’on lui présenta le registre des dépenses qu’il s’empressa de jeter pardessus l’oued après avoir pris connaissance des sommes considérables dépensées: “*Ce qui est beau n’est cher, tant grande en soit la somme*”.  
La médersa a connu de nombreuses restaurations, en particulier au XIe/XVIIe siècle après le tremblement de terre qu’a connu la ville. Sous le règne du sultan alaouite Moulay Slimane (1206/1792- 1237/1822), des pans entiers ont été refaits. Au XXe siècle, les restaurations portèrent essentiellement sur les décors de plâtre, de bois et de *zellige*.  
Du côté nord de la médersa, deux portes contiguës s’ouvrent sur la rue *Tal‘a Lekbira*; côté sud s’ouvre aussi une troisième porte, sur la rue *Tal‘a Sghira*. Toutes donnent accès à un vestibule qui permet d’accéder au niveau du patio, entièrement pavé de marbre et renfermant en son centre une vasque dont on ne trouve aujourd’hui que les vestiges, qui s’ouvre sur une salle d’études.  
L’oued Lamtiyyin, l’un des bras de l’oued Fès, traverse le côté sud du patio et le sépare de la mosquée. Deux petits ponts jetés de part et d’autre de l’oued permettent de pénétrer dans la mosquée. Celleci s’élève selon un plan rectangulaire. Son côté nord s’ouvre largement sur le patio par cinq grandes baies. La mosquée est divisée en deux travées parallèles au mur sud. L’arcade qui les sépare est composée de cinq arcs reposant sur six colonnes en marbre blanc jaunâtre. Le *mihrab*, percé au milieu du mur sud, est richement décoré. Le minaret, de forme carrée, s’élève à l’angle nord-ouest.

ar.name: صحن
description: الأنواع القليلة من القرن السابع عشر لأوعية الخزف الإيرانية والمطلية بطراز نفيس حر والمغطاة بشقوق كانت تعرف تقليديا بخزف الكوباشي (Kubachi). وهذا الاسم التقليدي أتى من قرية داغستان حيث تركز هناك في القرن التاسع عشر عدد كبير من مراكز صنع الفخار الإيراني الصفوي.لكن مراكز الإنتاج لأوعية الكوباشي المتنوعة ما تزال بحاجة لتحديد. و إن الابتكارات في طلاء المنمنمات الإيرانية في القرن السابع عشر و بشكل خاص تلك المرتبطة باللوحات الشخصية / البورتريهات كانت تنعكس في تزيين الأوعية الخزفية. والطبق الكبير المزين بطلاء متعدد الألوان يمثل الصور المفضلة  للعصر الصفوي. وإن صور الحديقة الخصبة ذات الطيور ترمز لمتعة الجنة الأرضية والسعادة الموعودة للجنة السماوية. والدرويش الوسيم الشاب الذي يتأمل في الحديقة اليانعة يعبر عن القدسية المحببة في لغة صوفية إسلامية رمزية. إن الطلاء متعدد الألوان لنباتات متنوعة تظهر بانحناءات طبيعية لأشطائها وأغصانها وكانت مستوحاة من طراز الخزف التركي في إزنيق في أواخر القرن السادس عشر. ومثل هذا النوع من الأوعية ربما أنتج في ورشات كوميشه (الآن شهريزا) وهي بلدة صغيرة قرب أصفهان.

en.name: Dish
description:
A few types of the AD 17th century Persian ceramic ware, painted in a free expressive style and covered with cracks, were traditionally known as “*Kubachi*” ceramics. This conventional name came from a village in Daghestan, where in the 19th century huge amounts of Iranian Safavid pottery were concentrated. However, the production centres of various "*Kubachi*" wares are still to be specified.  
The innovations in the 17th -century Iranian miniature painting, and particularly in the portrait genre, were reflected in décor of ceramic ware. A large plate, decorated in multicoloured painting, represents the favourite motifs of the Safavid era. Images of the lush garden with birds symbolized the joy of earthly paradise and the promised enjoyment of heavenly paradise. A handsome young dervish meditating in the blooming garden stood for the Divine Beloved in the symbolic language of Islamic mystics.  
Multicolour painting of various plants, rendered in natural bends of their sprouts and branches, was inspired by the style of Turkish Iznik ceramics of the late 16th century. Such kind of ware was probably produced in the workshops of Qumisheh (now Shahreza), a small town near Isfahan.
keywords: Ceramics; stonepaste; Iran; Safavid
materials: Stonepaste; underglaze painted with polychrome glazes
partner: The Bohdan and Varvara Khanenko National Museum of Arts

en.name: Ottoman Clothing Album
short_description: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.
holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah
partner: Ministry of Culture and Tourism (General Directorate for Cultural Heritage and Museums)

en.name: Black Eagle Pharmacy Museum
description:
The three-axis facade of the 18th-century, L-shaped, two-level, saddle-back-roofed building of the Black Eagle Pharmacy Museum is in the Classical style. The ground floor is adorned with simple toothing and the upper floor is embellished with surface decoration. The upper-floor windows have curved top-planes. The door frame of the former pharmacy entrance (in the middle axis of the street facade), and the red limestone frames of the windows on the ground floor, are adorned with carved garlands.  
Inside, the pharmacy service area was in the arched, divided space on the ground floor. Four pieces of oak furniture made by Bernát Baumgartner (SJ) and his workshop are still in situ, including a carved and gilded unit with shelves of different lengths and widths, a worktop, cupboards and drawers; the names of medicines are written in Latin in white letters on the white surface of the cabinet drawers, which have handles of either brass or wood. The Empire table, made under Ferenc Braun the owner after 1811, is horseshoe shaped, and holds gilded wooden statues of Hygeia and Panacea, daughters of Asclepius, the god of healing. The pharmaceutical jars on the shelves are of various periods. About 160 wooden skillets, a dozen holders for powders and liquids with the initials “I.H.S.”, a brass mortar (with the inscription: “Apothecae S. J. Alba Regalensis Anno 1752”) and a tincture-press remain from the original mid-18th-century apothecary set.

The history of the Black Eagle Pharmacy in Székesfehérvár is associated with the Jesuit order. The Society of Jesus (SJ) considered the professional healthcare of the community as an integral part of its duty and established pharmacies in several Hungarian towns. Granted the right to operate a pharmacy in Székesfehérvár in 1745, the first pharmacy was established in the refectory of the old Jesuit monastery from 1746, for which Bernát Baumgartner (SJ) and his workshop produced richly adorned wooden furniture in 1758. The furnishings were auctioned after the dissolution of the order in 1773, but did not go far, however, for Ferenc Walter purchased the furnishing for the Black Eagle Pharmacy that he opened across the street and which operated for 200 years.
artist: Wood Carver: Bernát Baumgartner (1704–after 1773); József Codelli (mid- 1700s)
history:
The Jesuit order settled in Székesfehérvár in 1688. The first pharmacy was opened in the town the same year and owned secularly up until 1745 with exclusive rights to run a pharmacy. The Jesuits then bought the rights, operating pharmacies in several Hungarian towns including Pozsony (Bratislava), Nagyszombat (Trnava), Trencsén (Trenčin), Eger, Győr and Kőszeg. Besides their devotion to providing healthcare in the local community, the order had extensive experience in pharmacy-management worldwide owing to their missionary activities in, for example, Europe and the Far East. The Jesuit Székesfehérvár pharmacy was established in the old monastery refectory in 1746, where Brother Joannes Maschner was apothecary until 1747. He was succeeded by Mathias Hyll who remained in the position from 1748 to 1774.  
The cabinetmaker, Bernát Baumgartner (SJ) and his workshop produced richly adorned wooden furniture for the Rococo-stuccoed pharmacy in the monastery refectory in 1758. In 1773, when the order was dissolved, the finely carved and gold encrusted apothecary’s unit, the table (since destroyed) and the pharmacy equipment were auctioned. The equipment did not go far, however, for Ferenc Walter purchased it for the Black Eagle Pharmacy that he opened across the street. After 1811, Ferenc Braun, the owner at that time, replaced the table with one in the Empire style. The secular pharmacy operated continuously until 1971 under several different owners. Recent restorations have revealed the original blue-green mottled surfaces of several wooden skillets with inscriptions in a Rococo cartouche frame. These, along with certain pieces of wooden furniture from the pharmacy laboratory, must have belonged to the furnishing of 1758 and are thought to be the works of József Codelli, a Jesuit convert and head of the furniture workshop between 1746 and 1747. A pharmacy museum was opened on the premises in 1973; since 1975 it has been known as the Black Eagle Pharmacy Museum.
keywords: Pharmacy, Black Eagle Pharmacy, Jesuit order, Society of Jesus (SJ), Bernát Baumgartner, József Codelli, Ferenc Walter, Joannes Maschner, Mathias Hyll, Székesfehérvár
tags: Pharmacy, Black Eagle Pharmacy, Jesuit order, Society of Jesus (SJ), Bernát Baumgartner, József Codelli, Ferenc Walter, Joannes Maschner, Mathias Hyll, Székesfehérvár

ar.name: المفتاح الكعبة
description:
ُزيّن الزخارف بالفضة هذا المفتاح البرونزي المربوط بحلقة على شكل قمر. تتجسد المهمة الفريدة لهذا المفتاح في حماية بيت الله الحرام.  
  
تحمل النقوش رسائل دينية وسياسية بما في ذلك آيات قرآنية واسم السلطان عبد العزيز، المُفوّض بحفظ هذا المفتاح في القرن 19 ميلادي.  
  
رفع النبي إبراهيم وابنه إسماعيل القواعد من البيت، من هنا بدأ تشريع حماية وتعظيم بيت الله الحرام.  
اليوم، يحتفظ بني شيبة بالمفتاح في حقيبة مصنوعة من الحرير مطرزة بخيوط الذهب والفضة، فقد عهد الرسول محمد (صل الله عليه وسلم) إلى بني شيبة بشرف حمل مفتاح الكعبة عند فتح مكة، وتُفتح الكعبة مرتين في العام بهذا المفتاح بغاية تنظيفها باستخدام ماء الورد وماء زمزم.

en.name: Kaaba Key
description:
Silver-inlaid inscriptions embellish this bronze key attached to a moon-shaped ring. Its unique profile safeguards the house of God in Islam.  
  
The inscriptions bear religious and political messages, including Qur’anic verses and the name of Sultan Abd Al-Aziz, commissioner of this key in the 19th century.  
  
Prophet Ibrahim and his son Ismail are believed to have raised the sanctuary’s foundations, carrying a sacred tradition of guardianship. Today, the Shayba family preserves the key in a bag made of silk, gold and silver. As authorized keykeepers entrusted by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), twice a year, they unlock the Kaaba for purification with rosewater and holy water.
holder: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani
keywords: Saudi Arabia; Key; Kaaba; Mecca; Bani Shayba
partner: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani Museum (FBQ Museums)

description: القطعة عبارة عن سجادة مستطيلة كبيرة ذات وبر محاك من نوع يعرف بالسجاجيد الكبيرة/الرئيسية وهي النوع المستخدم أساسا لتغطية الأرضيات ومستخدمة في الخيام التركمانية. وهي مزينة بتسعة صفوف من أربعة أشكال قبلية رئيسية (جولز) متكررة ذات 36 نموذج متكرر في المنطقة الرئيسية وسعيفات تقليدية ذات تشكيل من الأحمر ، الكريم ، الأسود والأزرق الداكن. وهذه السجادة يمكن أن تنسب للتكة وهي مجموعة فرعية من شعوب التركمان البدوية المرتحلة استنادا للشكل الخاص لرسوم الجول والذي هو أمر فريد لكل وحدة قبلية. والمنطقة الحمراء من السجادة فيها نموذج متكرر لرصائع متطاولة مفصصة مرتبطة بأربعة صفوف شاقولية. وإن الخطوط الزرقاء التي تسري عبر مراكز الرصائع تقسم المنطقة إلى حجرات مستطيلة وكل رصيعة ذات مقطع برتقالي – أحمر أو أبيض تحيط بشكل نجمة بالأحمر والأخضر أو أحمر وأزرق مع شكل أصغر لشكل نجمة بالأحمر والأبيض وإن الأشكال المزهرة ذات الطراز الخاص بالأحمر والبني تنبع من أشكال النجوم وبين الرضائع يوجد تصاميم بشكل متصالب بالأبيض ، الأزرق ، البرتقالي والأحمر. وتحتوي الحدود صفا من الرصائع المثمنة الأضلاع تتناوب بالأبيض والأحمر والأزرق أو الأخضر. ويحيط كل مثمن بوريدات أو أشكال نجوم بالأحمر والأزرق أو الأخضر. والرصائع مفصولة بعصابات ذات تصاميم هندسية متنوعة والعصابات الخارجية تسري فقط على ثلاثة جوانب ومقسمة إلى قطاعات ضيقة بالأبيض ، الأصفر ، الأحمر ، الأزرق والأخضر والقطاعات الخارجية لها نموذج شطرنجي.

en.name: *Tekke* Turkmen Main Carpet with Nine Rows of Four Major Tribal *Guls* in Repeat
description:
A large rectangular knotted pile carpet of a type known as "main carpets," the primary floor covering used in Turkmen tents. It is decorated with nine rows of four major tribal *guls* in repeat, with 36 *guls* in the main field and a traditional palette, with a range of reds, cream, black, and dark blue. This carpet can be attributed to the *Tekke* subgroup of the Turkmen nomads based on the specific form of the *gul* motifs, which are unique to each tribal unit.  
The red field of the carpet has a repeat pattern of lobed, elongated medallions arranged in four vertical rows. Blue lines, running through the centers of the medallions, divide the field into rectangular compartments. Each medallion with an orange-red or a white section encloses a star motif in red and green, or red and blue, with a smaller star-shaped form in red and white. Stylized floral forms in red and brown issue from the star motifs. Between the medallions are cross-shaped designs in white, blue, orange, and red. The border contains a row of octagonal medallions alternately in white, red, blue, or green. Each octagon encloses rosettes or star motifs in red and blue or green. The medallions are separated by bands with various geometrical designs. The guard bands, running only on three sides, are divided into narrow stripes in white, yellow, red, blue, and green. The guard stripes have a chequered pattern.
dates: Hegira Early 12th to early 13th century / AD 19th century
keywords: Tekke; Turkman; Carpet; Textile; Wool; Central; Asia; Turkmenistan; Asia; Turkmen
materials: Wool; asymmetrical knot, open right, approximately 68Vx36-37H per decimetre

en.name: Military personnel records
description:
The information sheets are part of the medical examination prior to the training of the new recruits. The newly enrolled were destined for the Protectorate which, due to the pressure of public opinion, refused the presence of Spaniards in that area.  
The records, along with a pair of photographs, gathered information on individuals’ social and professional backgrounds, as well as descriptive data and anthropometric values. Those values were used by the Medical Corps to determine the minimum size permitted to enter in the Army, but they were also important according to the existing racial theories in Spain.  
The sheets refer to these soldiers as “Moors” in a generic way, a colloquial and sometimes pejorative term of Latin etymology, which alludes to the population of the Maghreb with no regard to their origin, ethnicity or beliefs.
keywords: Photography; War

en.name: *The Immaculate Conception with the Saints Petronius and Dionysius*
description:
This altarpiece is one of the most celebrated works of the young Giovanni Antonio Burrini. It was commissioned by the noble Ratta family at the end of the seventeenth-century. Two saints are surrounding the Virgin. They are Petronius the bishop and patron of Bologna, and Dionysius the martyr and bishop of Paris who is often confused with the Areopagite. Saint Dionysius was probably painted by request of the patrons. It is believed that one of the members of the Ratta family was a diplomat sent by the pope to France to persuade Louis XIV to abolish the edit of Nantes and restart the prosecution of the Huguenots.  
The altarpiece is built on a pyramidal composition and is dedicated to the Carraccis and to Guido Reni. The delicate features and the brush strokes are reflective of Lorenzo Pasinelli and Sebastiano Ricci as both artists were working in Bologna at that time.

This celebrated altarpiece is one of the masterpieces of the young Burrini. Depicted at the feet of the Virgin, Saint Petronius, the patron of Bologna, and Saint Dionysius, the patron of France. The lively figures are reminiscent of Lorenzo Pasinelli, while the luminous colours and the quick brush strokes are an homage to the Venetian artist Sebastiano Ricci.
place: Ratta Garganelli Chapel, San Giacomo Maggiore, Bologna
keywords: Ratta family; altarpiece; religious/liturgical painting; Giovanni Antonio Burrini

it.name: *L’Immacolata con i Santi Petronio e Dionigi*
description: La pala d'altare è una delle opere più note dell'attività giovanile di Giovanni Antonio Burrini. Zanotti nel 1739 riporta che il dipinto venne commissionato dalla famiglia Ratta, mentre il Masini nel 1690, documenta che nel “1684 Antonio Burrini, della Scuola del Pittore Pasinelli, dipinse una tavola per la Cappella de' Ratta Garganelli nella Chiesa di San Giacomo maggiore con la Madonna sopra la luna e più sotto li Santi Petronio Vescovo Protettore di Bologna e Dionigi Aeropagita Vescovo di Parigi Martire, prima sua operazione veduta in pubblico”. In realtà si ritrova anche qui la tradizionale confusione tra san Dionigi martire, vescovo di Parigi  e protettore della Francia, e san Dionigi l'Aeropagita discepolo di Paolo e vescovo di Atene. Il santo rappresentato dal Burrini è *saint Denis*, vescovo e martire parigino decollato a *Montmartre*, lo strano affiancamento a san Petronio, fu probabilmente voluto dalla committenza, infatti, uno dei membri della famiglia Ratta era alto funzionario pontificio alla corte di Francia per conto di papa Innocenzo XI, con la specifica funzione di convincere Luigi XIV a revocare l'editto di Nantes e inasprire la repressione degli Ugonotti. La tavola in quest'ottica appare come l'esplicito plauso della famiglia Ratta alla politica estera papale anti-ugonotta, attraverso la specifica devozione per il santo parigino e perla causa de esso rappresentato. La saggezza compositiva del giovane Burrini si esplica attraverso la classica articolazione verticale a piramide della pala d'altare bolognese, che tanto richiama le esperienze carraccesche d'inizio secolo. La cultura cittadina è il motore dell'*ars pictorica* dell'artista, si noti l'affinità tra la pittura di Guido Reni per la cattedrale di Siviglia e il san Biagio di Forlì. Nel tratteggio e nella delicatezza delle forme, si palesa il tentativo, sulla scorta del Passinelli, di superare i suoi giovani rivali, soprattutto il Franceschini e il Dal Sole. La rappresentazione si traduce così in una vibrazione continua delle cromie modulate attraverso quella pennellata violenta che ben richiama i grandi maestri veneti, il Ricci su tutti, allora già presente a Bologna da alcuni anni.

La famosa pala d'altare è oggi collocata nella chiesa dell'Assunta a Monghidoro e rappresenta una delle più importanti opere di Giovanni Burrini. Al di sotto della Beata Vergine, che sovrasta la luna, sono rappresentati, in una composizione piramidale tipica della pittura bolognese d'inizio Seicento, i santi Petronio, patrono della città, e Dionigi, protettore di Francia. La tela venne commissionata dalla famiglia Ratta per San Giacomo Maggiore a Bologna, venne poi trasferita, in data ignota, nella chiesa di Monghidoro. La vivacità delle forme dipinte dal giovane Burrini richiama il Pasinelli, mentre la sferzante vibrazione delle cromie fa eco alla pittura veneta del coevo Sebastiano Ricci.
place: Cappella de’ Ratta Garganelli, San Giacomo Maggiore, Bologna
keywords: Famiglia Ratta; pala d'altare; pittura religiosa; Giovanni Antonio Burrini

en.name: Portrait Album – Ottoman State Officers
short_description: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.
holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah
partner: Ministry of Culture and Tourism (General Directorate for Cultural Heritage and Museums)

en.name: *Titus Flavius Josephus and Titus Livius*
description:
This representation is depicted in one of the seven lunettes of the main room. In this room the central theme is the *Ascension to the Mountain of Knowledge*. The allegories of several disciplines (Philosophy, Mathematics, Moral Philosophy, Theology, History and Law) are flanked by pairs of their significant representatives. The lunettes allude to the books held in the bookshelves below.  
In the middle, standing on a basis inscribed in capital characters: PEPLUM MINERVA / D.D.D. / A: T: P, a crowned female figure leans with her shoulder against a great fasces (around which twines a cartouche with the words VERITAS and VIVIT) and shows a book. At her feet are two busts of Roman emperors. On the right, a massive masculine figure (reminiscent of the gigantic characters in Pellegrino Tibaldi's frescoes in palazzo Poggi) turns towards the statue, holding in his hand a medal with a man's portrait. On the left Titus Flavius Josephus reads and at the same time unrolls a scroll written in Jewish characters.
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: *Flavio Giuseppe e Tito Livio*
description:
La raffigurazione si trova in una delle sette lunette della sala centrale dove sono dipinte la salita al monte della virtù e le allegorie delle varie discipline (Filosofia, Matematica, Filosofia Morale, Teologia, Storia e Legge), attraverso la raffigurazione di una coppia di sapienti, e con la funzione di indicare le varie discipline cui afferivano i volumi posti nelle scaffalature sottostanti.  
Al centro, (su un piedistallo recante la scritta a lettere capitali: PEPLUM MINERVA / D.D.D. / A:T:P ) una figura femminile eretta, incoronata, regge con la spalla destra un grande fascio (cui si avvolge un filatterio con le parole VERITAS e VIVIT) e scopre un volume. Ai suoi piedi busti frammentari di imperatori romani. Alla sua sinistra una figura maschile possente (memore ancora del gigantismo degli affreschi manieristi di pellegrino Tibaldi in Palazzo Poggi) si rivolge verso di lei reggendo nella mano un medaglione con un profilo maschile. Sulla destra è posto Giuseppe Ebreo in atto di leggere, svolge con la mano sinistra un ampio cartiglio con una scritta a caratteri ebraici.
place: Biblioteca, S. Michele in Bosco, Bologna (sala 2)

en.name: *Shadda*
description: The cells are completely separated from the central area by a yellow stripe. Each cell is decorated with diamond shape elements. The borders on both sides are also made up of small diamond shaped elements.
dates: Date unknown, purchased by the Museum in the 19th century
keywords: Carpet; Azerbaijan; *Shadda*
materials: Wool warp and weft; plain weave

en.name: *Infantry-attack during the occupation-campaign in Bosnia-Herzegovina 1878*
short_description: With an energetic stroke of the brush, Rudolph Konopa shows us an episode from the occupation campaign of the Austro-Hungarian Army in the Ottoman provinces of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1878. Konopa studied at the Academy of Fine Arts in Vienna and was a co-founder of the *Hagenbund* in 1900. Konopa received many awards, including the gold medal of the Vienna *Künstlerhaus*. Later during World War I, he became member of the so called *k.u.k. Kriegspressequartier* (art division of the ministry of War) and worked as a war painter on the eastern and southern fronts.
holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
keywords: Bosnia; Austrian army; Ottoman army; Ottoman Balkans; war; warfare
partner: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History

en.name: Astronomer Pierre Janssen (1824–1907) is carried in a ladder chair to the inauguration of the observatory on the Mont Blanc, at 4.807 m.

ar.name: صحيفة من كتاب الحيل الهندسية
description: صحيفة من" كتاب في معرفة الحيل الهندسية" لإسماعيل ابن الرزاز الجزري، يشرح بالرسم تقنية تعتمد على الماء لتشغيل ناي" دائم العزف". كتب النص بخط النسخ الأنيق، ووقع عليه فاروق بن عبد اللطيف.
